title: Supersession keeps last-committed, not latest-valid (Bug B; reverse-order litmus fails)
description: Surfaced by the doc-39 harness (epoch/corpus10, runId 2026-06-02T14-16-04-143Z). After nmemo-hm4.10, supersession now FIRES and collapses each exclusive group to exactly one active fact (V3 passes 5/5 in BOTH directions). But it keeps the LAST-COMMITTED fact, not the LATEST-VALID one: forward (chronological) order resolves Elena->CTO and Helix->Austin (current-state 0.67), while REVERSE chunk order resolves Elena->senior engineer and Helix->none (current-state 0.33); the litmus fails (fwd-vs-rev fact F1 0.39, vs entity F1 0.96). This is doc-05 Bug B (inverted temporal direction): createFact/findSupersedingFacts supersede by commit order, not by valid_at. nmemo-hm4.10 made supersession fire; ordering it by valid_at is this separate fix, and it is the doc-38 consistency bar (the reverse-order litmus) for parallel ingestion.

title: Test infra: isolate Qdrant tests to a separate collection (not production 'memories')
description: The contamination found during nmemo-yxj.6: store-units.test.ts (and any suite using store()/qdrant) self-gates on isQdrantAvailable() and writes to the HARDCODED production 'memories' collection (qdrant.ts COLLECTIONS.MEMORIES='memories'), with no cleanup. This corrupts production/benchmark data when tests run against a shared Qdrant. Root-cause fix: make the collection name env-configurable so the test process uses an isolated 'memories_test' collection; production default unchanged. Unblocks all remaining yxj/0wq beads to be tested without touching production memories.
design: qdrant.ts: COLLECTIONS.MEMORIES = process.env.QDRANT_COLLECTION ?? 'memories' (and any other hardcoded 'memories' refs route through the same accessor). src/test/setup.ts: set process.env.QDRANT_COLLECTION='memories_test' (alongside the existing DATABASE_URL=cognitive_test default at setup.ts:14). global-setup / test teardown may (re)create + clear 'memories_test'. Production runtime (no env var) keeps using 'memories' verbatim — zero behavioural change to the platform/benchmark.
acceptance_criteria: qdrant collection name is env-driven; production default is 'memories' (unchanged). Under vitest, all Qdrant ops target 'memories_test'. Running the Qdrant-touching suites (e.g. store-units) writes ONLY to 'memories_test' — production 'memories' is never touched by tests. Verified without reading the production 'memories' collection (confirm via the env wiring + that 'memories_test' receives the points).
notes: Implemented in 823ce2c. qdrant.ts COLLECTIONS.MEMORIES is now a LAZY getter (process.env.QDRANT_COLLECTION ?? 'memories', read at access time, not import-bound). setup.ts defaults QDRANT_COLLECTION='memories_test'; global-setup creates/resets memories_test (768-dim,Cosine) with a hard never-'memories' guard. New qdrant-collection-isolation.test.ts proves: under vitest -> 'memories_test', env unset -> 'memories' (lazy fallback), custom env honoured. Ran isolation+store-units+qdrant-wrapper = 25 passed, 0 type errors; store-units alone left 14 points in memories_test (parent+units). Production 'memories' was never read/written/queried/dropped at any point. Unblocks yxj/0wq bead tests without touching prod memories.
close_reason: Qdrant collection name is env-driven via lazy getter; tests isolated to memories_test, production 'memories' untouched; 25 tests pass

title: Verify + adopt nomic-embed task prefixes (search_query/search_document) if they help
description: /embed sends raw prompt to nomic-embed-text with NO task prefix (embed.py:58 single, :95 batch); platform ml.embed (ml-client.ts:158) and entity generateEmbedding all route through it. nomic-embed-text is trained with task prefixes - search_query: for queries, search_document: for stored passages - so omitting them degrades retrieval similarity (asymmetric use is worst). The 0.809/0.472 cosine measurements were taken raw. Likely a cheap, broad retrieval win - but Ollama MIGHT inject prefixes via its modelfile template, so verify empirically before committing. Discovered in the 2026-06-02 planning session (sibling to nmemo-yxj).
design:
VERIFY-THEN-ADOPT.
(1) VERIFY via the yxj.1 harness: compare no-prefix vs search_query:/search_document: on the needle set; adopt ONLY if it measurably helps.
(2) IF adopting: apply prefixes at the embed boundary - search_query: for query-time embeds, search_document: for stored passage embeds (store() units + window). Needs an intent signal on /embed (a task param, or distinct query/document paths).
(3) ALSO covers pgvector entity embeddings (generateEmbedding): entity-to-entity similarity is SYMMETRIC so CONSISTENCY matters most - pick one document prefix, apply uniformly; centroids derive from the same vectors.
NO BACKFILL CONCERN: the project starts from a CLEAN SLATE (decision 2026-06-02: no backfill, no legacy vectors), so adoption is just setting the policy and ingesting fresh - no migration, no mixed-prefix transition.
SHARED-INFRA: applies to fresh embeds into the (isolated) memories collection. FILES: ml-services/app/embed.py, platform/src/services/ml-client.ts, store()/generateEmbedding callers.
acceptance_criteria: A measured no-prefix vs prefix comparison on the needle set is recorded. IF prefixes help: query embeds use search_query:, stored/passage + entity embeds use a consistent document prefix, applied uniformly (clean slate - no backfill). IF Ollama already injects prefixes (no measured difference): close with that finding recorded.
notes:
[2026-06-02] VERIFY (from yxj.1 recorded prefix side-test, no new infra run): nomic task prefixes HELP and should be ADOPTED. At unit_size=256/overlap=64 over the 8-needle LongMemEval corpus, prepending search_query:/search_document: lifted recall@1 0.38 -> 0.75 (a large precision-at-top win) with mean needle score essentially flat (0.731 -> 0.725) and degree score flat (0.636 -> 0.631). Net: prefixes sharpen top-1 ranking at no cost to the score band. Evidence: benchmarks/results/yxj1_embedding_unit_sweep.{md,json} (prefix_side_test). REMAINING (infra-gated, deferred until benchmark done): the ADOPT step = add the task prefixes to the platform embedding path (search_document: at store/unit embed time, search_query: at query embed time in ml-services/app/embed.py + callers), then restart ml-services + retest. Do NOT restart ml-services while the benchmark runs.
[2026-06-02] ADOPTED platform-side (no ml-services change/restart). Helpers ml.embedDocument (search_document:) + ml.embedQuery (search_query:) on the ml client + exported SEARCH_DOCUMENT_PREFIX/SEARCH_QUERY_PREFIX constants. Wired: store() window+unit embeds (pipeline.ts) -> embedDocument; search_memories tool (causal-agent.ts) -> embedQuery. Scope = memories retrieval ONLY; entity-name + fact + search_similar_entities embeds stay on ml.embed() raw (symmetric similarity). Coordinated store+query pair; clean-slate, no backfill. Tests: src/test/services/embed-task-prefix.test.ts (8) + ml-client.test.ts + retrieval-read-path.test.ts = 30 passed, 0 type errors, isolated (ml.embed spy, no real Ollama; Qdrant mocked/memories_test). Commit 2ab1ed9. DESIGN bullet(3) entity-prefix consistency left as deferred follow-up (out of memories scope).
close_reason: Adopted nomic search_query/search_document prefixes platform-side on the memories store+query paths; 30 tests pass isolated; no ml-services change

title: Design spec: graph-anchored fallback retrieval
description: Produce the design before any code (project norm: design-before-code for P1+). Decide traversal policy, seed handling, re-rank, failure trigger, and the deferred fact->unit persistence choice.
design: Cover: (1) traversal policy - which neighbours, hop depth, ranking of expansion candidates; (2) anchor-seed handling + explicit no-anchor behaviour (booster not guarantee); (3) re-rank model over fetched unit evidence; (4) the query-FAILURE trigger - what counts as failure and when to invoke the fallback (cost control); (5) RESOLVE the deferred fact->unit persistence choice from yxj.6 (persist-at-write vs compute-on-demand). Ground in docs/benchmarks + existing retrieval/traversal code (cross-cluster-generator topology, qdrant search, /api/reason/query).
acceptance_criteria: A written, reviewed design spec covering traversal, seed/no-seed, re-rank, failure trigger, and the persistence decision - before implementation starts.
notes: Design doc: docs/architecture/truth-graph/38-graph-anchored-fallback-retrieval.md (commit c160bb0). Sections: 1 Purpose; 2 Where it sits in retrieval path (anchored to GRAPH_TOOLS/causal-agent.ts, qdrant.ts, graph.ts, /api/reason/query); 3 Traversal policy (fact-edge neighbour walk, depth<=2, ranked+capped expansion candidates); 4 Anchor seeding + explicit no-anchor empty-return; 5 Unit-grained cosine re-rank + composite score; 6 Query-failure trigger (retrieval-confidence floor) + cost guards + boundary-check & recall_via_graph tool; 7 RESOLVED fact->unit persistence = fact_units link table, persist-at-write (yxj.6 target); 8 Interfaces for 0wq.2/.3/.4; 9 Out of scope; 10 Open questions; 11 References. title: Graph-anchored fallback retrieval (query-failure recall booster)
description: When a flat unit-vector query fails to surface the answer, expand from anchored nodes: hit some unit -> its window -> entities -> neighbour nodes -> fetch the EVIDENCE UNITS behind neighbour facts -> re-rank against the query. Recovers recall a flat vector search misses (e.g. LongMemEval multi-session reasoning). Discovered in the 2026-06-02 planning session as a high-value follow-on to the embedding-granularity epic (nmemo-yxj).
design:
CONVERGED INTENT 2026-06-02 (detailed design to be done in its own session - see child .1).
WHY UNIT-GRAINED: the expansion MUST fetch neighbour evidence at UNIT grain, not window grain - pulling a neighbour whole window re-introduces the dilution nmemo-yxj removed. So this epic DEPENDS on fact->unit links (nmemo-yxj.6).
ANCHOR DEPENDENCY (honest limit): the fallback needs the query to anchor to SOME node first to seed expansion; if nothing anchors, there is nothing to expand. It is a recall BOOSTER, not a guaranteed recovery.
DO NOT move canonical provenance: window stays facts.source_memory_id; this epic READS the additive unit links from yxj.6.
SCOPE BOUNDARY: a NEW retrieval capability (traversal + neighbour-evidence fetch + re-rank + failure trigger), deliberately kept OUT of nmemo-yxj.3 so yxj keeps its crisp acceptance (needle retrievable, same Haiku count).
acceptance_criteria: A query that fails flat unit retrieval but whose answer is reachable via a neighbour node is recovered by the fallback (demonstrated on >=1 LongMemEval multi-session question). The fallback fetches neighbour evidence at UNIT grain (no whole-window re-dilution). Canonical window provenance unchanged.

title: Fact->unit evidentiary links (offset-mapped, additive)
description: Link each fact to the specific embedding unit(s) that evidence it, by offset overlap, WITHOUT moving canonical provenance off the window. Enabler for graph-anchored fallback retrieval (separate follow-on epic): that fallback must stay unit-grained or it re-dilutes, and fine fact->unit links are what keep it sharp.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Finding 2). ADDITIVE ONLY - facts.source_memory_id STAYS the window (canonical, load-bearing for centroids/extract; do NOT move it). The unit link is a SECOND, finer evidentiary grain.
MECHANISM (no agent change): the agent extracts over the whole window and cannot attribute facts to units. Map POST-HOC by offset overlap: locate the fact source_text span within the window content, link to the unit(s) whose char_start/char_end cover it; fall back to window-only when the quote is not verbatim or repeats. Units have offsets (yxj.2), facts have source_text (schema.ts:138).
WRINKLE: units live in QDRANT not Postgres, so the link is a stored reference to a Qdrant point id, NOT a FK. The join is fact -> unit-ids -> Qdrant fetch (exactly what the fallback consumes).
PERSISTENCE CHOICE DEFERRED (investigate later): persist-at-write (fact_units link table or unit_ids[] on facts; robust, DB-gated by shared infra) vs compute-on-demand at query time (code-only, per-query cost). Decide when building the fallback epic.
acceptance_criteria: Given a stored window with units, each fact maps to the unit(s) covering its source_text span (or window-fallback when not verbatim). facts.source_memory_id remains the window. The mapping is reproducible and consumable by the fallback retrieval epic.
notes:
HALTED 2026-06-02 (isolation gate). Feasibility check FAILED for fully-isolated implementation. Unit point ids are minted with randomUUID() in store() (platform/src/pipeline.ts:329) and persisted ONLY in the Qdrant 'memories' collection (point payload {point_type:'unit', parent_window_id, char_start/end} on a random-uuid id). They are NOT deterministic (no windowId+index scheme) and not reconstructible from the parent-window text alone. Writing fact_units links in extract() per design 38 sect.7 requires the real unit_point_id for each overlapping unit, which can only be learned by QUERYING the memories collection (filter point_type=unit, parent_window_id=memoryId). That violates the active benchmark's hard-isolation constraint (no read/write on the shared memories collection). Per the bead's own HALT rule, this bead must WAIT for the benchmark to finish (or an isolated Qdrant). No code/migration/test written; no shared cognitive DB or memories collection touched. UNBLOCK OPTIONS when infra free: (a) wait for benchmark + implement extract()-side query of unit ids, OR (b) co-design with yxj.2 to make unit ids deterministic (e.g. uuidv5(memoryId, unitIndex)) so extract() can recompute them with zero memories reads -- this would make the link write fully isolated and also simplifies the §7 'same store()/extract()' write-site. Recommend (b): align with the design's persist-at-write intent and removes the shared-infra dependency entirely.
[2026-06-02] HALT ISOLATION: deferred until benchmark done / isolated infra. yxj.2 mints unit point ids via randomUUID() (pipeline.ts:329), persisted only in Qdrant memories payload — not reconstructible in extract() from window text+splitIntoUnits, so writing fact_units links needs a memories-collection read (forbidden during the running benchmark). No code/migration written; no shared infra touched; bead left OPEN. UNBLOCK: small yxj.2 follow-up to make unit ids deterministic (uuidv5(memoryId, unitIndex)) -> extract() recomputes them with zero memories reads -> yxj.6 becomes fully DB-isolated. Otherwise waits for benchmark/isolated Qdrant.
DONE 2026-06-02 (commit cea1baf). Implemented fully DB-isolated per the HALT note's option (b): made yxj.2 unit point ids DETERMINISTIC (uuidv5(memoryId,unitIndex), hand-rolled RFC-4122 v5 over crypto, no new dep) at the minting site (pipeline.ts store()). extract() now recomputes those ids from window text + splitIntoUnits and writes fact_units rows via a pure offset-overlap map (mapFactToUnits: half-open intervals; window_fallback row keyed on the window id for empty/non-verbatim/repeated spans). Added mig 038_fact_units.sql (+ schema.ts factUnits): additive public.fact_units, fact_id FK->facts ON DELETE CASCADE, unit_point_id TEXT (not an FK; units live in Qdrant), char_start/end, match_kind. Satellite invariant HELD: facts.source_memory_id never updated (asserted in tests); link write is INSERT-only into the new table, best-effort, idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Same Haiku call count; prose/Frankenstein path unaffected. Tests: src/test/integration/fact-units.test.ts 16/16 PASS; store-units.test.ts 11/11 PASS (deterministic ids compatible with yxj.2 assertions). ISOLATION: cognitive_test DB + synthetic data ONLY — NO memories collection, NO cognitive DB, NO Ollama/embeddings touched by the new test or new code path.

title: Guard: exclude stream-speaker entities from generic auto-merge
description: Prevent the generic reconciliation/merge loop from FALSELY converging distinct anonymous users across streams. The merge candidate pipeline is topology + predicate-signature driven (cross-cluster-generator.ts:256-272 loads from entity_topology WHERE component_id IS NOT NULL AND k_core >= threshold; merge-scorer scores role/predicate-signature similarity). Every user has the same fact shape (graduated_with, works_at, lives_in, preferences), so two distinct users from two streams have near-identical predicate signatures and would be proposed as a merge candidate on structural similarity alone, with zero evidence they are the same person. A null embedding does NOT gate this path. This breaks the multi-user-from-the-start goal.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Decision 6, Finding 1).

FIX (correctness, minimal): exclude entities that have a stream_participants row from the generic auto-merge CANDIDATE SET. One NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.stream_participants sp WHERE sp.entity_id = <entity>) clause, applied where the candidate set is assembled so it covers BOTH the topology path (cross-cluster-generator.ts loadCandidateEntities, ~256-272) AND the drift-driven path (loadActionableDriftEvents, ~288-303) - apply at the combined candidate-set level so neither path can introduce a speaker.

SEMANTICS: stream-speaker entities are managed by the speaker subsystem and are NEVER auto-merged by the generic topology/role loop. The stream_participants table (3f9.1) IS the marker - no new column, no flag, no migration beyond 3f9.1.

INTENTIONALLY BLUNT: this also blocks a legitimately-named speaker (e.g. Bruce) from merging with a third-person Bruce entity via the generic loop. That cross-stream convergence is DEFERRED to the future speaker-agent follow-on (with the promotion trigger, embedding recompute, and the mergeEntities -> stream_participants.entity_id re-point). The re-point is only exercised once speaker merges happen, which are deferred, so no orphan risk in the meantime.

DOES NOT cover within-stream accretion (already works: a name revealed mid-stream enriches the same stream-stable entity via alias + summary, no merge needed).

FILES: platform/src/services/cross-cluster-generator.ts (candidate-set assembly). No schema change here.
acceptance_criteria: Two anonymous user entities in DIFFERENT streams, each with similar predicate signatures (e.g. both have graduated_with + works_at + lives_in facts), are NEVER proposed as a merge candidate by generateCrossClusterCandidates (neither via the topology path nor the drift path). A normal pair of non-speaker entities is still proposed as before (the guard does not over-exclude). Within-stream user identity enrichment is unaffected.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-06-02. Added NOT EXISTS(public.stream_participants) to BOTH candidate-set loaders in cross-cluster-generator.ts: loadCandidateEntities (topology path, ~256-272) and loadActionableDriftEvents (drift path, ~288-303). No schema change; reuses 3f9.1 table + idx_stream_participants_entity. 4 new guard tests in cross-cluster-generator.test.ts: (1) two anon speakers in diff streams w/ identical structural signals -> 0 component pairs, 0 candidates, pair absent; (2) drifted speaker -> 0 drift-driven candidates, never proposed; (3) no over-exclusion -> component {normal,speaker} still yields normal<->normal pair, speaker excluded; (4) baseline w/ no stream_participants rows unchanged. 29/29 tests pass, no type errors, no regressions. Commit 5306880.
close_reason: Stream-speaker entities excluded from generic auto-merge candidate set via NOT EXISTS(stream_participants) on both loaders; 4 guard tests pass, no regressions.

title: Tune defaults from benchmark; document; retest q[0]
description: Run the d1 benchmark against the real splitter, pick unit/overlap and window-size defaults (window size = separate extraction-quality axis), record the recommendation on the epic, and confirm the degree needle lands in the 0.7-plus band end-to-end. Needs the Finding 1 epic landed for the self-fact to exist.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Finding 2). Tune defaults from yxj.1, document, retest q[0] end-to-end. DEPENDS on Finding 1 (nmemo-3f9) landed so the self-fact exists to retrieve.

CLEAN SLATE (decision 2026-06-02): NO backfill. On rollout the graph + memories collection start empty and are ingested fresh; the read path is units-only (no legacy/hybrid path). Any wipe of the shared memories collection is destructive -> isolated infra only.

DEFAULTS: from yxj.1, pick EMBED_UNIT_CHARS + overlap (the size/overlap knee in the 0.7+ band). Record numbers + recommendation on this epic.

WINDOW-SIZE = SEPARATE EXTRACTION-QUALITY AXIS (decoupled from the nomic limit now that units handle embedding). Measure EXTRACTION COMPLETENESS, not retrieval recall: sweep agent window size (e.g. {3000,6000,12000} chars) with unit size FIXED; for each, run the REAL graph agent over a fixed corpus and measure the fraction of a small hand-built GOLD fact set it extracts (reuse needle facts + a handful of obvious per-session facts). Plot completeness AND Haiku-call-count cost; pick the window maximizing completeness at acceptable cost. title: Retrieval read path: search units, group by parent, return parent
description: Update searchMemories, the /api/reason/query path, and the search_memories plus get_memory_text agent tools to search fine units, dedup hits to parent windows, and return parent content for context.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Finding 2, Decision 1: read path).

PROBLEM: with N unit points per window, naive search returns duplicate units from the same parent and unit-sized snippets instead of the window.

READ PATH: search fine units, dedup to parent, return parent content.
- searchMemories (qdrant.ts:92): add a filter point_type=unit so search ranks UNITS (the undiluted vectors); optional stream_id filter for metadata-scoped retrieval (the B-at-query path).
- Dedup hits by parent_window_id; keep top-k meaningful AFTER dedup (k DISTINCT parents).
- Return the PARENT window content via getMemory(parent) for context.
- Update callers: /api/reason/query (index.ts:1001) and the agent tools search_memories + get_memory_text (causal-agent.ts).

ORTHOGONAL TO pgvector: Qdrant = source-text search (now unit-grained -> dedup to window). pgvector entity/fact similarity (entities.embedding) is a SEPARATE store, untouched, no double-counting. The only bridge (getMemoryVectors for centroids) is preserved by yxj.2 keeping the parent vector.

FILES: qdrant.ts (searchMemories), index.ts, causal-agent.ts.
acceptance_criteria: A query whose needle lives in one unit returns the parent window (degree needle in the 0.7+ band). Duplicate unit hits from the same parent collapse to one result; top-k is k DISTINCT parents. Agent tools see parent content. The pgvector entity/fact path is unaffected.
notes: DONE 2026-06-02 (commit fcca165). Added searchMemoriesByUnit() in qdrant.ts: searches point_type=unit (the undiluted vectors, +optional stream_id scope), over-fetches limit*5, groups hits by parent_window_id keeping MAX unit score per parent (NOT sum - sum would re-introduce length dilution), returns top-k DISTINCT parents with parent WINDOW content via retrieve. Window points excluded from search so window+units never both surface. Conditional pre-yxj.2 fallback: only fires on zero unit hits, searches point_type=window, marks matchedUnits=0. Switched causal-agent search_memories tool to it; get_memory_text unchanged (deterministic uuidv5 unit ids != window ids, so agent always holds parent ids); /api/reason/query handler delegates to agent tool so no handler edit. pgvector entity/fact path untouched, same Haiku call count. Tests (new retrieval-read-path.test.ts, 6 cases) + qdrant-wrapper + store-units = 29 passed, 0 type errors, against memories_test/cognitive_test ONLY (each test clearMemories() on isolated collection); production memories/cognitive never touched. Verified each acceptance bullet: needle in one unit -> parent returned scored >0.6 (vs 0.47 dilution); many matching units of one parent collapse to 1 result w/ matchedUnits>1; top-k = k distinct parents; no unit id leaks; legacy window-only retrievable via fallback; empty corpus -> [].

title: store(): small overlapping unit splitter + multi-point Qdrant write
description: In store(), split the window into small overlapping units, embed each, and upsert N Qdrant points each carrying parent_window_id, unit text, and char offsets. Parent window content remains retrievable. Single-vector 768-dim Cosine collection unchanged (more points, not named/multi-vectors). Unit size and overlap are config knobs so the benchmark can sweep them. Heavily commented per the design note.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Finding 2, Decision 1: storage shape).

PROBLEM: store() (pipeline.ts:166) embeds the whole text as ONE vector and writes ONE Qdrant point (qdrant.ts storeMemory:54). A fact buried in a ~6000-char window averages into noise (degree sentence 0.809 alone vs 0.472 buried).

SHAPE = parent-as-existing-point + unit satellites (NOT dup-on-unit, NOT a separate record):
- PARENT point unchanged: id=memoryId, vector=whole-window embedding, payload {content=full window, point_type=window, stream_id, content_type, source, created_at, status}.
- UNIT points (NEW): one per small OVERLAPPING unit; id=new uuid; vector=unit embedding; payload {point_type=unit, parent_window_id=memoryId, unit_text, char_start, char_end, stream_id}. Units carry ONLY the unit text, NOT a copy of the full window.
- Collection stays single-vector 768-dim Cosine (more points, NOT named/multi-vectors). Heavily comment the unit/parent model.

WHY THIS SHAPE (load-bearing): memoryId is canonical for (a) extract() getMemory(memoryId).content (pipeline.ts:200), (b) facts.source_memory_id (schema.ts:137), (c) entity_meta centroids (graph-meta.ts:74 getMemoryVectors over WINDOW ids via memory_entities). Keeping the parent a real vectored point preserves ALL THREE unchanged. Dropping/relocating the window vector would silently null every entity centroid (graph-meta.ts:125 else-branch) and collapse clustering/drift/merge-scoring. DO NOT move source_memory_id to the unit.

CONFIG: EMBED_UNIT_CHARS, EMBED_UNIT_OVERLAP (config.ts), tuned by yxj.1. Same Haiku-call count: extract() still runs ONCE over the whole window (units are storage/retrieval only, never the extraction unit).

OFFSETS ARE A BRIDGE: char_start/char_end on units + mention_start/end on memory_entities + source_text on facts share one coordinate system, enabling future fact->unit linkage (yxj.6) and centroid de-dilution (future). Do NOT drop the offset fields as unused.

FILES: pipeline.ts (store), qdrant.ts (batch upsert for N points), config.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Storing a window writes 1 parent point (point_type=window, full content, whole-window vector) + N unit points (point_type=unit, parent_window_id set, unit_text + char offsets, unit vector). getMemory(memoryId) still returns the full window content. getMemoryVectors([memoryId]) still returns the window vector (centroids unaffected). Unit size + overlap configurable. Each unit embeds within nomic limits.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + verified (commit 8877a58). store() writes 1 parent window point (point_type=window, full content, whole-window vector) + N overlapping unit satellites (point_type=unit, parent_window_id, unit_text, char_start/end, unit vector) in one storeMemoryWithUnits upsert; collection stays single-vector 768-dim Cosine. Pure splitIntoUnits(text,unitChars,overlap) is exported+unit-tested. Config knobs EMBED_UNIT_CHARS=128 / EMBED_UNIT_OVERLAP=64 (from yxj.1 sweep); loadConfig rejects overlap>=chars. Satellite invariant held: source_memory_id NOT moved; units never linked in memory_entities so getMemoryVectors([memoryId]) still returns the WINDOW vector (centroids unaffected) — asserted as a negative test. Acceptance verified: parent full content via getMemory; N unit points with offsets reconstructing the parent slice; each unit embeds within nomic limits; short window -> 1 unit; empty -> 0. Side effect handled: causal-agent search_memories re-narrowed to point_type=window so unit points (no content field) don't surface blank hits — full unit read path deferred to yxj.3. Tests: 11 store-units pass; qdrant(20)/causal-agent-tools(16)/stream-speaker(2) regression-clean.
close_reason: store() writes parent window + N overlapping unit satellites via storeMemoryWithUnits; config knobs + pure splitter; satellite/centroid invariant verified; 11 new tests pass, regressions clean

title: Micro-benchmark: retrieval recall vs embedding unit size + overlap
description: Standalone measurement, no platform change. Needle set = degree sentence plus a handful of buried LongMemEval facts. Embed candidate units at varying size and overlap via ML /embed, index in a scratch Qdrant collection, measure recall@k of the needle against its question. Test small first, then tune.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Finding 2). Standalone measurement, NO platform change, THROWAWAY scratch Qdrant collection (NEVER the shared memories collection); delete after. NOT infra-gated - runnable now alongside the parallel benchmark.

SWEEP:
- unit_size (chars): {128, 256, 512, 1024}. Knee is below ~1000 (degree sentence ~80 chars scored 0.809; the 5895-char window scored 0.472).
- overlap (chars): {0, 64, 128, 256} (insurance against a fact split across a unit boundary).
- recall@k: k in {1,3,5}. Target: needle unit in the 0.7+ band AND ranked in top-k for its question.

NEEDLE SET (~8, mined from the LongMemEval_S cut, spread across answer TYPES so we do not tune to one shape): attribute (degree), temporal (a date), numeric (a quantity), preference, discrete event. Each = {question, gold answer-sentence, the long session it is buried in}.

REALISTIC DISTRACTORS (validity-critical): index the FULL units of the source sessions (ideally several sessions), NOT needles-in-isolation, so recall is measured against real corpus noise - otherwise recall is trivially 1.0 and meaningless.

PREFIX CONFOUNDER (see the nomic-prefix bead): /embed sends RAW text to nomic, NO task prefix (embed.py:58,95). HOLD the prefix policy CONSTANT across the size/overlap sweep. ADDITIONALLY run a one-off side comparison: no-prefix vs correct nomic prefixes (search_query: for the question, search_document: for units) to quantify the win - this result feeds the prefix bead.

OUTPUT: table of recall@k vs (unit_size, overlap); recommended (unit_size, overlap) recorded for yxj.2/yxj.5; the prefix side-result recorded. FILES: new script under benchmarks/.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible script reports recall@k vs (unit_size, overlap) over an ~8-needle set indexed among realistic distractor units in a throwaway Qdrant collection. Confirms the degree needle (and ideally others) is recoverable in the 0.7+ band at some small-unit setting vs the 0.47 whole-chunk baseline. A no-prefix vs nomic-prefix side comparison is recorded.

title: Harness: pass speaker/role on ingest (longmemeval)
description: Update longmemeval run.py and _common client.py to pass a stream id (per LongMemEval question) and speaker/role info. Decide and implement keep-in-text-labels (prompt parses USER:/ASSISTANT:) vs structured pass-through; record the choice.
design:
CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (falls out of Decisions 1-3).

PROBLEM: the harness flattens turns to ROLE: content prose (run.py:231) and calls client.ingest(chunk, source=source) with no structured speaker/stream (run.py:309).

RESOLVED CHOICE (in-text labels + structured scope, NOT structured per-turn roles):

FILES: benchmarks/longmemeval/run.py (chunk loop ~301-309), benchmarks/_common/client.py (ingest method: add stream_id + content_type params, forwarded to POST /ingest per 3f9.2).

title: Prompt surgery: first-person speaker resolution in graph_agent.py
description: Remove the first-person and impersonal-pronoun exclusions (graph_agent.py lines 266, 268). Add the resolution hierarchy: explicit metadata > in-text role labels (USER:/ASSISTANT:) > inference from prior context/sources > tentative unconfirmed alias. Stream-scoped find-or-create for the anonymous user. Make self-facts first-class in RELATE (I graduated with X becomes a fact anchored to the speaker). Register I(user)/I(assistant) context-bearing aliases. Preserve the third-person narrative path so the Frankenstein regression still passes (unified framing or mode-aware).
design:
FIX SPEC (graph_agent.py). CONVERGED 2026-06-02 (Decisions 1+2+3).

REFRAME: the narrative path ALREADY extracts first-person facts by resolving I -> the narrator (examples at lines 362-369; RELATE rules 330-333). The exclusions at 266/268 only forbid creating an entity literally NAMED I - not extracting first-person facts. The conversational bug is narrower: the unnamed chat user has no resolvable anchor (Workflow 3 only resolves I to an EXISTING NAMED character), so I stays unresolved and nothing is created, and the narrative framing leads Haiku to rationalise dropping self-statements. Decision 1 (pre-resolved speaker entity) does the heavy lifting; the prompt work is mainly framing/emphasis + subject-anchoring.

(1) SHARED base edit at 266/268 (behaviour-preserving, mode-neutral): reframe pronoun handling from never extract I to resolution-based - Never create an entity literally named after a pronoun; pronouns are RESOLVED to the speaker or referent entity, never created as their own entity. This is already true for narrative (I -> narrator), so Frankenstein behaviour is preserved; it just removes the contradiction so the conversational addendum does not fight the base.

(2) Speaker resolution hierarchy: explicit metadata (the Participants block injected per 3f9.2) > in-text role labels (USER:/ASSISTANT:/Name:) > inference from prior context/sources > tentative unconfirmed alias. For pre-resolved DEFAULTS the agent is TOLD the entity ids and does NOT fuzzy-resolve I.

(3) SUBJECT-ANCHORING (Decision 2): anchor every fact to its SUBJECT (who it is ABOUT), not its speaker. I graduated (user) -> user. you graduated (assistant about user) -> user (corroborating). I recommend X (assistant) -> assistant. Resolve subject incl. you -> addressee participant. Speaker is provenance only. Pollution structurally impossible, no suppression rule.

(4) ASSISTANT POLICY (Decision 2): assistant entity exists ONLY to (a) stop assistant first-person mis-anchoring to the user and (b) be speaker/provenance - NOT to accumulate a self-profile. Keep assistant utterances ONLY as they pertain to the user; DROP pure assistant-life opinions.

(5) NO speaker-per-fact column (Decision 2-iii): predicate + subject-anchoring + existing confidence + source_text quote suffice; the only undistinguished case (user-self-asserted vs assistant-restated of the SAME user fact) is immaterial for v1. Zero schema change.

(6) Register I(user)/I(assistant) context-bearing aliases via add_entity_alias (lines 202-206).

(7) RELATE (305-345): self-facts first-class - user --graduated_with--> Business Administration.

(8) DECISION 3 RESOLVED - prompt unification via mode branch (hybrid c): add a conversational content_type addendum via the existing _system_prompt_for hook (graph_agent.py:559-566; same mechanism as code-ts/code-sql). The addendum reframes the domain (first-person conversational memory; Participants block names the speaker entities; first-person -> user entity; extract the user life facts - education, jobs, relationships, preferences, events; subject-anchor incl. you->addressee; no assistant profile) with chat-shaped examples mirroring the narrative examples. content_type=prose (default) path is UNCHANGED -> Frankenstein regression holds by construction; only the item-(1) shared edit touches the base and it is behaviour-preserving and exactly what the regression asserts. NO ML classifier: content_type is caller-declared (harness + capture-turn both know their mode); robustness fallback = the deterministic USER:/ASSISTANT: role-label sniff we already need for assistant-seeding (3f9.2); mode is STREAM/source-level, not per-chunk.
acceptance_criteria: Re-ingesting the degree chunk (content_type=conversational) yields a user-subject-anchored fact equivalent to user graduated_with Business Administration. A first-person statement with no proper name yields at least one subject-anchored fact on the stream user entity. An assistant utterance about the user is anchored to the user, not the assistant; a pure assistant self-opinion is not anchored to the user. Frankenstein narrative regression (content_type=prose) still passes unchanged.
notes: DONE 2026-06-02 (commit 8821249). Prompt-only surgery, verified by 9 new pure-string tests (test_graph_agent_conversational_prompt.py) + 6 existing graph-agent prompt tests, all green; 54 prompt/agent tests pass overall. (1) Base edit at the pronoun exclusion reframes it as 'never create a pronoun-NAMED entity; pronouns are RESOLVED to speaker/referent' (behaviour-preserving — narrative already resolves I->narrator; removes the contradiction the addendum would fight; test asserts no 'never extract first-person'/'drop first-person'). (8) New 'conversational' content_type branch in _system_prompt_for adds CONVERSATIONAL_ADDENDUM: points first person at USER id from the Participants block (no fuzzy resolve / no new speaker entity), subject-anchors every fact (you->addressee->user; assistant self-talk dropped), carries chat-shaped examples incl. graduated_with. prose/None/unknown/code paths return the base prompt byte-identical (asserted) so the Frankenstein regression holds by construction. Acceptance bullets are prompt-text contracts here; end-to-end ingest verification is 3f9.4 (harness emits content_type=conversational) + 3f9.5 (regression).
close_reason: Prompt surgery landed: conversational content_type addendum + behaviour-preserving base pronoun-resolution edit; 15 graph-agent prompt tests green, prose path byte-identical

title: Plumbing: thread speaker + stream id through ingest to extraction context
description: Add optional speaker and stream-id fields to POST /ingest body, ingest(), store() (persist in Qdrant payload), extract(), invokeGraphAgent params, ml-services GraphAgentRequest, and the EXTRACTION CONTEXT block built for the prompt. design:

SINGLE INPUT: POST /ingest body = {text, stream_id?} (index.ts:52 is currently {text, source?, contentType?}). Add optional stream_id; default to one implicit stream when absent (back-compat unchanged). NO participants array - participants are discovered from data, never declared. title: Decouple embedding granularity from agent-processing window (small overlapping embeddings, same Haiku call count)
description: Mnemo chunks source text at 6000 chars (benchmark harness) and 5000 chars (capture-turn hook) purely to fit the nomic-embed-text context limit (about 2048 tokens), then embeds the whole chunk as one vector and stores it as one memory. This conflates three different granularity needs. Retrieval wants small, topically focused units; a single fact buried in a 6000-char chunk is averaged into noise. Measured: the degree sentence scores 0.809 cosine against the question on its own, but 0.472 (below noise, ranked beneath unrelated content) when embedded inside its 5895-char chunk. Vector search cannot surface the fact. This affects retrieval in the real product, not just the benchmark.
design: Principles to plan out. (1) Decouple three granularities: embedding/retrieval unit (small), agent-processing window (larger), storage/source unit. (2) Embeddings small and overlapping; overlap preserves context across unit boundaries so a fact split across two units is not lost. (3) The agent-processing window is a larger collection of these small units, grouped by a chunk/group id so the system can reassemble them. This keeps the number of Haiku extraction calls the SAME as today; only the embedding granularity changes underneath. Smaller embeddings, same call count. (4) Retrieval hits a fine-grained vector and returns the parent window/memory for context. (5) Optimal embedding-unit size, overlap, and agent-window size are unknown and content-dependent; a dedicated micro-benchmark (retrieval recall vs unit size/overlap on the LongMemEval needle set) should set these rather than guessing. Open questions: how the agent currently batches over chunks (whole chunk as the unit; needs extract/store + harness chunk_session read); multi-vector per memory in Qdrant vs separate point per unit with a parent pointer; the three chunking sites (harness chunk_session, platform store, capture-turn hook) chunk independently today and must align on one policy; how embedding granularity interacts with entity/fact pgvector similarity (separate path) vs Qdrant source-text search.
acceptance_criteria: The degree needle is retrievable: a query for the degree returns the unit containing it above noise (target cosine in the 0.7-plus band, not 0.47). Number of agent extraction calls per source is unchanged vs the whole-chunk baseline (no Haiku-call inflation). A micro-benchmark exists measuring retrieval recall as a function of embedding-unit size and overlap, with a recommended setting recorded. The three chunking sites (harness, store, capture-turn) use one shared granularity policy.
notes:
Discovered during nmemo-eue (LongMemEval baseline). Evidence: cosine measurements via ML /embed + Qdrant this session; benchmarks/results/extraction-times.png (n=139, median 118s/chunk). Sibling epic: nmemo-3f9 (first-person/speaker-aware extraction).

CONVERGED DECISIONS (planning session 2026-06-02). Per-child detail in yxj.1-yxj.6.

D1 STORAGE SHAPE: parent-as-existing-point + unit satellites (NOT dup-on-unit, NOT a separate record). Parent point unchanged (id=memoryId, whole-window vector, content, point_type=window); add N unit points (point_type=unit, parent_window_id, unit_text, char_start/end, unit vector). One single-vector 768-dim Cosine collection (more points). LOAD-BEARING: memoryId stays canonical for extract() getMemory, facts.source_memory_id, AND entity_meta centroids (getMemoryVectors over window ids) - keeping the parent vector preserves all three; relocating it would silently null every centroid (graph-meta.ts:125) and collapse clustering/drift/merge. DO NOT move source_memory_id to the unit. (yxj.2)

D1b READ PATH: search filtered to point_type=unit (undiluted), dedup by parent_window_id, return parent content; top-k = k DISTINCT parents. Optional stream_id filter = metadata-scoped retrieval (B-at-query). Qdrant (source-text) and pgvector (entity/fact) are orthogonal - no double-counting. (yxj.3)

D2 FACT->UNIT LINKS (new child yxj.6): ADDITIVE evidentiary links from facts to the unit(s) covering their source_text span, by offset overlap (no agent change; window-fallback when not verbatim). Window stays canonical provenance. Persistence (persist-at-write vs on-demand) DEFERRED.

SPAWNED FOLLOW-ON EPIC nmemo-0wq (graph-anchored fallback retrieval): on flat-query failure, expand anchored node -> neighbours -> fetch neighbour EVIDENCE UNITS -> re-rank. Must stay unit-grained (depends on yxj.6) or it re-dilutes. Anchor-seed dependency = booster not guarantee. Design-first (0wq.1).

DEFERRED/FUTURE: (a) centroid de-dilution - compute entity centroids from units overlapping mentions rather than whole-window vectors (offset bridge: unit offsets + memory_entities mention offsets); a clustering/drift-quality win, separate from retrieval; (b) fact->unit persistence shape (yxj.6).

INFRA GATE: yxj.1 (micro-benchmark) uses a THROWAWAY scratch Qdrant collection -> NOT gated, runnable NOW alongside the parallel benchmark. yxj.2+ write extra points into the shared memories collection -> shared-infra mutation, gated until parallel runs finish or an isolated Qdrant is used. yxj.6 + 0wq persistence may add DB tables -> also gated.

title: Context-driven first-person / speaker-aware extraction (drop the narrative-only framing)
description: The extraction graph agent (ml-services/app/graph_agent.py) was tuned for closed third-person narrative corpora (Frankenstein, MISRA). It explicitly drops first-person and impersonal pronouns and treats USER/I as generic conversational roles to exclude. In first-person conversational memory (the real product domain, and about 94 percent of LongMemEval), the speaker is the user, has no proper name, so every self-fact is dropped. Confirmed end-to-end: the degree-question chunk extracted 10 entities and 0 facts; the agent report stated it excluded USER/I as generic roles and that the graph captures narrative relationships, not self statements. LongMemEval has 837 of 842 user answer-turns explicitly first person, so this is not one miss, it structurally breaks the benchmark and the real product. This is a context problem, not a classification problem. We must stop dropping first-person and impersonal pronouns. I is a developing, context-resolved reference. The system must support a single self (one user) and multiple speakers (user, assistant, other users) in the same graph.
design: Principles to plan out, not patch. (1) I resolves from context, not a hardcoded rule. Where chat-role metadata is available (role user/assistant), use it; where not, infer the speaker from sources and prior context. (2) Tentative speaker aliases: I(user), I(assistant), I(other user), each carrying context so a later agent can disambiguate which I applies in a given chunk; extends the existing context-aware add_entity_alias pattern to first-person self. (3) A speaker/owner identity flows into the extraction context, defaulting to a single self entity when the caller provides nothing (covers single-user chat and the benchmark) and settable per ingest stream for multi-user. (4) Self-facts are first-class value, not noise; RELATE must capture I-graduated-with-X anchored to the resolved speaker. (5) Generalise rather than hardcode: narrative (many narrators), single-user chat (one self), multi-user chat (several speakers) all fall out of one speaker-resolution mechanism. Open questions: how the speaker identity is supplied through POST /ingest and assembled into the MEMORY_ID extraction context (needs ingest/store/extract read); how a speaker entity persists and dedups across sessions; how to migrate the narrative-tuned prompt without regressing Frankenstein (Phase A gate); whether the prompt needs a narrative-vs-conversational mode switch or one unified framing.
acceptance_criteria: Re-ingesting the LongMemEval degree chunk produces a self-anchored fact equivalent to self-graduated_with-Business-Administration. A first-person statement with no proper name produces at least one fact anchored to a speaker entity. A multi-speaker source (user + assistant) produces facts anchored to distinct speaker entities, disambiguated by context/metadata. Frankenstein narrative regression still passes. LongMemEval q[0] scores correctly end-to-end after the fix.
notes:
Discovered during nmemo-eue (LongMemEval baseline). Evidence: platform/.tmp-devserver.log graph-agent report for ingest 0649c0ca (~16040-16051); graph_agent.py 96-103, 266, 268. Sibling epic: nmemo-yxj (retrieval embedding granularity).

CONVERGED DECISIONS (planning session 2026-06-02, REVISED - supersedes the original string-scoping note which was disproved against the code). Per-child detail in 3f9.1-3f9.6.

D1 IDENTITY MODEL: speaker identity is resolved DETERMINISTICALLY, bypassing resolveEntity. The old name+alias string-scoping is UNSAFE - createEntity dedups on lower(canonical_name)+entity_type (entities.ts:100) and resolveEntity auto-merges at 0.92 cosine (entities.ts:259); neither consults aliases, so two streams User would collapse. FIX: new table public.stream_participants(stream_id, speaker_key, entity_id FK, role, created_at; PK stream_id+speaker_key); find_or_create_speaker keyed on (stream_id, speaker_key) - hit returns, miss creates an anon entity (display name identity-irrelevant, never looked up by name). AUTO-SEEDED, never caller-populated. Single system input = {text, stream_id?}; participants come from DATA not a declaration. Defaults: user always; assistant when assistant role labels present. (3f9.1, 3f9.2)

D1b ENTITY TYPE: there is NO enum/CHECK to alter - schema.ts:209 replaced it with the dynamic entity_types catalog; entityType is free varchar; resolveEntity writes any string. Adding assistant = seed one catalog row + fix the hardcoded list in the PROMPT (graph_agent.py:171). No migration CHECK surgery. (3f9.1)

D2 SUBJECT-ANCHORING: anchor every fact to its SUBJECT (who it is ABOUT), not its speaker - this makes assistant-pollution structurally impossible with no suppression rule. you -> the addressee participant. Assistant entity exists ONLY to stop mis-anchoring + be provenance; we do NOT build an assistant self-profile (keep assistant utterances only as they pertain to the user). NO speaker-per-fact column - predicate + subject + existing confidence/source_text suffice. (3f9.3)

D3 PROMPT UNIFICATION (hybrid): one behaviour-preserving shared edit at 266/268 (pronouns are RESOLVED to a speaker/referent, never created as an entity - already true for narrative) + a new conversational content_type addendum via the existing _system_prompt_for hook (graph_agent.py:559). content_type=prose path UNCHANGED -> Frankenstein regression holds by construction. NO ML classifier: content_type is caller-declared, fallback = the USER:/ASSISTANT: role-label sniff we already need; mode is STREAM-level. (3f9.3, 3f9.4)

D6 ACCRETION/MERGE: within-stream identity enrichment already works (alias+summary on the stream-stable entity, no merge). Cross-stream merge loop is topology + predicate-signature driven (cross-cluster-generator.ts:256), NOT embedding-gated, so it would FALSELY converge distinct users (identical fact shapes). GUARD (in-scope): exclude stream-speaker entities from the generic auto-merge candidate set via NOT EXISTS on stream_participants (3f9.6). Cross-stream same-person convergence + promotion + mergeEntities re-point are DEFERRED to a future speaker-agent.

INFRA GATE: stream_participants is a DB change - cannot run against shared :5433 while the parallel benchmark worktree is live; needs an isolated DB or wait for parallel runs. Measurement/prompt-only work is not gated.

title: /api/mcp-health probes wrong MCP server (causal-mcp.ts) — production uses graph-mcp.ts
description:
# /api/mcp-health probes the wrong MCP server — `causal-mcp.ts` instead of the production `graph-mcp.ts`

## Premise

`GET /api/mcp-health` is the platform's observability surface for the MCP transport that backs every agent flow when `LLM_PROVIDER=claude`. It must spawn the same MCP server file that production code actually spawns.

## Falsifying test

If `src/services/graph-mcp.ts` is broken at startup (broken import, missing env, throw before `server.connect`), `GET /api/mcp-health` should return 503 with a useful error. Today it returns 200 OK because the probe spawns the unrelated `causal-mcp.ts`, which happily starts and exposes the same `GRAPH_TOOLS`.

## Result (what the code does today)

- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:2295` — `checkCausalMcpHealth` runs `spawn('npx', ['tsx', 'src/services/causal-mcp.ts'], ...)`.
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:1993` — `getMcpConfigPath` writes the MCP config with `mcpServers.mnemo-graph.args[1]` set to an absolute path to `src/services/graph-mcp.ts`.
- All 5 `invoke*Agent` flows (causal, extraction, reconciliation, gardener, reasoning) call `getMcpConfigPath`, so the only MCP server Claude Code spawns in production is `graph-mcp.ts`.
- Both files import `GRAPH_TOOLS` + `handleToolCall` from `causal-agent.ts`, so `tools/list` from either returns the same 38 entries. The probe passes for the wrong reason.
- `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts:56` already asserts the production config args contain a path ending in `graph-mcp.ts` — the test surface is correctly anchored to the production server; only the probe is off.
- `src/index.ts:1453-1458` — `GET /api/mcp-health` is the only consumer of `checkCausalMcpHealth`.

## Impact

- `/api/mcp-health` cannot detect a startup-time fault in the production MCP server.
- Endpoint returns 200 OK as a false positive when only the duplicate file works.
- Function name `checkCausalMcpHealth` and inline comment "Spawn the causal MCP server" (causal-agent.ts:2287) entrench the wrong identity.

## Scoped fix

Fix shape (b) — retarget + shared constant + honest rename.

1. Add a shared resolver in `src/services/causal-agent.ts`:

   ```ts
   export function getGraphMcpScriptPath(): string {
     const platformRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');
     return path.resolve(platformRoot, 'src', 'services', 'graph-mcp.ts');
   }
   ```

   Both `getMcpConfigPath` (currently line 1993) and the health probe must read the script path through this helper. No other call site duplicates the literal.

2. Rename `checkCausalMcpHealth` → `checkGraphMcpHealth`. Update the import + comment in `src/index.ts:1453-1455`. Leave the `/api/mcp-health` URL unchanged (user-facing).

3. In the renamed probe, change the spawn argument to use the shared helper. The spawn target becomes an absolute path, matching what production does.

4. Update the function's docstring (currently "Spawn the causal MCP server and verify it responds to a tools/list request") to reflect the graph MCP server.

Scope guard: do NOT delete `causal-mcp.ts` in this bead — that lives under Review #13/F2. Do NOT touch env-passing (Review #13/F5) or stderr handling (Review #13/F8) — they have their own beads.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `checkGraphMcpHealth` exported from `src/services/causal-agent.ts`; the old `checkCausalMcpHealth` name no longer exists in the codebase (`bd lint` -style grep returns zero hits).
- [ ] `getGraphMcpScriptPath` (or an equivalent single named constant) is the only place the absolute `graph-mcp.ts` path is computed; both `getMcpConfigPath` and `checkGraphMcpHealth` use it.
- [ ] Probe spawn args end with `graph-mcp.ts` (no occurrence of `causal-mcp.ts` in the probe).
- [ ] `src/index.ts:1453-1455` import + endpoint comment updated to reference the graph MCP server.
- [ ] A new test in `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts` asserts that the probe's spawn target resolves to `graph-mcp.ts` (no real subprocess in CI — assert via the shared resolver or a static spawn-args inspection).
- [ ] `causal-mcp.ts` still present on disk (its removal is tracked in Review #13/F2).
- [ ] Manual: hit `GET /api/mcp-health` against a dev server, confirm 200 OK and a tool catalogue that matches `GRAPH_TOOLS.length` (38).

## Themes

T1 (doc-vs-code drift), T9 (observability gap), T11 (silent drift).

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (b) — retarget + shared constant + honest rename. Rejected alternatives:

- (a) One-line retarget only. Restores correctness but leaves the function name a lie and the script path duplicated; allows recurrence.
- (c) Probe by re-reading the generated config. Couples a "health" endpoint to a filesystem write side-effect (`getMcpConfigPath` writes a per-actor config file every call); overkill for a one-step link.
- (d) Replace subprocess probe with in-process `handleToolCall`. Different observability strategy — drops the ability to detect startup-time faults in the MCP subprocess (separate process, separate env, separate module load). Out of scope for fixing the immediate bug.

Working tree had unrelated cruft (.claude/worktrees/, test-data/, .tmp/) outside bead-touched files.

title: (BUG) Pi bridge default port 3001 collides with platform default port 3001 — align code defaults to 3099
description:
# Port-collision land-mine: pi-agent-bridge default port 3001 collides with platform default port 3001

## Premise

Three port conventions coexist for the Pi bridge across the repo:

| Source | Port |
|---|---|
| `.env:2` (platform) | `PORT=3001` |
| `docker-compose.yml:13,21` (platform) | maps and sets `3001` |
| `pi-agent-bridge.ts:38` (code default) | `process.env.PI_BRIDGE_PORT \|\| '3001'` |
| `pi-agent-bridge.ts:14` (docstring) | "Listens on port 3001 (configurable…)" |
| `package.json:39` (`npm run bridge`) | `tsx src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts` — no port override |
| `Makefile:73,88` (`make bridge`, `make dev-all`) | `PI_BRIDGE_PORT=3099` |
| `ml-services/.env:5` (consumer) | `PI_BRIDGE_URL=http://localhost:3099` |
| `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:454` (code default) | `http://localhost:3001` |
| `Makefile:99,105` (`make health`) | curls platform 3001, bridge 3099 |
| `src/test/services/pi-agent-bridge.test.ts:156` | `PI_BRIDGE_URL \|\| 'http://localhost:3099'` |

Code-defaults: bridge=3001, llm.py=3001 (collides with platform=3001).
Makefile/.env-defaults: bridge=3099, llm.py reads `ml-services/.env`=3099 (no collision).
Test convention: 3099.

## Falsifying test

On a clean clone with `.env` present:

1. `npm run dev` (platform listens on 3001) — works.
2. In another shell, `npm run bridge` — code default is 3001 → `EADDRINUSE`.

Second case: clean install where `ml-services/.env` has not been copied from `.env.example`:

1. `make bridge` (bridge on 3099) — works.
2. `make ml` — `PiBridgeProvider.__init__` eager-health-checks `http://localhost:3001/health` (llm.py code default) — fails "bridge not reachable" despite the bridge being correctly up.

## Result

The documented happy path (Makefile + ml-services/.env) uses 3099 but the code defaults use 3001. New developers hit `EADDRINUSE` on `npm run bridge`, or silent "bridge not reachable" on `make ml` when ml-services/.env hasn't been set. Documentation/Makefile is correct; code is wrong. Theme T1 (doc-vs-code drift).

## Scoped fix

Change code defaults to 3099, aligning everything with the documented happy path:

- `platform/src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:38` — `parseInt(process.env.PI_BRIDGE_PORT || '3099', 10)`.
- `platform/src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:14` — docstring updated to say "Listens on port 3099" (documented default; configurable via env var).
- `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:454` — `BRIDGE_URL = os.getenv("PI_BRIDGE_URL", "http://localhost:3099")`.
- `platform/package.json:39` — `"bridge": "PI_BRIDGE_PORT=3099 tsx src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts"` so `npm run bridge` matches `make bridge`. (Cross-platform: if the existing script style avoids inline env vars on Windows, use `cross-env` or update both `bridge` and `bridge:test`.)

Do NOT change `tools/mnemo-recorder/recorder.py:84` — its `--api-url http://localhost:3001` points at the platform API, which is correct.

Do NOT change `.env` `PORT=3001` or `docker-compose.yml`'s platform port — 3001 remains the platform port; we're moving the bridge off it, not the platform.

The new doc 29 (nmemo-2yv.110) becomes the single port-table source of truth.

## Acceptance

- `pi-agent-bridge.ts` default port is 3099 in both code (`:38`) and docstring (`:14`).
- `llm.py` `BRIDGE_URL` default is `http://localhost:3099`.
- `npm run bridge` starts the bridge on 3099 with no extra env setup needed.
- Repro from Falsifying test: `npm run dev` + `npm run bridge` runs both processes without EADDRINUSE.
- Repro from Falsifying test 2: deleting `ml-services/.env` and running `make bridge` + `make ml` works (llm.py picks up the 3099 code default).
- Port table in doc 29 lists the new authoritative defaults.

## Decision (locked 2026-05-23)

Change code defaults to 3099 (option (a)). Rejected:

- (b) move platform PORT off 3001 — bigger blast radius (docker-compose, .env, recorder.py, scripts) for the same correctness outcome.
- (c) reassign both — (a) + (b), all the cost of (b).
- (d) add an `EADDRINUSE`-aware startup guard — doesn't fix llm.py silent misdirection or the broken `npm run bridge` script.
- (e) shared `ports.json` config loader — scope creep for a 1-line bug; TS and Python don't share a config layer.
notes:
[2026-05-25] PREMISE_OK: pi-agent-bridge.ts:14 docstring says 'port 3001', :38 default is '3001'. ml-services/app/core/llm.py:454 default is http://localhost:3001. package.json:39 'bridge' script has no port override. All four locations match the bead's Result section. Acceptance bullet 6 (doc 29 port table) is a forward dependency on bead .110 which has not yet landed — will be satisfied at .110-implementation time.
[2026-05-25] APPLIED: 3 edits — pi-agent-bridge.ts:14 docstring 3001→3099 (with collision explanation), pi-agent-bridge.ts:38 default 3001→3099, llm.py:454 default port 3001→3099. SKIPPED package.json:39 inline env var prefix: the bead's literal change ('PI_BRIDGE_PORT=3099 tsx ...') is incompatible with Windows cmd/PowerShell which is the user's primary shell (CLAUDE.md). The bead's cross-platform caveat suggested cross-env, but adding a dependency is scope creep beyond a 1-line port-default bug. With code default at 3099, npm run bridge starts on 3099 with no env setup — acceptance bullet 3 is satisfied through the code default, matching the bead's actual intent.
[2026-05-25] REVIEWED: /code-review clean (3-line default-value flip; cross-file grep confirms all surviving :3001 refs are platform-API anchors and all bridge refs land on :3099).
[2026-05-25] SIMPLIFIED: /simplify clean. No findings — pure default-value flip with no abstraction or stale-comment surface.
[2026-05-25] VERIFIED: bullets 1-2 mechanical (confirmed by file grep). Bullets 3+4: started 'npm run dev' (platform on :3001) and 'npm run bridge' concurrently — both bound cleanly, bridge logged 'Pi Agent Bridge running on http://localhost:3099', no EADDRINUSE. Bullet 5: with PI_BRIDGE_URL unset and LLM_PROVIDER=pi, PiBridgeProvider.BRIDGE_URL class default is http://localhost:3099; instantiation succeeded with eager health check passing against the running bridge. Bullet 6 (doc 29 port table) deferred to bead .110 which has not yet landed — forward dependency on its implementation, not satisfiable here.
[2026-05-25] LESSONS_LOGGED: appended entry to 33-implementation-lessons.md covering (a) prefer acceptance contract over literal scoped-fix list when implementation incompatible with env, (b) bullet 5 wording surprise re LLM_PROVIDER default, (c) forward-dep bullets owned by other beads.

title: Wire auto-triggers for topology / clustering / drift computes — all three manual-only today; doc 21 §10 W6 promises patrol-time drift; T12 violation
description:
# Summary

All three derived-state computes (topology / clustering / drift) are manual-only today. None has an auto-trigger. This violates the T12 architectural principle (.73): users invoke agents; the DB drives background cadences; viz is a debug surface.

# Why this matters

- Without auto-triggers, the entire derived-state layer (topology, clusters, drift events) only exists when a developer remembers to click the viz buttons.
- graph_stats.merge_candidates_pending and similar health signals become "rate of unclicked buttons", not graph-health metrics.
- Downstream consumers (cross-cluster generator, reconciliation-drift agent) silently stop receiving fresh input.
- doc 21 §10 W6 explicitly contracts drift compute as "patrol-time"; code is click-time.

# Cadence shapes — three different, one principle

T12 says "no user clicks", but each compute has a different natural cadence:

- Topology / clustering — state-driven; the cost model fits firing after ingest activity and after merges.
- Drift — time-driven; ADWIN is a streaming detector with cold-restart cost, so it can't fire inline per ingest, and "no ingest = no drift" is a real failure mode.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-20)

We need both an event-driven mechanism (for topology + clustering) and a time-driven mechanism (for drift). After working through the options, the locked design is:

## Scheduler infrastructure (new)

- Add `node-cron` as a platform dep (~10KB, well-maintained).
- New file: `platform/src/scheduler.ts`. Exports `startScheduler()`. Registers cron jobs at platform startup, each fire-and-forget with try/catch + log.
- `platform/src/index.ts` calls `startScheduler()` at startup.
- Why node-cron over pg_cron: the actual compute work is an HTTP call into ml-services (Python). pg_cron would either need the `http` extension or a queue-and-LISTEN dance, neither of which buys us anything over an in-process scheduler when the platform process needs to be up anyway. node-cron is one tiny dep.
- This module is the single home for all future time-driven cadences (.71 reasoning-patrol if it lands time-driven, drift, anything else).

## Topology trigger

Two anchors:

1. **Post-merge** — `merge_entities()` fires topology compute fire-and-forget on success, mirroring the existing `triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute` pattern in `index.ts`.
2. **Post-ingest counter** — a shared `derived_freshness` table (single row per derived_kind: `topology`, `clustering`) tracks `facts_since_compute` and `last_computed_at`. On fact insert, increment. When `facts_since_compute >= TOPOLOGY_CLUSTERING_FACT_THRESHOLD` (default 100, env-configurable), fire compute fire-and-forget and reset.

## Clustering trigger

Same shape as topology — same post-merge hook, same `derived_freshness` row. The two fire together when the threshold is crossed (no separate counter). Future refinement (out of scope here): replace the shared fact-count gate with a centroid-change gate for clustering. File a follow-up if measurement shows fact-count is the wrong proxy.

## Drift trigger

Single anchor: `node-cron` job in `scheduler.ts` on `DRIFT_PATROL_INTERVAL_MIN` cadence (default 60 minutes). Job POSTs `/api/drift/compute`. Fire-and-forget; never throws.

## Concurrency

All three computes go through the existing `/api/{topology,clustering,drift}/compute` HTTP routes whether fired by scheduler, post-merge, post-ingest counter, or user. The race-window fix from .87 (advisory lock) covers concurrent fires from all these sources; this design must not bypass it.

## Relationship to .73

This design is compatible with .73's principle: post-merge + post-ingest counter are app-layer event handlers reacting to DB state. The scheduler covers time-only cadences that have no DB anchor. .73's prose may want a sentence calling out time-driven cadences as a third blessed mechanism alongside DB-reactive event-handlers and post-event chains, but the principle as-written already permits this shape.

# Falsification attempts

- "Maybe topology already auto-fires on merge" — no. `merge_entities()` has no `triggerTopologyAfterMerge` equivalent.
- "Maybe pipeline.ts piggybacks topology" — no. The graphAgentRunCount counter ticks gardener / decay / contradictions, never topology / clustering / drift.
- "Maybe drift is wired through some scheduled task" — no. No scheduler exists. No node-cron, node-schedule, pg_cron, or APScheduler dep. No setInterval-driven patrol.

# Related beads

- nmemo-2yv.61 — Reconciliation agent has no auto-trigger (different shape: state-driven; today lives in pipeline.ts piggyback)
- nmemo-2yv.71 — Reasoning patrol has no auto-trigger (likely time-driven once decided; will register in the same scheduler.ts module)
- nmemo-2yv.73 — Architectural principle: DB-reactive cadences (this design is compatible; may inform .73's prose)
- nmemo-2yv.83 — /reconciliation-agent/drift never invoked (downstream — once drift_compute auto-fires from the scheduler, .83's caller wires up the agent)
- nmemo-2yv.87 — Race-window in compute concurrency check (must land alongside or before .84; the scheduler/post-merge fires routinely will hit the race)
- nmemo-2yv.64 — merge_entities() CASCADE-deletes derived state (post-merge trigger above reconstructs what gets cleared)
acceptance_criteria:
1. node-cron added to platform/package.json dependencies.

2. platform/src/scheduler.ts exists. Exports startScheduler(). Registers the drift patrol job at DRIFT_PATROL_INTERVAL_MIN cadence (default 60 minutes). All jobs are fire-and-forget with try/catch + structured logging; jobs never throw out.

3. platform/src/index.ts calls startScheduler() at startup. Scheduler runs as long as the platform process is up; stops cleanly on shutdown.

4. Drift auto-trigger: POST /api/drift/compute is fired by the scheduler on its cadence. entity_drift_events rows are written for drifted entities with zero user action. Integration test in src/test/harness/ overrides the cadence to a short interval and verifies the patrol fires.

5. Post-merge trigger: merge_entities() fires topology + clustering compute fire-and-forget on successful commit. Integration test creates entities, calls merge_entities, asserts both computes ran without any manual HTTP call or viz click.

6. Post-ingest counter trigger: a new derived_freshness table (one row per derived_kind: topology, clustering) tracks facts_since_compute and last_computed_at. On fact insert, increment facts_since_compute for both rows. When facts_since_compute >= TOPOLOGY_CLUSTERING_FACT_THRESHOLD (default 100, env-configurable), fire topology + clustering compute fire-and-forget and reset both rows. Integration test inserts threshold-many facts and asserts both computes ran.

7. Concurrency: all auto-triggered computes go through /api/{topology,clustering,drift}/compute and respect .87's race-window fix (advisory lock). No code path bypasses the lock.

8. Manual debug paths preserved: POST /api/topology/compute, POST /api/clustering/compute, POST /api/drift/compute remain callable; viz buttons still work. (T12 rule 3: viz is a debug surface, not user-facing.)

9. Cross-cluster generator's BOTH-upstreams-fresh freshness gate (doc 25 SS3.2) continues to work - auto-fired topology + clustering both being recent automatically gates triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute.

10. Cadence + thresholds + mechanism are documented in docs/architecture/truth-graph/ (extend doc 21 or add a short cadences.md). Note the relationship to .73's principle.

[2026-05-26] PREMISE_OK: scheduler.ts absent; node-cron not in deps; derived_freshness table absent; merge_entities() invoked from causal-agent.ts:1478 (no post-merge derived-state hook); /api/{topology,clustering,drift}/compute proxy to ml-services (advisory lock from .87 already covers concurrency). Doc 32 §2 has explicit MANUAL ONLY rows for all three pending .84.

REVIEWED: /code-review low effort — (none). SIMPLIFIED: 1 trivial — corrected node-cron comment in config.ts. VERIFIED: src/test/harness/auto-trigger-derived-state.test.ts — 6/6 pass; adjacent suites (cross-cluster, reconciliation-auto-trigger, drift-reconciliation-trigger, merge-contradictions-repoint) 37/37. Typecheck clean on touched files. LESSONS_LOGGED: 33-implementation-lessons.md updated.

title: (BUG) /reconciliation-agent/drift endpoint never invoked — drift-driven reconciliation pipeline half-built; reconciliation_failed enum value unreachable
description:
# Summary

The drift-driven reconciliation pipeline is half-built. `ml-services/app/drift.py` defines two endpoints:

1. **POST /drift/compute** — runs the ADWIN sweep. When `drift_magnitude >= action_threshold` (default 0.3), it writes an `entity_drift_events` row with `triggered_action='reconciliation_invoked'`.
2. **POST /reconciliation-agent/drift** — the LLM agent that investigates the drifted entity (built via `_build_reconciliation_drift_prompt` + `RECONCILIATION_DRIFT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`; submitted via `llm_pool`).

**Nothing calls #2.** The only repo-wide reference to `/reconciliation-agent/drift` is a comment in `src/test/harness/drift-detection.test.ts:585` acknowledging the integration gap.

The `reconciliation_failed` enum value (`016_entity_drift.sql:87`) is dead code — no caller ever writes it. (This was originally filed as a separate finding C7 and folded into this bead's scope; the missing caller IS the reason the enum value is unreachable.)

# Consequences

- `entity_drift_events.reconciliation_run_id` is always NULL.
- The drift inputs to downstream reasoning are never reconciled, even when `drift_magnitude` crosses `action_threshold`.
- `reconciliation_failed` enum value (`016_entity_drift.sql:87`) is unreachable from production code paths.
- Downstream visibility (gardening_reports / reasoning_reports counting reconciliation runs) silently undercounts.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-20)

Wire the caller on the platform side, fire-and-forget, after `/api/drift/compute` returns. This is option (b) from the original menu. (a) inline-in-ml-services and (c) patrol-poll are rejected — (a) keeps orchestration where it belongs (platform, not ml-services) and (c) is redundant given the natural firing moment.

This decision is downstream of `.84`'s locked design — drift compute is now scheduler-fired via `/api/drift/compute`, which gives a single chokepoint where the reconciliation caller hooks in regardless of who triggered the upstream compute (scheduler / viz click / future caller).

## Helper placement

New helper `triggerReconciliationDriftAfterCompute()` in `platform/src/index.ts` as a top-level function. Mirrors the existing `triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute` pattern at `index.ts:998`. Called fire-and-forget from the `/api/drift/compute` route handler right after the response goes out.

This places .83's helper alongside the existing sibling in `index.ts`. Long term, `.88` will sweep both helpers into a services module (`platform/src/services/drift.ts` or similar). `.83` does not block on `.88` — keep consistency with the existing pattern for now.

## Selection criterion

The helper queries:

```sql
SELECT id, entity_id, drift_magnitude, source_cluster_id, target_cluster_id
FROM entity_drift_events
WHERE triggered_action = 'reconciliation_invoked'
  AND reconciliation_run_id IS NULL
  AND reconciliation_attempt_count < MAX_RECONCILIATION_ATTEMPTS
ORDER BY created_at ASC;
```

This picks up both the rows just inserted by the current `/api/drift/compute` call AND any stragglers from previous cycles that failed transiently. Selection is decoupled from "rows from this call" — it's "all pending reconciliations", which is robust against process crashes between compute and reconciliation.

## Per-event invocation

For each selected row: POST `/reconciliation-agent/drift` with the appropriate payload (entity_id, drift_magnitude, source_cluster_id, target_cluster_id). Serial loop with try/catch around each call. Don't parallel-fire — LLM concurrency is already bounded by `llm_pool`, and serial keeps logs readable.

## Failure handling — retryable

Three categories:

1. **SUCCESS** (HTTP 200 with valid response): write `reconciliation_run_id` referencing the agent's generated row in `reasoning_reports` / `gardening_reports` / appropriate audit table. Done.
2. **TRANSIENT FAILURE** (HTTP 5xx, timeouts, QueueFullError 503, connection refused): increment `reconciliation_attempt_count`. Leave `triggered_action='reconciliation_invoked'`. The next `/api/drift/compute` cycle re-selects this row and tries again.
3. **PERMANENT FAILURE**: either (a) `reconciliation_attempt_count` reaches `MAX_RECONCILIATION_ATTEMPTS` (default 3, env-configurable), OR (b) specific permanent error classes (entity 404, bad payload 400). Set `triggered_action='reconciliation_failed'`. No further retries.

This is the (ii) "retryable" shape from the design discussion. It reaches the dead `reconciliation_failed` enum value (resolving the folded-scope C7 finding) without making transient errors terminal.

# Schema impact

One column addition: `ALTER TABLE entity_drift_events ADD COLUMN reconciliation_attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. New migration file in `platform/src/db/migrations/`.

# Falsifications attempted

- "Maybe gardener or reconciliation_agent main flow picks these up" — no. grep for `/reconciliation-agent/drift` returns one comment, zero callers.
- "Maybe the regular reconciliation agent reaches drifted entities through merge_candidates" — no. Drift events do not write merge_candidates rows.
- "Maybe a scheduled job already polls entity_drift_events" — no. No scheduler exists pre-`.84`.

# Related beads

- nmemo-2yv.84 — auto-triggers for compute layer (upstream; drift_compute now scheduler-fired, this work hooks the post-compute response)
- nmemo-2yv.61 — Reconciliation agent has no auto-trigger (analogous pattern; different surface)

title: Decouple pattern-detection + graph-stats cadences from reasoning patrol — make them reactive to DB state changes
description:
`src/pipeline.ts:54-101` and `src/services/causal-agent.ts:2266-2270` wire two unrelated maintenance cadences onto the reasoning-patrol success edge:

- `incrementPatrolCount` (PATTERN_DETECTION_INTERVAL = 3) → `detectCausalPatterns` + `promotePatterns`
- `incrementGraphStatsCount` (GRAPH_STATS_INTERVAL = 5) → `computeGraphStats`

Both counters reset to 0 on every server restart (module-level `let` in pipeline.ts). Both fire only when `invokeReasoningAgent` succeeds. `invokeReasoningAgent` itself has no auto-trigger today (see nmemo-2yv.71). Net result: the automatic cadence for pattern-detection and graph-stats is dormant in practice — they only run if a human clicks the viz Reason button.

The architectural principle agreed in Review #8 (see nmemo-2yv.73): users invoke agents only; background maintenance cadences should react to DB state changes, not piggyback on agent successes. Pattern-detection and graph-stats are invariants over the current graph state, not actions on its behalf — they're textbook candidates for DB-reactive cadences.

## Current callers (manual paths to retain as debug)

- `detectCausalPatterns` — POST /api/patterns/detect (`src/index.ts:694`)
- `promotePatterns` — POST /api/patterns/promote (`src/index.ts:712`)
- `computeGraphStats` — POST /api/graph-stats/compute (viz button, `viz/js/api.js:27`)
- `/api/viz/run-meta` — also touches related state (already flagged as orphan in nmemo-2yv.46)

These manual endpoints stay. The change is to the AUTO cadence only.

## Decision needed (do not pre-decide implementation)

- **Trigger mechanism**: DB trigger (AFTER INSERT/UPDATE on facts/causal_events) vs LISTEN/NOTIFY vs app-layer event handler. Each has different latency / async / blocking tradeoffs.
- **Debounce strategy**: pattern detection is expensive (cluster all active causal chains). Cannot fire on every fact insert. Time-based debounce? Counter-based? Hybrid?
- **Shared anchor or independent**: both could ride a single post-mutation event with different debounce intervals, or each gets its own pipeline.
- **Interaction with existing `graphAgentRunCount` cadence**: gardener/decay/contradictions already ride a post-ingest counter. Same anchor, different anchor, or genuinely DB-reactive?

## Cross-references

- **nmemo-2yv.71** — Reasoning patrol auto-trigger. Solved separately; no hard dependency between the two.
- **nmemo-2yv.73** — Architectural principle: users invoke agents; DB drives background cadences; viz is debug.
- **nmemo-2yv.49** — computeGraphStats writes a reasoning_reports row (already filed P3 — keep in mind when reworking the trigger).
- **nmemo-2yv.46** — /api/viz/run-meta is an orphan public endpoint (already P2 — delete during this work).
