title: Skip predicate-affinity recompute when poller fetch returns unchanged nodes
description:
## Premise (what the finding asserts)
A /code-review finding on nmemo-pd5.6 asserts that computePredicateAffinityLinks() (invoked at viz/js/app.js:49) runs an O(N^2) Jaccard pass over fact-subject entities on EVERY fetchData(), which is poller-driven every 5s when auto-refresh is on, even when state.forces.predicateAffinity defaults OFF (state.js:63). The finding's primary suggestion was to flag-gate the call. That primary suggestion is REJECTED here: nmemo-pd5.6's locked Scope deliberately chose eager precompute-on-each-fetch ("not per tick - too expensive") so toggle-ON is instant, and its acceptance budgets <100ms for ~200 entities. This bead captures only the finding's SECONDARY, lock-compatible suggestion: skip the recompute when state.data.nodes is unchanged.

## Falsifying test (how to disprove or confirm)
With auto-refresh ON and no new ingests, observe whether computePredicateAffinityLinks() re-runs the full O(N^2) pass on each 5s poll despite identical node membership. If the node set (ids/predicate signatures) is byte-for-byte identical between consecutive fetches yet the pass re-executes, the redundant work is confirmed. If a cheap identity/dirty check already short-circuits it, the finding is disproven.

## Result (what the code does today)
At viz/js/app.js:45-49, fetchData() unconditionally calls computePredicateAffinityLinks() after assigning state.data = unified, on every poll. The comment at app.js:46-48 acknowledges the per-tick cost (hence per-fetch, not per-tick) but does not guard against re-running on unchanged data. On a steady-state poller with no new ingests, the same Jaccard cache is recomputed every 5s.

## Impact
Low-to-moderate, scaling with N. At ~200 entities the lock's <100ms budget holds, but the epic targets ~944 nodes / ~200 fact-subject entities and is explicitly a hairball-scale experiment. Repeated O(N^2) work every 5s on unchanged data is wasted CPU on the render thread and grows quadratically as the corpus grows. No correctness defect; a steady-state efficiency leak.

## Scoped fix (rough sketch)
- Preserve eager-precompute semantics (toggle-ON must stay instant - cache always warm). Do NOT flag-gate.
- Add a cheap dirty check before the O(N^2) pass: e.g. compare a fingerprint of node membership + fact-subject predicate signatures (node count + a hash of sorted entity-id/predicate pairs) against the value from the prior fetch.
- If unchanged, reuse the cached state.predicateAffinityLinks and skip recompute.
- Recompute (and refresh the fingerprint) only when the fingerprint differs.

## Acceptance
- With auto-refresh ON and no new ingests, consecutive polls do NOT re-run the full Jaccard pass (verifiable via a counter/log or profiling).
- After an ingest that changes nodes or fact predicates, the next fetch recomputes and the cache reflects new affinities.
- Toggle-ON remains instant (cache present without waiting for a recompute).
- No change to the locked eager-precompute contract from nmemo-pd5.6 (precompute still happens whenever data changes, not lazily on toggle).

## Decision (UNLOCKED - needs human review per qualifier on 2026-05-28)
Awaiting human review to lock fix shape. Filed by qualifier from nmemo-pd5.6 on 2026-05-28.

## Derived from
- ORIGINATING_BEAD: nmemo-pd5.6
- SOURCE_SKILL: code-review
- FINDING_TEXT: viz/js/app.js:49 - computePredicateAffinityLinks() runs an O(N^2) Jaccard pass over fact-subject entities on EVERY fetchData() (poller-driven at 5s when auto-refresh on), even when state.forces.predicateAffinity defaults OFF (state.js:63). Suggestion: flag-gate OR skip recompute when state.data.nodes is unchanged.
design:
## Decision (locked 2026-05-29)
Add a cheap LINEAR dirty-check guarding the O(N^2) Jaccard pass in computePredicateAffinityLinks() (forces.js). Fix shape locked:
- Fingerprint is computed over the ONLY input that affects the result: fact edges' (subjectEntityId, predicate) pairs. Build it in one linear pass over state.data.edges (filter _edgeType==='fact'): a count + a 32-bit rolling string hash (h = (h*31 + charCode)|0) over a concatenation of subjectId+'\x1f'+predicate per fact edge, in natural array order. Linear O(E_fact), far cheaper than O(N^2).
- Store the fingerprint in a module-level closure var in forces.js (mirrors the causalRadialForce.groups stash pattern). On entry, if the new fingerprint === stored, RETURN the existing state.predicateAffinityLinks reference unchanged (skip the pass). Else compute, then store both the cache and the new fingerprint.
- Returning the same array reference on skip is the observable /verify signal (reference equality across two unchanged-data calls).
- Eager-precompute preserved: still called on every fetchData; only the expensive inner pass is skipped on unchanged data. No flag-gate (honours pd5.6 lock).
- Natural-order (not sorted) hash: the API returns fact edges in stable order across polls, so order changes (rare) only cause a harmless recompute (false-dirty). A true hash collision (false-clean) is negligible; worst case is one stale 5s window until the next real change.
- Reset the stored fingerprint to null is unnecessary; first call always differs from null and computes.
notes:
[2026-05-29] PREMISE_OK: confirmed computePredicateAffinityLinks (forces.js) recomputes unconditionally each fetchData; app.js still calls it post state.data=unified. Every fact edge's source is an entity (index.ts guards), so fact-edge (source,predicate) pairs fully determine signatures -> fingerprinting them alone is sound.

[2026-05-29] APPLIED: forces.js — module-level lastPredicateAffinityFingerprint; computePredicateAffinityLinks now does a linear fingerprint pass over fact edges (count + 32-bit rolling hash of epId(source)+0x1f+predicate) before the O(N^2) work; on fingerprint match returns the cached state.predicateAffinityLinks reference (skips signatures+Jaccard); else computes and stores fingerprint. Eager-precompute preserved (still called every fetch), no flag-gate (honours pd5.6 lock). Per locked Decision 2026-05-29.
[2026-05-29] REVIEWED: /code-review — no correctness fix needed. Finding 1 (false-clean if a fact-edge source flips entity->non-entity with same source+predicate) is UNREACHABLE in Mnemo: fact-edge sources are always entity-UUID nodes (index.ts guards), node-type id-spaces don't cross (entity UUID vs _val_N vs event/memory UUID), and merges re-point edges to a different canonical id (changes fingerprint). Soundness rests on this documented invariant; defense-in-depth (hashing entity set too) considered + rejected as non-actionable hardening for an unreachable case — not filed. Findings 2-5 (cached-ref safety, first-call computes, hash|0 identity token, epId hoist) all clean. Finding 6 (doc comment understates the skip) -> /simplify.
[2026-05-29] SIMPLIFIED: /simplify applied 1 trivial stale-comment fix (Finding 6) — function doc-comment now notes the dirty-check skips the O(N^2) Jaccard on unchanged data. No dup (epId was de-duplicated by hoisting), no dead code, no over-abstraction.
[2026-05-29] VERIFIED: /verify PASS (Playwright, single-evaluate probes to dodge poller). B1 unchanged->same array ref (skip). B2 +synthetic fact edge->different ref (recompute fires); re-skip after. B3 remove synthetic->recompute reproduces exact 23-link baseline; forcing two entities to share predicate sets raised links 23->24 with expected A-B pair, restored to 23 on removal — recompute reflects genuine content change, skip never serves stale content (returns last-computed ref). B4 cache warm at load (23 links).
[2026-05-29] LESSONS_LOGGED: new memory dirty-check-skip-observable-via-ref-equality — make a skip path return the cached object reference so /verify can confirm skip-vs-recompute via === (no debug counter); correctness is free (skip returns last-computed); key the fingerprint on exact inputs, bias toward false-dirty.
close_reason: linear fingerprint dirty-check skips O(N^2) Jaccard on unchanged data; /verify PASS (skip=same ref, change=recompute, content round-trips correctly); eager-precompute + pd5.6 lock preserved

title: articulation ring: radius from N nodes (arc-length spacing)
description:
ywe's ring uses a fixed viewportMin*0.35 radius — independent of articulation count. Visibly too tight at N=31, and would scale wrong for graphs with very different N. Switch to arc-length-per-node: pick a target spacing per slot and derive radius so circumference = N * spacing. Clamp to viewport bounds so neither tiny nor huge N breaks the layout.

# Scope

Decision (locked 2026-05-28): replace ywe's fixed radius with arc-length-derived radius.

Formula in applyForces():
- `const arcPerNode = 60;` (target px per articulation slot — leaves space for entity radius ~6-10px plus collision buffer)
- `const idealRadius = articulationToRing.length * arcPerNode / (2 * Math.PI);`
- `const floor = viewportMin * 0.2;` (small-N guard: ring doesn't shrink absurdly when only a few articulation points exist)
- `const ceil = viewportMin * 0.5;` (large-N guard: ring stays inside the viewport even with 100+ articulation points)
- `const radius = Math.max(floor, Math.min(ceil, idealRadius));`

Everything else from ywe is preserved: id-sort, even angular spacing, alpha 1.0 kick on toggle, drag-end overrides slot, etc.

# Acceptance

- Radius formula matches `clamp(N * 60 / (2π), viewportMin * 0.2, viewportMin * 0.5)`.
- At current data (N=31, viewport ~680px), expected radius ≈ 296px (within the clamp range, no clipping). Probe `Math.hypot(fx - cx, fy - cy)` on all articulation entities → all equal to expected within 0.001.
- Radius is visibly larger than ywe's 238px (≥ 290px probe baseline).
- Probe with synthetic N — e.g. compute the formula for N=5 (would be ~48 → clamped to floor) and N=200 (~1910 → clamped to ceil) and confirm clamp behaviour exists in code. No need to test live with synthetic data; pure-function check.
- ywe regressions hold: angles evenly spaced, deterministic across toggle cycles, non-articulation entities null, toggle OFF releases all.

Depends on nmemo-ywe.
notes:
2026-05-28T16:46:04+01:00: PREMISE_OK: ywe's ring radius hardcoded as viewportMin*0.35. # Scope locked in chat. CLAIMED.
2026-05-28T16:49:33+01:00: VERIFIED. Formula clamp(N*60/2π, viewport*0.2, viewport*0.5) confirmed correct: observed radius 222.5 matches live-computed 222.5 within FP epsilon. Clamp fires correctly at synthetic N=5 (→floor 89) and N=200 (→ceil 222.5). At this viewport (445px short axis, narrower than prior sessions) ideal 296 is clamped to ceiling — narrower windows mean N saturates and the ring scales with viewport instead of N. At 680px viewport (prior sessions) the same N would give un-clamped 296. ywe regressions hold (deterministic + non-articulation null). Observation: literal 'expected radius ≈ 296' acceptance bullet was viewport-dependent and didn't hold this session; lesson filed via bd remember. VERIFIED → LESSONS_LOGGED.

title: articulation hard pin: arrange on central ring + faster settle
description:
Hard pin (nmemo-smr) locks articulation entities at their current x/y — wherever the layout happened to be. That's stable but not visually structured. Arrange them deliberately on a central ring instead so bridges become a visible backbone and clusters drape around them. Also bump the toggle's alpha kick from 0.3 to 1.0 so the layout reorganises in one snappy pass.

# Scope

Decision (locked 2026-05-28): replace smr's 'pin at current position' with 'pin on a deliberate ring'.

When `state.forces.articulationPins` is ON and `state.topology.loaded`, in applyForces():
- Compute center from `simulation.force('center').x()/.y()`.
- Compute radius as `Math.min(svg.clientWidth, svg.clientHeight) * 0.35` (scales with viewport, leaves room for clusters around the ring).
- Filter articulation entities (`_nodeType === 'entity'` + `isArticulationPoint` flag).
- Sort by id (deterministic, stable across reloads — re-toggling produces identical positions).
- Angular step = 2π / N. Each entity i pins at `(cx + R·cos(i·step), cy + R·sin(i·step))`.

Non-articulation entities: clear fx/fy as before (regression-preserve smr).

Toggle OFF: clear fx/fy on all entities (regression-preserve smr).

Drag end on a pinned articulation node: still preserves the drop position via isPinnedArticulationNode predicate (regression-preserve smr). Re-toggling OFF/ON snaps back to the ring.

Settling speed: in bindForcesPanel, bump `sim.alpha(0.3).restart()` → `sim.alpha(1.0).restart()` so any force toggle gets a full re-settle. 0.3 was a gentle nudge; 1.0 is a hard kick that finishes reorganising in one cooldown cycle.

# Acceptance

- With toggle ON + topology loaded, every articulation entity's fx,fy is on the ring: `Math.hypot(fx - cx, fy - cy)` equals R within 0.001 for all.
- Angles (atan2(fy-cy, fx-cx)) when sorted are evenly spaced — consecutive diffs equal to 2π/N within 0.001.
- Ordering is deterministic: toggling OFF then ON twice yields identical fx/fy values per entity.
- With toggle OFF, all entity fx/fy null (smr regression-preserved).
- Drag end on a pinned node sets fx/fy to drop position; predicate-based drag-end logic unchanged.
- Toggle change kicks alpha to 1.0 (probe sim.alpha() immediately after a checkbox change).
- Default OFF.

Depends on nmemo-smr (locks the predicate + applyForces structure this bead builds on).

2026-05-28T16:29:36+01:00: VERIFIED via Playwright. 31 articulation entities on ring of radius 238 (min(viewport)*0.35); distances [237.999986, 238.000003] within FP noise. Angles evenly spaced at 2π/31. Deterministic (OFF→ON yields same positions per id). smr regressions hold: toggle OFF clears all entity fx/fy; non-articulation always null. Checkbox-driven toggle change kicks alpha 0.20→1.0 (real DOM event path). VERIFIED → LESSONS_LOGGED.

title: articulation hard pin: replace soft 5x charge with fx/fy lock
description:
Soft pin (5x charge multiplier, bead nmemo-pd5.4) shipped but proved visually unconvincing — articulation nodes still drift between alpha.restart cycles. Replace it with a hard pin (fx/fy lock) on the same toggle. Single concept, single checkbox.

# Scope

Decision (locked 2026-05-28): replace soft with hard on the existing `articulationPins` toggle. Soft path goes away entirely — kill the charge composition in forces.js applyForces() and the chargeStrength import added by pd5.4.

When `state.forces.articulationPins` is ON and `state.topology.loaded`: in applyForces(), iterate the simulation's nodes; for each entity flagged `isArticulationPoint`, set d.fx = d.x and d.fy = d.y (lock at current position). For entities that are NOT articulation points but have non-null fx/fy from a prior pin (e.g. flag was on, topology changed and they're no longer articulation), clear fx/fy so they release.

When toggle is OFF: sweep simulation nodes and clear fx/fy on any entity (regardless of articulation status) so previously-pinned nodes release. Non-entity nodes are never touched.

Drag handlers in viz/js/canvas/render.js:260 currently `d.fx = null; d.fy = null` on drag end unconditionally. Change to: if the dropped node should be pinned (entity + isArticulationPoint + articulationPins flag on + topology loaded), set d.fx = e.x and d.fy = e.y so the user's new position becomes the new pin. Otherwise clear as before.

# Acceptance

- With toggle ON + topology loaded, every articulation entity has non-null fx/fy equal to its current x/y, and stays put across multiple simulation.alpha(0.3).restart() cycles (probe via simulation.nodes().filter then check fx/fy values).
- With toggle OFF, every entity has null fx/fy; articulation entities behave like every other entity.
- Drag a pinned articulation node to a new position — on release fx/fy is set to the new x/y (not null); the node stays at the dropped position across the next alpha.restart.
- Drag a non-pinned node (regular entity, OR articulation with toggle OFF) — fx/fy null on release as before (no regression).
- Default OFF.
- chargeStrength import and the soft-pin composition block in forces.js are gone.

title: extract default link distance/strength accessors from simulation.js
description:
## Premise (what the finding asserts)

A /simplify pass over nmemo-pd5.2 surfaced that viz/js/canvas/forces.js:113-130 duplicates simulation.js:61-75 link distance/strength accessor tables. 12 lines are kept in sync only by a comment (forces.js:105-107). Subsequent force beads in epic nmemo-pd5 (cluster centroid pd5.3, articulation pd5.4, centrality radial pd5.5, predicate affinity pd5.6, causal radial pd5.7) will each potentially override their own branch of this same table, compounding the drift risk per added force.

## Falsifying test (how to disprove or confirm)

Open viz/js/canvas/simulation.js lines 61-75 and viz/js/canvas/forces.js lines 113-135 side by side. The non-sameAs branches of the .distance() and .strength() accessors are byte-identical between the two files. Confirmed at HEAD on feat/cognitive-platform-v1 (2026-05-28): causalAnchor=80, causal=60, sourceLink=140, mergeCandidate=100, sameAs=120 (default), default=140 appears in both; matching strength branches likewise.

## Result (what the code does today)

simulation.js:61-75 defines the canonical link distance/strength accessor tables inline when constructing d3.forceSimulation(). forces.js:108-136 (applyForces) replaces those accessors wholesale to inject the sameAs fusion override, restating every other branch verbatim. d3's link force replaces the accessor function, not individual cases, so any override must respecify the whole table.

## Impact

Forward-compounding duplication. Each future sibling bead under nmemo-pd5 that wants to override one edge type's distance or strength will either (1) copy the full 12-line table again with its own one-line override (drift risk multiplies by N forces), or (2) override only its branch while inheriting the simulation.js defaults via composition (clean, but requires the extraction this bead proposes). Severity: low per-bead, but multiplicative. Best fixed before pd5.3 lands.

## Scoped fix

- Export `defaultLinkDistance(d)` and `defaultLinkStrength(d)` from simulation.js (named exports alongside the existing chargeStrength/nodeRadius/initSvg exports — same file, no new module).
- simulation.js's d3.forceSimulation() chain calls `.distance(defaultLinkDistance).strength(defaultLinkStrength)` instead of inlining the 6-branch tables.
- forces.js applyForces sameAs override composes against the defaults:
    `.distance(d => (d._edgeType === 'sameAs' && state.forces.sameAsFusion) ? 10 : defaultLinkDistance(d))`
    `.strength(d => (d._edgeType === 'sameAs' && state.forces.sameAsFusion) ? 0.9 : defaultLinkStrength(d))`
- Drop the now-incorrect synchronisation comment at forces.js:105-107 (replace with a one-liner pointing at the imports).

title: causal events as radial decorations (geometric placement)
description:

arranged in a ring around their anchor entity. Kills the porcupine effect.

In forces.js applyForces(), when toggle is ON:
- For each entity, gather its anchored causal events (via causalAnchor edges
  or events.subjectEntityId).
- Compute ring radius:
  `nodeRadius(entity) + 20 + min(eventCount * 2, 30)`
- Place events at evenly-spaced angles:
  `angle = (2π / eventCount) * idx`
  `event.fx = entity.x + radius * cos(angle)`
  `event.fy = entity.y + radius * sin(angle)`
- Recompute on every fetchData() (when membership changes) and on every tick
  (so events follow their anchor as the entity drifts).

Drag handover for events is bead 7b — out of scope here. For now, events stay
locked to their geometric position.

- With toggle ON, every entity's causal events form a clean ring around it
  instead of a porcupine.
- Multiple causal events at different angles — no overlap with each other or
  the entity centre.
- Dragging an entity moves its ring of events with it (events follow because
  fx/fy recomputes per tick from anchor position).
- Default ON.

title: predicate affinity force
description:

feel a weak invisible attraction. Surfaces latent semantic groupings beyond
what AGE traversal shows.

# Scope

too expensive):
- Multiset of predicates from state.data.edges where _edgeType === 'fact' and
  the entity is subject.
- For every pair with non-empty signatures, compute Jaccard similarity.
- For pairs above threshold (start: 0.3), push a synthetic pseudo-link into
  the simulation's link list with strength = 0.01 * similarity, distance 200.
- Pseudo-links carry a flag (`_edgeType: 'predicateAffinity'`) so render.js
  skips them when drawing edges.

into the link force. On toggle OFF, strip pseudo-links and rebind link force.

  nearer than under pure topology (visual inspection on a fixture with shared
  predicates).
- Performance: precompute adds <100ms to fetchData() for current data size
  (~200 entities).
- Pseudo-links do not render as visible edges.
- Toggling off cleanly removes pseudo-links without leaving phantom edges in
  the simulation.
- Default OFF.

title: viz force-layout experimentation framework
description:
A toggleable "Forces" sub-panel in the viz left sidebar that exposes individual
layout forces as on/off experiments, persisted to localStorage. Goal: empirically
find the force combination that produces the most readable graph layout for the
unified viz (currently ~944 nodes / 1075 edges).

# Background

The current single-force simulation in viz/js/canvas/simulation.js produces a
hairball:
- 500 causal events porcupine around 200 entities (each entity becomes a spiked ball).
- 94 source memories pull the graph in as ballast — load-bearing, stays.
- Cluster hulls render *after* a force-blind layout instead of driving placement.
- sameAs links visualise as 120px gaps instead of fusing identity for unresolved pairs.

# Approach

Small, individually-shippable beads add one toggle + one force each. Each force
reads a state.forces.X flag and short-circuits when off. localStorage persists
experimentation state across refresh so tweaks survive sessions.

# Acceptance

When child beads are all closed, a user can open the viz, click into the Forces
panel, and toggle any combination of:
- sameAs fusion
- cluster-centroid pull
- articulation pinning
- centrality radial
- predicate affinity
- causal-event radial placement (with drag handover)

to compare visual outcomes side by side.
close_reason: All 11 children closed. Forces panel exposes all 6 toggles (sameAs fusion, cluster-centroid pull, articulation pinning, centrality radial, predicate affinity, causal-event radial + drag handover), each /verify-confirmed against the live graph. Epic acceptance met.

title: Pattern detection perf: <2s @ 1000 chains (klv.6 graduation gap)
description: The klv.6 benchmark surfaced a perf gap: detectCausalPatterns at 1000 chains measures ~5-6s on Windows + Docker, well over the spec 17:733 budget of <2000ms. The dominant cost is the per-chain normaliseChain() SQL round-trip in services/causal-patterns.ts (O(N) round-trips). Likely fix: batch the entity-type + predicate-category lookups via a single query keyed on the chain's event IDs, then normalise in JS. Captured by the G8 benchmark in src/test/harness/causal-patterns.test.ts (asserted with SOFT_CAP_MS=10000 so the suite stays green while this is open). When closed, tighten the assertion to expect(elapsedMs).toBeLessThan(2000).
notes:
Closed by commits d094caf (perf fix) + 8787ed0 (tighten assertion).

Root cause: detectCausalPatterns had two O(N) round-trip patterns — per-chain normaliseChain() (2 SQL queries each) and per-edge linkEdgesToPattern() (1 UPDATE each). At 1000 chains / 2000 edges that produced ~4000 round-trips and dominated detection cost.

Fix:
1. normaliseChainsBatch(chains[]) fetches edges + events for the union of edge IDs in two queries total, then assembles each chain template in JS. normaliseChain(single) delegates to the batch helper so single-chain callers benefit and the exported API stays identical.
2. linkEdgesToPattern emits one UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...) per cluster keyed on edge_id instead of one UPDATE per edge.

Result (G8 benchmark, 1000 chains, Windows + Docker):
- baseline: ~5-6s
- batched normalise only: ~3.5s
- batched normalise + link: ~120-150ms (well under 2000ms spec)

G8 assertion tightened from SOFT_CAP_MS=10000 to expect(elapsedMs).toBeLessThan(SPEC_TARGET_MS=2000). G1-G7 all green (64/64). G8 detect benchmark now asserts the spec directly — regression will fail the test.

title: Startup-validation invariants — fail-fast for Qdrant dim, ml-services, transport, port collisions
description:
# Startup-validation invariants — fail-fast cross-checks for Qdrant dim, ml-services reach, transport health, port collisions

## Premise (cross-cutting from Review #14)

Config values that span code + .env + migrations drift silently. Every boundary should cross-check its config at startup; a drifted value should be fatal, not silently-running. This bead stands up a `validateStartup()` integration point with validators for the four current boundaries; per-boundary fix beads remain open and slot into the same integration point.

## Cycle evidence (T11 — silent drift)

| Bead | Silent drift |
|---|---|
| `.121` (P2) | `qdrant.ensureCollections` is dead AND doesn't validate Qdrant collection dimension against `config.EMBED_DIMENSIONS`. Mismatch silently writes garbage vectors |
| `.123 .126` (P1/P2) | MCP probe spawns the wrong server file + doesn't pass env. Drift between probe and production spawn |
| `.127` (P2) | Write-tool serialization in Pi only; one env-var flip silently reactivates the unguarded MCP write path |
| `.112` (P1) | Port collisions: code defaults at 3001 (platform + bridge), Makefile/`.env` documented at 3099; `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:454` BRIDGE_URL default reads `http://localhost:3001` (collides) instead of 3099 |

Every one of these would be caught by a fail-fast startup check.

## Falsifying test

Edit `migrations/004_qdrant_collections.sql` to change `EMBED_DIMENSIONS` to a different value than what `qdrant` already has provisioned. Restart the platform. Today: starts OK; subsequent writes corrupt the vector store silently. After this bead: startup fails with `[startup] Qdrant collection MEMORIES dim mismatch: provisioned 768, expected 1024`; `process.exit(1)`.

## Result (what the code does today)

- No `validateStartup()` integration point. `src/index.ts` builds the Hono app, registers routes, and calls `serve()` directly.
- Each boundary has its own ad-hoc startup behaviour: `ensureCollections` exists but is dead (`.121`); `ml.health` exists but is never called (R12/F2); Pi bridge `/health` is checked only by `ml-services/PiBridgeProvider.__init__`; MCP transport `/api/mcp-health` is only checked when an operator hits the endpoint manually.
- Port collisions reproduce reliably on a clean clone (`.112` falsifying test).

## Impact

- Startup runs against misconfigured infrastructure. The platform reports "Platform listening on :3001" while writes are silently corrupted (Qdrant dim) or silently routed to the wrong transport.
- Each per-boundary fix (`.121 .126 .127 .112`) closes its own instance, but the structural pattern — *boundaries don't cross-check at startup* — recurs the next time a new boundary lands.
- T11 is one of the harder themes to catch in code review; the right place to enforce these invariants is at startup, not in PR review.

## Scoped fix

### Step 1 — Integration point

Create `src/services/startup-validation.ts`:

```ts
export interface ValidatorResult {
  name: string;
  ok: boolean;
  detail?: string;
  durationMs: number;
}

export async function validateStartup(): Promise<ValidatorResult[]> {
  const results: ValidatorResult[] = [];
  for (const v of VALIDATORS) {
    results.push(await runWithTimeout(v, 5_000));
  }
  return results;
}
```

Each validator is a `{ name, run: () => Promise<ValidatorResult> }`. Total startup budget ≤30s (six validators × 5s each).

### Step 2 — Initial validators

1. **Qdrant collection dim.** Call `qdrant.getCollections()`; for each in `COLLECTIONS`, fetch info; assert `vectors.size === config.EMBED_DIMENSIONS`. Calls `ensureCollections` first to create missing ones (now wired). Closes `.121`'s structural concern.
2. **ml-services reach.** Call `ml.health()`. Assert 200 with expected shape. Wires up R12/F2's previously-dead export.
3. **Transport health.** Inspect `process.env.LLM_PROVIDER`:
   - `pi` (default in `ml-services/.env`): GET `http://localhost:${PI_BRIDGE_PORT}/health`, assert 200.
   - `claude`: call `checkGraphMcpHealth()` (post-`.123` rename), assert `ok: true`, assert `tools.length === GRAPH_TOOLS.length`.
   - `zai`: skip (no host transport process; provider runs in ml-services).
4. **Port-collision check.** Read `PORT` and `PI_BRIDGE_PORT` from env; if equal, fail with a message naming both. Closes `.112`'s structural concern.

### Step 3 — Wire into startup

In `src/index.ts`, before `serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port })`:

```ts
const results = await validateStartup();
const failed = results.filter(r => !r.ok);
if (failed.length > 0) {
  console.error('[startup] Validation failures:');
  for (const r of failed) {
    console.error(`  - ${r.name}: ${r.detail ?? 'failed'} (${r.durationMs}ms)`);
  }
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('[startup] All validators passed');
```

### Step 4 — Tests

New file `src/test/harness/startup-validation.test.ts`. Mock each boundary; for each validator, assert:
- Healthy boundary → `ok: true`.
- Drifted dim / missing host / port collision / wrong transport → `ok: false` with a useful `detail` string.
- Timeout → `ok: false` with `detail` containing 'timeout'.
- Aggregate function calls all validators (no short-circuit on failure — every validator reports).

### Scope guards

- No `STRICT_STARTUP=true|false` env opt-out (option b). Strict-only — adding a second config layer that can itself drift recreates the problem this bead is fixing.
- No composed-into-`/health`-only (option c). `/health` reports current state; startup gates initial state. Both matter; this bead is the startup gate. `.111` (the `/health` composer) is the runtime check.
- Per-boundary fix beads (`.121 .126 .127 .112`) remain open. C3 provides the integration point; each per-boundary bead lands its specific validation logic. The integration point is mockable so each per-boundary bead can ship + test independently.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `src/services/startup-validation.ts` exists with `validateStartup()` + four initial validators.
- [ ] `src/index.ts` calls `validateStartup()` before `serve()`; on failure logs all failures and `process.exit(1)`.
- [ ] All four validators have unit-level tests (mocked boundary) covering healthy, drifted, timeout cases.
- [ ] Falsifying test reproduces: modifying Qdrant dim out of band → startup fails with a clear message.
- [ ] Manual: `make dev-all` startup time increases by ≤30s; on a clean clone with all services up, all validators pass.
- [ ] `ensureCollections` (dead per `.121`) is wired up via the Qdrant validator; close `.121`'s "is dead" concern (dim-validation concern moves into the Qdrant validator).

## Themes

T11 (silent drift) — root-cause infrastructure for the pattern.

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (a) — startup validator with strict fail-fast behaviour. Rejected alternatives:

- (b) Soft-fail mode behind `STRICT_STARTUP` env. Adding an env-var escape hatch recreates the silent-drift problem the bead is fixing. Two startup behaviours mean operators can't predict which is live; "did I forget to set STRICT_STARTUP?" becomes a new failure mode.
- (c) Compose into `/health` only, no startup gate. `/health` reports runtime state; startup-time misconfig writes garbage immediately and operators see a passing `/health` line they wrote yesterday. Startup gate is the right shape for *initial* state; `/health` (already covered by `.111`) is the right shape for *current* state.
- (d) Punt to per-boundary beads. Each per-boundary fix closes its own instance but the structural pattern recurs next boundary.

## Discovered from

Review #14 cross-feature synthesis (`docs/architecture/truth-graph/31-review-cycle-synthesis.md` §2.6 + §4 C3).
notes: [2026-05-26] APPLIED+VERIFIED+CLOSED: startup-validation.ts created with 4 validators (qdrant_dim, ml_services, transport, ports). Wired into index.ts VITEST guard. 10 tests covering wrapper behaviour, aggregator no-short-circuit, per-validator units. Replaces bare ensureCollections() call from .121 — both beads compose cleanly.

title: (DOC) Compute-trigger registry (doc 32) — enumerate every graph compute + trigger condition
description:
# Compute-trigger registry — doc 32 enumerating every graph compute and its trigger contract

## Premise (cross-cutting from Review #14)

Every graph compute (graph_stats, topology, clustering, drift, cross_cluster, gardener, reconciliation, reasoning_patrol, pattern_detection, decay) should have a documented trigger condition: post-ingest hook, DB-state-change reactive, scheduled, threshold-driven, or explicitly manual. Today no single doc lists them; the trigger model is ad-hoc per-feature and inconsistent. This bead creates the registry doc; the actual missing triggers are filed at P1 elsewhere.

## Cycle evidence (T12 — missing auto-triggers)

| Compute | Current trigger | Bead |
|---|---|---|
| Reconciliation | Manual-only (`/api/reconcile`) | `.61` P1 |
| Reasoning patrol | Manual-only | `.71` P1 |
| Pattern detection + graph-stats | Coupled to reasoning-patrol cadence (wrong cadence) | `.72` P1 |
| Topology / clustering / drift | All three manual-only despite doc 21 §10 W6 promising patrol-time drift | `.84` P1 |
| Cross-cluster generator | No drift-event refresh hook | `.85` P3 |

Every compute that auto-triggers (gardener, decay, graph_stats counter) does so via the patrol-cascade, which has accumulated drive-by hooks. No coherent model.

## Falsifying test

A reviewer of a new graph-compute feature can point at one doc that lists every existing compute and its trigger condition, and the new feature's PR is required to add its row to that doc.

## Result (what the docs say today)

- No registry doc exists.
- Trigger conditions are documented (when at all) in the feature's own arch doc: doc 21 §10 W6 mentions patrol-time drift; doc 10 hints at reasoning patrol cadence; doc 25 describes cross-cluster refresh. Each in its own vocabulary, with no comparison table.
- New computes have no place to register; reviewers can't cross-check.

## Impact

- Every compute landed with manual-only triggers as MVP. The "we'll wire the trigger in Phase 2" promise is unfulfilled across the cycle.
- State accumulates without reconciliation (`.61` symptom: `merge_candidates` pile up).
- Patrol cascade is becoming a kitchen sink (`.72` symptom: pattern-detection and graph-stats hitched to reasoning-patrol cadence, which is the wrong cadence for both).
- Operators don't know which compute requires manual intervention vs. which fires automatically; the answer requires reading the source.

## Scoped fix

### Step 1 — Create doc 32

New file `docs/architecture/truth-graph/32-compute-trigger-registry.md`. Sections:

1. **Overview.** Every graph compute has a documented trigger. No compute ships without a row here. New PRs that add a compute must add a row in the same PR.
2. **Registry table.** Columns: compute name, service file (`src/services/...`), trigger condition (post-ingest / DB-reactive / scheduled / threshold / manual), cadence or threshold value, `*_runs` table name (or "n/a"), source of trigger code (the call site that registers the trigger).
3. **Initial rows.** One per known compute. For computes whose auto-trigger is still missing, the trigger column lists `MANUAL ONLY — see <bead-id>` with a pointer at the P1 bead that will land the trigger.
4. **Trigger taxonomy.** A short glossary distinguishing the five trigger types — what each is appropriate for and an example.
5. **Cross-references.** Points at C4 (feature integration checklist) which enforces the registry-update rule.

Initial rows (incomplete TODO list — fill during writing):

- `graph_stats` — patrol-cascade hook in `pipeline.ts:incrementGraphStatsCount` — threshold-driven, every N patrols. Coupling with reasoning patrol is a known issue, see `.72`.
- `entity_topology` — `MANUAL ONLY — see .84`.
- `hdbscan_clustering` — `MANUAL ONLY — see .84`.
- `drift_detection` — `MANUAL ONLY — see .84`.
- `cross_cluster_generator` — post-compute fire-and-forget hooks (topology + clustering + drift → cross-cluster); drift hook missing, see `.85`.
- `gardener` — patrol-cascade hook; auto-trigger writes don't reach `gardening_reports`, see `.67`.
- `reconciliation_agent` — `MANUAL ONLY — see .61`.
- `reasoning_patrol` — `MANUAL ONLY — see .71`.
- `pattern_detection` — hitched to reasoning patrol cadence; should be DB-reactive, see `.72`.
- `decay` — `MANUAL ONLY via /api/decay` (intentional? confirm during writing).

### Step 2 — Update reading order

`docs/architecture/truth-graph/README.md` — add doc 32 to the reading order after doc 31 (Review #14 synthesis).

### Step 3 — Cross-references in existing docs

Each per-feature arch doc that describes a compute trigger should reference doc 32 as the canonical registry. Minimal touch — one line in doc 21 §10, doc 10, doc 25.

### Scope guards

- C2 does NOT implement any missing triggers. Those are filed at P1 already (`.61 .71 .72 .84 .85`).
- C2 does NOT create a code-side registry (option b in review). TS source-of-truth would couple every trigger registration through one module; saves nothing the doc doesn't catch.
- C2 does NOT add a YAML/JSON machine-readable manifest (option c). Single markdown doc; CI lint is a follow-up if drift becomes a problem.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/architecture/truth-graph/32-compute-trigger-registry.md` exists with all five sections.
- [ ] Registry table includes one row per known compute (target ≥10 rows from the initial list above).
- [ ] Every compute whose auto-trigger is still TODO has a `MANUAL ONLY — see <bead>` row pointing at the implementing bead.
- [ ] `README.md` reading order includes doc 32 after doc 31.
- [ ] At least one per-feature arch doc (e.g. doc 21 §10) cross-references doc 32 as the canonical trigger registry.
- [ ] As the P1 trigger beads (`.61 .71 .72 .84`) close, their rows in doc 32 update from `MANUAL ONLY — see <bead>` to the real trigger condition. (Tracking only — doc 32 closes when initial rows are populated; subsequent edits land with each P1 bead.)

## Themes

T12 (missing auto-triggers) — root-cause infrastructure for the pattern.

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (a) — doc 32 lands first with TODO rows pointing at the P1 trigger beads. Rejected alternatives:

- (b) Code-side registry (TS module). Would couple every trigger through one module; reshaping the four P1 beads to fit it slows them down for negligible benefit.
- (c) Doc + machine-readable manifest + CI lint. More moving parts; YAML/JSON alongside markdown is novel for this repo; doc 32 alone suffices until proven otherwise.
- (d) Punt — let the P1 beads land independently. Misses the cross-cutting cure; next compute repeats the pattern.
- (a) but holding doc 32 until all five trigger beads land. Would hold doc 32 hostage to four P1 beads; better to land doc 32 first and evolve TODO rows into real entries as each bead closes.

## Discovered from

Review #14 cross-feature synthesis (`docs/architecture/truth-graph/31-review-cycle-synthesis.md` §2.7 + §3 G4 + §4 C2).
notes: [2026-05-26] APPLIED+CLOSED: doc 32 created (5 sections, 10-row registry, 5-type taxonomy). README + doc 21 §10 cross-references added. Tracking rows for MANUAL ONLY computes name .61/.71/.72/.84/.85 — those beads update doc 32 when they land.

title: Enum-vocabulary single source of truth — TS constants + canary migration .60 (resolve_candidate/merge_candidates.resolution)
description:
# Enum-vocabulary single source of truth — TS constants + hand-synced schema CHECK; canary migration: `resolve_candidate` / `merge_candidates.resolution` (.60)

## Premise (cross-cutting from Review #14)

Enum vocabularies (CHECK constraint values, tool enums, agent prompt strings, viz strings, HTTP API values) are duplicated across schema, code, and prompts with no single source of truth. Each layer validates locally; cross-layer messages get rejected silently. This bead stands up the infrastructure (a TS module of `as const` tuples) and migrates one instance as the canary.

## Cycle evidence (T7 — naming mismatch)

| Bead | Disagreement |
|---|---|
| `.60` (P1) | `resolve_candidate` tool sends `'same_as'`; `merge_candidates.resolution` CHECK admits a different token set. Same-as resolutions silently fail to close candidates |
| `.27` (P3) | doc 03 §5.2 uses one cascading-invalidation vocabulary; code uses another |
| `.28` (P3) | doc 03 §5.3 uses `'inferred'/'explicit'`; code uses `'llm_extraction'/…` |
| `.39` (P2) | schema admits `chain_conflict` contradiction type; no tool enum exposes it for insertion |
| `.69` (P3) | missing CHECK constraints on `gardening_reports.trigger_type` and `merge_candidates.candidate_source` — enums implicit in code, not enforced in schema |

All five share the same root cause: no single declaration of the enum vocabulary that every consumer reads.

## Falsifying test

Editing the canonical enum constant in `src/services/enums.ts` produces a one-line diff in the importing tool schema, agent prompt, and viz string. The matching migration CHECK constraint requires a hand edit, with a comment in the migration directing the reader to the canonical constant. Forgetting the migration edit fails a small CI lint script.

## Result (what the code does today)

- No `src/services/enums.ts` (or equivalent SSOT module) exists.
- Each layer declares its own copy: tool schemas inline `enum: ['same_as', ...]` in `causal-agent.ts`; migrations inline CHECK constraints in `*.sql`; agent prompts hard-code strings; viz panels hard-code strings.
- `.60` is the active P1: `resolve_candidate` tool input enum and `merge_candidates.resolution` CHECK constraint disagree on the token set for "same as" resolutions, silently dropping the resolution.

## Impact

- Cross-layer messages fail without a clear error path. `.60`'s `'same_as'` resolution writes the row, then the agent's subsequent read sees the candidate still open. Operators see no error; only the symptom (candidates pile up).
- Doc-vs-code drift compounds: every new enum addition is three or four edits (schema + tool + prompt + viz), one of which is forgotten.
- New contributors can't find the canonical list; copy-paste from one site produces a fourth divergent copy.

## Scoped fix

### Step 1 — Infrastructure

Create `src/services/enums.ts` (location open — could also be `src/shared/enums.ts`). Each enum exported as a `readonly` tuple plus a type alias:

```ts
export const RESOLUTION_VALUES = ['same_as', 'distinct', 'merge', 'dismissed'] as const;
export type ResolutionValue = typeof RESOLUTION_VALUES[number];
```

Initial enums to add (others migrate as their beads land):

- `RESOLUTION_VALUES` (for `merge_candidates.resolution`)
- — and only this one in the canary scope. The other instances (`.27 .28 .39 .69`) migrate in their own beads after C1 lands.

### Step 2 — Canary migration (.60's fix)

Migrate `resolve_candidate` tool + `merge_candidates.resolution` CHECK to read from `RESOLUTION_VALUES`:

1. Tool schema in `src/services/causal-agent.ts` — replace the inline `enum: [...]` with one referencing `RESOLUTION_VALUES`.
2. The migration that owns `merge_candidates.resolution` CHECK — update the value set to match `RESOLUTION_VALUES` (or add a new migration if the existing one's already shipped to production). Add an inline comment: `-- keep in sync with src/services/enums.ts:RESOLUTION_VALUES`.
3. Any agent prompt or viz string that hard-codes a resolution value — import the constant or reference it by name.
4. `.60`'s test (or a new one) verifies that emitting any value in `RESOLUTION_VALUES` from `resolve_candidate` results in the candidate row closing.

### Step 3 — Optional follow-up (not in this bead)

A small lint script in `scripts/` that diff-checks each enum constant in `enums.ts` against the matching migration CHECK. Filed as a follow-up bead if value warrants; not part of C1's acceptance.

### Scope guards

- C1 does NOT migrate `.27 .28 .39 .69`. Those beads stay open and migrate independently after C1's infrastructure lands.
- C1 does NOT introduce code generation (option (b) from review). TS is the source of truth; migrations hand-sync with a comment.
- C1 does NOT introduce a build step or codegen artefact in source tree.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `src/services/enums.ts` exists with at least `RESOLUTION_VALUES` exported as a `readonly` tuple + type alias.
- [ ] `resolve_candidate` tool input schema reads enum values from `RESOLUTION_VALUES` (no inline string literals).
- [ ] `merge_candidates.resolution` CHECK constraint admits exactly the values in `RESOLUTION_VALUES`, with a comment pointing at the constant.
- [ ] `.60`'s scenario passes: a `same_as` resolution emitted by the agent closes the candidate row (verified by test + manual run).
- [ ] Close `.60` when C1 closes (subsumed by canary scope).
- [ ] Other T7 instance beads (`.27 .28 .39 .69`) remain open; each will migrate to use `enums.ts` when its own work lands.

## Themes

T7 (naming mismatch) — root-cause infrastructure for the cross-feature pattern.

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (a) — TS-side `as const` tuple + hand-synced CHECK with sync comment; canary scope is `.60`'s fix (P1). Rejected alternatives:

- (b) Schema-first with code generation. No codegen precedent in this codebase; adds build complexity; codegen artefacts in source tree create churn.

- (a) without canary — stand up infrastructure only, no canary use. Less compelling; harder to validate the pattern without a real consumer; .60 stays open longer.

title: Write-tool serialization enforced only in pi-agent-bridge — move into handleToolCall, both transports inherit
description:
# Write-tool serialization enforced only in `pi-agent-bridge.ts` — MCP transport runs writes concurrently; move serialization into `handleToolCall`

## Premise

The 17 GRAPH_TOOLS that mutate the database must be serialized within any one transport process. Today this is enforced in the Pi bridge but not in the MCP transport. The serialization belongs in the shared dispatcher (`handleToolCall`) so both transports get it automatically.

## Falsifying test

If Claude Code (LLM_PROVIDER=claude) emits two `tool_use` blocks in one message — e.g. `create_fact` for entity A followed by `create_fact` for entity B — the MCP server should run them in order. Today it dispatches them concurrently via `setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, ...)`; the underlying writes can race against each other in the DB.

## Result (what the code does today)

- `src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:85-91` defines a `WRITE_TOOLS` set of 17 mutating tools:
  - `create_causal_edge, create_fact, resolve_entity, link_entity_to_memory, add_entity_alias, update_entity_summary, create_same_as_link, execute_merge, resolve_candidate, expire_fact, invalidate_fact, restore_fact, update_fact_confidence, expire_causal_edge, revise_causal_edge, resolve_contradiction, save_reasoning_report`.
- `src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:70` sets `executionMode: isWriteTool(toolDef.name) ? 'sequential' : 'parallel'` — Pi's framework respects per-tool serialization.
- `src/services/graph-mcp.ts` has no equivalent. `setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, ...)` accepts concurrent JSON-RPC `tools/call` messages and dispatches them; no mutex on writes.
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:handleToolCall` is the shared dispatcher used by both transports; it is unguarded.

Anthropic's tool_use protocol allows the assistant to emit multiple `tool_use` blocks in one message. Claude Sonnet 4+ does this commonly for read tools and occasionally for writes. When Claude Code dispatches that batch to the MCP server, the handlers run concurrently in Node.js.

## Impact

- T11 (silent drift): two transports with the same surface but different concurrency contracts. If `LLM_PROVIDER` toggles from `pi` (current default in `ml-services/.env`) back to `claude` (code default in `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:610`), the dormant bug becomes live with no log signal.
- T13 (half-built): Pi bridge was introduced as a replacement and the serialization was added there; the original MCP transport never got the equivalent fix.
- Concrete races on the same actor process: two `create_fact` calls can race on entity_id resolution; `execute_merge` + `expire_fact` on the same entity can interleave; `create_causal_edge` writes ordering with respect to its referenced `causal_events` is no longer guaranteed.

## Scoped fix

Move serialization into `handleToolCall` in `src/services/causal-agent.ts`. Single mechanism, single source of truth, both transports inherit it.

### Steps

1. **Add a module-scoped write set + queue** at the top of `src/services/causal-agent.ts` near the GRAPH_TOOLS definition:

   ```ts
   // Tools that mutate the graph. Serialised in handleToolCall — the dispatcher
   // is the single source of truth for write ordering across MCP and Pi transports.
   const WRITE_TOOLS = new Set<string>([
     'create_causal_edge', 'create_fact', 'resolve_entity', 'link_entity_to_memory',
     'add_entity_alias', 'update_entity_summary', 'create_same_as_link', 'execute_merge',
     'resolve_candidate', 'expire_fact', 'invalidate_fact', 'restore_fact',
     'update_fact_confidence', 'expire_causal_edge', 'revise_causal_edge',
     'resolve_contradiction', 'save_reasoning_report',
   ]);

   let writeQueue: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();
   ```

2. **Gate mutating calls in `handleToolCall`** (the outer wrapper at line 1022):

   ```ts
   export async function handleToolCall(toolName, toolInput, context) {
     // ...existing context resolution...

     if (WRITE_TOOLS.has(toolName)) {
       // Chain on the previous write. catch() so a prior failure doesn't poison
       // the queue — every write must run regardless of upstream outcome.
       const prev = writeQueue.catch(() => undefined);
       const next = prev.then(() => _handleToolCallInner(toolName, toolInput, resolved));
       writeQueue = next;
       return next;
     }
     return _handleToolCallInner(toolName, toolInput, resolved);
   }
   ```

   Reads run freely; writes serialize globally per process. Queue fails open (one failed write does not block the next).

3. **Drop the duplicate set in pi-agent-bridge**:
   - Delete `WRITE_TOOLS` constant (lines 85-91), `isWriteTool` helper (lines 93-95).
   - Change line 70 from `executionMode: isWriteTool(toolDef.name) ? 'sequential' : 'parallel'` to `executionMode: 'parallel'`.

4. **Document the contract** — add a "Write-tool serialization" subsection to doc 30 (Review #13/F3 / nmemo-2yv.125) describing the dispatcher-level queue and that both transports rely on it. Cross-link this bead.

### Scope guards

- Per-actor scoping (one queue per `MNEMO_AGENT_ACTOR`) explicitly rejected — see Decision section. Use a single per-process queue.
- DB-level transactional / row-locking concerns are out of scope. This bead is in-process serialization for the agentic-loop case only.
- The `mutates: boolean` per-tool flag refactor (option d in the review) is rejected — set in `causal-agent.ts` is the simpler shape.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `src/services/causal-agent.ts` has a module-scoped `WRITE_TOOLS` set and `writeQueue` variable; `handleToolCall` awaits the queue for any tool in the set.
- [ ] `rg "WRITE_TOOLS|isWriteTool" src` returns only the `causal-agent.ts` occurrences — no Pi-bridge duplicate.
- [ ] `src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:70` uses unconditional `executionMode: 'parallel'`; no `isWriteTool` import.
- [ ] One new test under `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts` (or `pi-agent-bridge.test.ts`): dispatch two `create_fact` calls concurrently via `Promise.all([handleToolCall(...), handleToolCall(...)])`, assert the inner timestamps show ordering (or assert via an instrumentation hook that the second call started after the first finished).
- [ ] Another new test: a write that throws does not block the subsequent write — `Promise.all([handleToolCall(failing-write), handleToolCall(succeeding-write)])` — the second must complete with a normal result.
- [ ] Read tools remain parallel — `Promise.all` of two reads completes without forced ordering.
- [ ] Doc 30 (when written under .125) includes the write-serialization subsection.

## Themes

T11 (silent transport drift), T13 (half-built — Pi got the fix, MCP didn't).

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (a) — move serialization into `handleToolCall` with a hand-maintained `WRITE_TOOLS` set; global per-process queue; queue fails open; Pi bridge's `executionMode: 'sequential'` dropped.

Rejected alternatives:

- (b) Add serialization wrapper in `graph-mcp.ts` mirroring Pi. Two sources of truth for the write-tool list — the divergence-prone state this bead exists to fix.
- (c) Add `mutates: boolean` to `ToolDefinition`. Cleaner in theory but moves the maintenance burden from one set into 17 per-tool flags; no easier to scan, no easier to grep ("which tools mutate the graph?"). Still requires duplicate mechanism (Pi `executionMode` + graph-mcp queue).
- (d) `mutates: boolean` + dispatcher serialization combined. Same per-tool-flag downside; larger diff for no functional gain over (a).
- Per-actor queue. Two MCP-spawned subprocesses (one per agent invocation) are already isolated at the process level. Pi bridge serves one actor per `/run` call; concurrent invocations are rare and the cost of cross-actor serialization is negligible. Per-actor adds complexity for no measurable benefit.
- Per-actor queue with reader-writer semantics. Significantly more code; no current evidence that read parallelism with concurrent write is a hot path.
- Keep Pi's `executionMode: 'sequential'` as defense-in-depth. Two mechanisms doing the same job hides which one is actually in effect; future readers can't tell. Single-mechanism story is honest.
- Queue fails closed (one failure blocks subsequent writes). Operationally unacceptable — would convert a transient write failure into a denial-of-service on the rest of the patrol.
notes: [2026-05-26] APPLIED+VERIFIED+CLOSED: WRITE_TOOLS+writeQueue centralised in causal-agent.ts; pi-agent-bridge dedup removed; 3 new tests in causal-mcp.test.ts (all 12 pass, plus 20/20 in pi-agent-bridge.test.ts). Doc 30 update DEFERRED — depends on .125 (canonical MCP transport doc) which hasn't shipped yet.

title: /api/mcp-health doesn't pass env and only does tools/list — add shared env builder + get_graph_topology round-trip
description:
# `/api/mcp-health` doesn't pass env to the spawned MCP subprocess and only exercises `tools/list` — too shallow to detect production-path startup failures

## Premise

The MCP health probe must spawn the production MCP server **with the same env contract** that production uses, and must exercise at least one DB-touching tool call so that "green" actually means "the agent can do useful work".

## Falsifying test

If `getMcpConfigPath` drops or mistypes a required env var (e.g. removes `DATABASE_URL` from the env allowlist on `src/services/causal-agent.ts:2001`), production agents fail to start the MCP server, but `/api/mcp-health` still returns 200 OK. Likewise, if the DB is unreachable, `tools/list` still returns 38 entries — the probe passes.

## Result (what the code does today)

Spawn block at `src/services/causal-agent.ts:2294-2299`:

```ts
const proc = spawn('npx', ['tsx', 'src/services/causal-mcp.ts'], {
  cwd: platformRoot,
  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  shell: process.platform === 'win32',
});
```

- No `env:` option. The subprocess inherits the platform process's full `process.env` — works incidentally in dev where `dotenv` has loaded everything.
- Production spawn path is structurally different: `getMcpConfigPath` (lines 2000-2015) assembles an explicit env dict and writes it into `mcpServers.mnemo-graph.env`. Claude Code does NOT inherit env to MCP children — only the explicit `env` block from the config is passed in.
- The probe therefore tests a strictly easier startup contract than production.
- The probe sends `initialize` (line 2364-2375) then `tools/list` (line 2328-2334). Neither touches Postgres, Qdrant, or Ollama. A server that starts cleanly but cannot reach the DB returns green.

## Impact

- Drift between probe-env and production-env goes undetected. An env-list edit in `getMcpConfigPath` that breaks production agents passes `/api/mcp-health`.
- Connectivity outages (Postgres down, MCP server can't reach :5433) don't surface on `/api/mcp-health` — endpoint reports OK while every real tool call would fail.
- Themes: T9 (observability gap), T11 (silent drift).

## Scoped fix

Two parts, both inside `src/services/causal-agent.ts`. Lands after Review #13/F1 retargets the spawn to `graph-mcp.ts` and renames the function.

### Part A — shared env builder

Extract env assembly out of `getMcpConfigPath` into a helper:

```ts
export function getMcpEnv(actor: Actor): Record<string, string> {
  const platformRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');
  const envFile = dotenv.config({ path: path.resolve(platformRoot, '.env') });
  const env: Record<string, string> = { MNEMO_AGENT_ACTOR: actor };
  for (const key of ['DATABASE_URL', 'QDRANT_URL', 'ML_SERVICES_URL', 'EMBED_MODEL', 'NODE_ENV']) {
    const val = process.env[key] || envFile.parsed?.[key];
    if (val) env[key] = val;
  }
  return env;
}
```

`getMcpConfigPath` calls `getMcpEnv(actor)` instead of inlining the loop. `checkGraphMcpHealth` (post-F1 name) calls `getMcpEnv('graph_agent')` and passes the result to `spawn(..., { env })`. Single source of truth — env drift on either side becomes a compile-time / lint-time signal.

### Part B — deeper probe

After `tools/list` succeeds (id=2), send a `tools/call` for `get_graph_topology`:

```ts
const callReq = JSON.stringify({
  jsonrpc: '2.0',
  id: 3,
  method: 'tools/call',
  params: { name: 'get_graph_topology', arguments: {} },
});
proc.stdin.write(callReq + '\n');
```

Wait for the id=3 response. Treat any structured response (success or an error envelope from the tool itself) as proof the MCP→DB path works. Treat a transport-level failure (connection refused, JSON parse error, timeout) as failure.

`get_graph_topology` chosen because:
- Hits Postgres only (no Ollama/Qdrant). `/api/mcp-health` is the **MCP transport** probe — keep it narrow and fast.
- Read-only — no side effects per probe.
- Already exists in `GRAPH_TOOLS`; no new tool needed.
- Ollama/Qdrant outages should surface via their own probes (`qdrant.checkQdrantHealth`, ML service `/health`).

Update the `McpHealthResult` shape to include the new step:

```ts
interface McpHealthResult {
  ok: boolean;
  tools?: string[];
  topologyOk?: boolean;
  error?: string;
  durationMs: number;
}
```

`ok` is true only if both `tools/list` AND the `get_graph_topology` round-trip succeed.

Scope guards:
- Stderr capture on success path (Review #13/F8) — separate bead.
- Replacing the entire probe strategy (Review #13's option (d) — in-process probe) — rejected upstream.
- `checkGraphMcpHealth` rename + script-path resolver — Review #13/F1's bead.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `getMcpEnv(actor)` exported from `src/services/causal-agent.ts`; `getMcpConfigPath` consumes it; the env-allowlist loop appears in exactly one place (`rg "DATABASE_URL.*QDRANT_URL.*ML_SERVICES_URL" src` returns one hit).
- [ ] `checkGraphMcpHealth` (post-F1) passes `env: getMcpEnv('graph_agent')` to `spawn`.
- [ ] Probe issues a `tools/call get_graph_topology {}` after `tools/list`; `ok: true` requires both succeed.
- [ ] `McpHealthResult` includes `topologyOk` (or equivalent) so consumers can tell which leg failed.
- [ ] Test added under `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts` that mocks the subprocess at the JSON-RPC level and verifies the probe sends all three messages (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`) and that an error response on the topology call flips `ok` to false.
- [ ] Manual: hit `GET /api/mcp-health` against a dev server with Postgres running → 200, `ok: true`, `topologyOk: true`. Stop Postgres → 503, `ok: false`, `topologyOk: false` or error.

## Themes

T9 (observability gap), T11 (silent drift between probe and production env contracts).

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (b)+(c) merged — shared env builder plus a `get_graph_topology` round-trip after `tools/list`. Rejected alternatives:

- (a) Pass env only. Closes the env-drift hole but leaves the probe testing only the easy startup path; DB outages still undetected.
- (c) alone (env extraction without deeper probe). Same problem.
- (d) Split into shallow and deep endpoints. Two endpoints means two contracts and two probe consumers to coordinate; the existing endpoint already implies a useful health signal — better to make `/api/mcp-health` honest than to bifurcate.
- `search_memories` as the deeper-probe tool. Pulls Ollama + Qdrant + Postgres into the probe; broader signal but `/api/mcp-health` is meant to be the MCP transport probe, not a system-wide aggregator. Per-system probes (Qdrant, Ollama, ML) belong in their own endpoints.
notes: [2026-05-26] APPLIED+VERIFIED+CLOSED: Part A getMcpEnv(actor) extracted, single env-allowlist grep hit confirmed. Part B id=3 tools/call get_graph_topology with topologyOk gating ok=true. Latent prod bug fixed: stdout re-iteration caused duplicate sends under 3-stage flow (added toolsListSent/topologyCallSent guards). 7 new tests via vi.mock('node:child_process') in separate test file. JSON-RPC error vs tool-level error semantics distinguished.

title: (DOC) Canonical MCP transport doc (30) + fix count/file-name drift in docs 04/07/11
description:
# Doc gap + count/file-name drift for the MCP transport layer — create canonical doc 30, fix references in docs 04/07/11

## Premise

There is no canonical architecture doc for the MCP transport that backs the agent flows when `LLM_PROVIDER=claude` (or `LLM_PROVIDER` is unset — that is the code default in `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:610`). References to MCP are scattered across three numbered docs, and each one carries a different incorrect tool count and (in two cases) the wrong server file name.

## Falsifying test

A new developer reading the truth-graph architecture docs cannot find any single doc that:

- Explains the two transports (MCP servers vs Pi bridge), when each is live, and the env-var switch (`LLM_PROVIDER`).
- States the parity contract: both transports dispatch the same `GRAPH_TOOLS` via `handleToolCall` in `src/services/causal-agent.ts`.
- Identifies the production MCP server file (`graph-mcp.ts`) and the consumers (`getMcpConfigPath` writes config → Claude Code spawns the server → `--allowedTools mcp__mnemo-graph__*`).
- Gives the current tool count or points at the constant that holds it.

And every existing reference is wrong on at least one axis.

## Result (what the docs say today)

Tool-count claims:

| Source | Quoted | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `04-sparse-branch-design.md:611` | "**7 tools** … MCP server (`services/causal-mcp.ts`)" | 38 tools in `GRAPH_TOOLS`; server is `graph-mcp.ts` |
| `04-sparse-branch-design.md:1103` | row "B6 \| Create `services/causal-mcp.ts`" | file shipped as `graph-mcp.ts` |
| `07-graph-agent-workflow.md:122` | "**12 MCP tools** via the unified `graph-mcp.ts` server" | 38; file name correct |
| `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:11` | reasoning agent "fully implemented — **25 MCP tools**" | 38 |
| `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:54` | D2 box `MCP Server / causal-mcp.ts` with "25 tools" | server is `graph-mcp.ts`; 38 tools |
| `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:118,132` | command snippet `npx tsx src/services/causal-mcp.ts` | should be `graph-mcp.ts` |

In-code drift in `src/services/causal-agent.ts:4` and `:2025` is handled by Review #13/F2 — out of scope for this bead.

## Impact

- T1 (doc-vs-code drift): every doc that mentions MCP is wrong.
- T9 (observability gap): no doc explains what `/api/mcp-health` actually probes (made worse by Review #13/F1 — the probe was probing the wrong server).
- T11 (silent drift): no documented parity contract between the two transports — the write-tool serialization divergence (Review #13/F6 candidate) has no place to live as a documented invariant.
- T13 (half-built): Pi bridge was introduced as a replacement transport but no doc covers the two-transport model; readers can't tell which path is live without reading `ml-services/.env`.

## Scoped fix

Two parts.

### Part A — create doc 30 (canonical MCP transport contract)

New file `docs/architecture/truth-graph/30-mcp-transport.md`. Sections:

1. **Overview** — two-transport architecture. MCP path (Claude Code subprocess + stdio MCP server) vs Pi bridge path (in-process tool dispatch over HTTP).
2. **Selection** — `LLM_PROVIDER` env var in `ml-services` (`claude` default, `pi`, `zai`). Document the current state (`ml-services/.env: LLM_PROVIDER=pi` as of 2026-05-25) and that the default is `claude`.
3. **MCP path data flow** — `pipeline.ts` → `invoke*Agent` → `getMcpConfigPath` writes `.graph-mcp-config.<actor>.json` → POSTs `mcp_config_path` to ml-service → `ClaudeCodeProvider._build_cmd` adds `--mcp-config + --strict-mcp-config + --allowedTools mcp__mnemo-graph__*` → Claude Code spawns `npx tsx src/services/graph-mcp.ts` → MCP server dispatches via `handleToolCall`.
4. **Pi bridge path data flow** — `pipeline.ts` → `invoke*Agent` → ml-service → `PiBridgeProvider` → HTTP POST to `pi-agent-bridge.ts:/run` → in-process `handleToolCall` (same function).
5. **Parity contract** — both transports use `GRAPH_TOOLS` + `handleToolCall` from `src/services/causal-agent.ts`. Tool count is whatever `GRAPH_TOOLS.length` returns (currently 38; verified by `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts`).
6. **Transport divergence** — known places where the two transports do not behave identically:
   - Write-tool serialization: Pi bridge serializes 17 tools via `executionMode: 'sequential'` (`src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:85-95`). MCP servers have no equivalent; concurrent writes go through unserialized. Tracked separately under Review #13/F6.
7. **Health probes** — `/api/mcp-health` (spawns `graph-mcp.ts`, does `tools/list`); `pi-agent-bridge.ts:/health` (in-process). Limitations: tools/list does not exercise DB connectivity (Review #13/F5).
8. **Process / port table** — entries for the two transports' processes and ports. Cross-link to doc 29 (Integrations layer port table, planned under nmemo-2yv.110) — single source of truth lives there once 29 is written; doc 30 references it, does not duplicate.

D2 diagram covering both data flows.

### Part B — patch existing docs

- `04-sparse-branch-design.md:611` — replace "the 7 tools are exposed as an MCP server (`services/causal-mcp.ts`)" with "the tools in `GRAPH_TOOLS` (see `src/services/causal-agent.ts`) are exposed as an MCP server (`src/services/graph-mcp.ts`); see doc 30 for the full transport contract".
- `04-sparse-branch-design.md:1103` — fix the B6 row to reference `services/graph-mcp.ts`.
- `04-sparse-branch-design.md:619` — fix the example `'--mcp-config', mcpConfigPath,` reference if surrounding prose names `causal-mcp.ts`.
- `07-graph-agent-workflow.md:122` — drop the "12 MCP tools" claim; replace with "all tools in `GRAPH_TOOLS` — see doc 30".
- `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:11` — change "25 MCP tools" to "the tools in `GRAPH_TOOLS` (currently 38) — see doc 30".
- `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:54` — fix the D2 diagram: `MCP Server / causal-mcp.ts` → `MCP Server / graph-mcp.ts`, drop the "25 tools" subscript.
- `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md:118,132` — fix the `npx tsx src/services/causal-mcp.ts` command snippets to `graph-mcp.ts`.
- `README.md` (truth-graph docs index) — add doc 30 to the reading order.

Scope guards:
- In-code stale references in `src/services/causal-agent.ts:4` and `:2025` are Review #13/F2's territory.
- Write-tool serialization fix itself (not just documenting the divergence) is Review #13/F6.
- The doc 29 port table is Review #12/F1 / nmemo-2yv.110's territory — doc 30 cross-links rather than duplicating.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/architecture/truth-graph/30-mcp-transport.md` exists with all 8 sections from Part A.
- [ ] One D2 diagram in doc 30 covering both transport data flows; valid via `d2 fmt`.
- [ ] `docs/architecture/truth-graph/README.md` lists doc 30 in the reading order.
- [ ] All 7 doc edits listed in Part B applied.
- [ ] `rg "causal-mcp\.ts" docs/architecture/truth-graph/` returns zero hits (any references to the file name in docs must be replaced — the file itself is going away under Review #13/F2).
- [ ] `rg "7 tools|7 MCP tools|12 MCP tools|25 MCP tools" docs/architecture/truth-graph/` returns zero hits.

## Themes

T1 (doc-vs-code drift), T9 (observability gap), T11 (silent transport drift), T13 (half-built — Pi bridge replacement not documented).

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Fix shape (b) merged with what would have been Review #13/F4 (the canonical-doc gap). Single bead creates doc 30 + patches the three existing docs. Rejected alternatives:

- (a) Edit in place only (no new doc). Fixes the wrong facts but leaves no canonical home for the MCP-vs-PiBridge contract; the next doc-vs-code drift has no place to land.
- (c) Drop tool counts entirely, reference code. Loses a useful skim-signal in the arch docs; no place to document the parity contract.
- (d) Doc-content CI test asserting tool counts. Speculative; introduces fragile coupling (regex over markdown). Doc 30 with a "currently 38; verified by causal-mcp.test.ts" phrasing achieves the same anti-drift signal without new infrastructure.
- Keep F3 and F4 as separate beads. Splitting them means doc 04/07/11 get edited twice (once to fix the wrong fact, once to add the cross-reference to the new doc). One bead is cleaner.
notes:
2026-05-25 — Review #13/F9 (server-name+version dedup) dropped after triage. F2 (nmemo-2yv.124) deletes causal-mcp.ts which resolves the original 'hard-coded twice' framing. Remaining state — the 'mnemo-graph' string in graph-mcp.ts + getMcpConfigPath (TS) + llm.py allowedTools pattern (Python) + test assertions — is the natural shape of a cross-language transport contract, not a defect. This bead inherits the responsibility of capturing that contract in doc 30: add an explicit 'Server identity invariant' subsection stating that the MCP server name is 'mnemo-graph', that this string appears in both TS (graph-mcp.ts, causal-agent.ts:getMcpConfigPath, tests) and Python (ml-services/app/core/llm.py:210), and that any rename requires a coordinated edit across both languages.
[2026-05-26 forward-ref from .127] When writing doc 30 (canonical MCP transport doc), add a 'Write-tool serialisation' subsection describing: WRITE_TOOLS set + writeQueue lives in causal-agent.ts:handleToolCall; both Pi and MCP transports inherit it; queue fails OPEN (.catch(() => undefined) on prior promise so a failed write doesn't DoS subsequent writes). # Delete `causal-mcp.ts` and the dead `CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS` export — duplicate MCP server with no consumer

## Premise

`src/services/causal-mcp.ts` is a 75-line MCP stdio server that exports the same `GRAPH_TOOLS` + `handleToolCall` as `src/services/graph-mcp.ts`. Production code (`getMcpConfigPath`, all 5 `invoke*Agent` flows, `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:ClaudeCodeProvider`) targets `graph-mcp.ts`. Once Review #13/F1 retargets the health probe to `graph-mcp.ts`, `causal-mcp.ts` has zero consumers in `src/**`, `ml-services/**`, or `.graph-mcp-config*.json`.

## Falsifying test

`rg -n "causal-mcp" src ml-services` after F1 + F2 returns zero hits (other than the body of this bead itself).

## Result (what the code does today, post-F1)

- `src/services/causal-mcp.ts` exists on disk, structurally identical to `graph-mcp.ts` except: server name `mnemo-causal` (vs `mnemo-graph`), version `1.0.0` (vs `2.0.0`), and a stale block comment on lines 17-19.
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:64-65` — `/** @deprecated Use GRAPH_TOOLS */ export const CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS: ToolDefinition[] = [];` — empty array, referenced only from the stale comment in `causal-mcp.ts:17-19` ("kept for backwards-compatible imports"). No live importer.
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:4` — file header still claims *"7 tools for the causal reasoning agent, exposed via MCP server (causal-mcp.ts)"*. Both numbers and file name wrong (38 tools, `graph-mcp.ts`).
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:2025` — jsdoc on `invokeCausalAgent` says *"MCP config pointing to the causal-mcp.ts server"*. Also wrong.

## Impact

- Every reader of the services directory has to re-derive that `causal-mcp.ts` is dead. The duplicate is the doc-vs-code drift signal.
- The `CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS = []` export is a tripwire: if anything ever imports it (e.g., a future refactor that grep's for "tools"), the agent silently runs with zero tools.
- `mnemo-causal` server name is unreachable from production config (registers `mnemo-graph`) and from the `--allowedTools mcp__mnemo-graph__*` pattern in `ml-services/app/core/llm.py:210`. If anyone wires `causal-mcp.ts` up by changing only the script path, Claude Code spawns it but rejects every tool call.

## Scoped fix

Hard delete. Concrete steps:

1. Delete `src/services/causal-mcp.ts`.
2. Delete `src/services/causal-agent.ts:64-65` (the `CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS` export and its `@deprecated` jsdoc).
3. Scrub stale `causal-mcp.ts` references in inline comments/jsdocs in `src/services/causal-agent.ts`:
   - Line 4 (file header — update to reference `graph-mcp.ts` and current tool count).
   - Line 2025 (jsdoc on `invokeCausalAgent` — update to `graph-mcp.ts`).
   - Any survivors after F1's rename.

Scope guards:
- Doc-side cleanup of `causal-mcp.ts` references in `docs/architecture/truth-graph/04-sparse-branch-design.md:611` and `11-smoke-test-reasoning-agent.md` (lines 54, 118, 132, 211, 214, 247) belongs to Review #13/F3 (doc-drift cleanup), not this bead.
- `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts` filename stays as-is. The test content covers `handleToolCall` + `getMcpConfigPath` and is unaffected. Cosmetic rename ("mcp-handlers.test.ts") is non-blocking polish, deferred.

Depends on Review #13/F1 — F1 must land first (the health probe still spawns `causal-mcp.ts` until then).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `src/services/causal-mcp.ts` no longer exists.
- [ ] `CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS` no longer exported from `src/services/causal-agent.ts` (`rg "CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS" src` returns zero hits).
- [ ] `rg "causal-mcp" src ml-services` returns zero hits in source code (`.tmp/` body files and arch docs may still contain the string — those are F3's territory).
- [ ] Comments at `src/services/causal-agent.ts:4` and `:2025` reference `graph-mcp.ts` and the correct tool count (38 or "all GRAPH_TOOLS").
- [ ] Build + existing test suite pass; `src/test/harness/causal-mcp.test.ts` still green (it doesn't import `causal-mcp.ts`).

## Themes

T1 (doc-vs-code drift), T13 (half-built pipeline — duplicate dangles after replacement landed).

## Decision (locked 2026-05-25)

Hard delete (option a). Rejected alternatives:

- (b) Keep-but-deprecate. The file's continued existence is itself the drift signal; an extra deprecation comment doesn't fix that.
- (c) Repurpose as a read-only MCP variant. Speculative — no current consumer for a read-only MCP; F6's parallelism concern has its own fix-shape conversation that may not need a separate file.
- (d) Rename `graph-mcp.ts` → `causal-mcp.ts` (preserve the older filename). Contradicts current production state where config + tests are anchored on `graph-mcp.ts`; broader blast radius; misnamed (GRAPH_TOOLS spans far more than causal).
