title: [bug] component_size NULL fallback uses post-k_core bucket length — inverts doc 25 §2.1 'A.size = full component size' invariant
description:
# Summary

In cross-cluster-generator.ts at lines 408-416, the MIN_COMPONENT_SIZE gate falls back to byComponent.get(cid).length when entity_topology.component_size is NULL:

    const componentIds = [...byComponent.keys()].filter(
      (cid) => (componentSizeMeta.get(cid) ?? byComponent.get(cid)!.length) >= minComponentSize(),
    );

byComponent was built from a query that already filtered by k_core >= MIN_K_CORE_FOR_BRIDGE. So a 50-entity component with 48 entities at k_core=0 gives a bucket of length 2. The MIN_COMPONENT_SIZE gate is supposed to use the FULL component size (per doc 25 §2.1 — 'A.size = the full component size (the gate), bucket length is the iteration surface for scoring') but the fallback inverts this.

# When it manifests

- Phase 2 hasn't run yet (cold start).
- Phase 2 partially completed (mid-migration).
- Dev/test DBs where the topology compute was bypassed.
- A bug or schema drift causes component_size to be unset.

# Why P3 not P2

In the steady state where Phase 2 runs to completion before cross-cluster fires (the documented contract), component_size is always populated and the fallback is never reached. The bug is latent. But the existing isUpstreamFresh gate does not catch NULL component_size — it only checks topology_compute_runs.completed_at vs entities.created_at. A successful topology compute that fails to populate component_size (schema/upstream bug) would slip through the freshness check and hit the broken fallback.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-21)

Option (a) from the design menu: treat NULL component_size as a hard skip with skippedReason='stale_upstream'. Aligns with the existing 'upstream incomplete' semantics — a missing meta column is the stale-upstream class of problem.

Rejected:
- (b) hard error on NULL — makes the generator brittle in mixed states (partial backfill, synthetic dev fixtures, recovery scenarios).
- (c) compensating SELECT-COUNT(*) query — papers over the symptom; a NULL meta column means upstream is broken and should be surfaced, not silently corrected.

# Fix shape

1. After loadCandidateEntities, before the MIN_COMPONENT_SIZE gate, scan for any (component_id, NULL component_size) row. If any exist:
   - console.warn with the affected component_ids.
   - Set result = { ran: false, skippedReason: 'stale_upstream', componentPairsEvaluated: 0, candidatesInserted: 0, driftDrivenCandidates: 0, durationMs: ... }
   - Return early (still inside the tx; the advisory lock auto-releases).

2. Remove the ?? byComponent.get(cid).length fallback. After the new gate, componentSizeMeta is guaranteed populated for every component_id present in byComponent.

3. Update the cross_cluster_runs telemetry row (when nmemo-2yv.92 lands) to record this skip reason — operator can see 'last run skipped because component_size missing' rather than guessing.

# Acceptance

1. Generator returns ran=false, skippedReason='stale_upstream' when any (component_id, component_size) row has NULL component_size.
2. console.warn logs the affected component_ids (or count, if too many to log individually).
3. The ?? byComponent.get(cid).length fallback is removed; the MIN_COMPONENT_SIZE gate reads exclusively from componentSizeMeta.
4. New unit test: seed entity_topology rows with component_id set but component_size NULL; assert ran=false with skippedReason='stale_upstream'.
5. Existing unit tests that pre-seed component_size correctly continue to pass without modification.
6. (Soft dependency) cross_cluster_runs telemetry (.92) records this skip distinctly from the existing freshness-gate skip, so operators can disambiguate.

title: Add synthetic-10k-cross-component fixture variant — current synthetic-10k's ground-truth bridges are intra-component, benchmark can't gate recall
description:
# Summary

cross-cluster-generator.snapshot.test.ts records recall/precision/F1 against synthetic-10k.ground_truth.bridge_pairs, but the synthetic-10k generator emits bridges intra-component (all in component_0). Phase 4 by design only targets cross-component pairs, so recall is structurally 0 on the current fixture. The benchmark tests comment this caveat:

  'the bead acceptance criteria explicitly say tuneable; recorded in benchmark report. We record but do not gate on the absolute value because synthetic-10k's ground-truth bridge pairs are intra-component (all in component_0), and Phase 4 by design only targets cross-component pairs. groundTruthDistribution captures this so the 0 recall is interpretable. Updating the synthetic generator to produce cross-component bridges is tracked as follow-up work.'

This bead IS that follow-up work.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-21)

Option (a) from the design menu: new fixture variant 'synthetic-10k-cross-component' that deliberately seeds N cross-component bridge pairs. Existing synthetic-10k stays as-is (still useful for intra-component testing). Benchmark gates recall ONLY on the new variant.

title: Doc 25 §3.2 says cross-cluster auto-trigger lives in pipeline.ts; code is in index.ts (post-compute fire-and-forget)
description:
# Summary

Doc 25 §3.2 says: 'in pipeline.ts, after both topology/compute and semantic-clustering/compute complete successfully on the same patrol, fire generateCrossClusterCandidates() in try/catch. Mirrors the existing incrementPatrolCount pattern from Phase 6.'

Actual code (index.ts:998 triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute + call sites at index.ts:1034 post-topology, index.ts:1196 post-clustering) implements a fire-and-forget post-HTTP-route hook, not a pipeline.ts patrol-counter pattern. Functionally equivalent because the freshness gate enforces both-fresh, but the doc and the code disagree on placement and pattern.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-21)

Option (a) doc-only fix. Update doc 25 §3.2 to describe the actual shape:
- Helper triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute(after: 'topology' | 'clustering') in platform/src/index.ts.
- Called fire-and-forget (void) from /api/topology/compute and /api/clustering/compute success branches.
- Idempotency / both-fresh enforcement via the freshness gate inside generateCrossClusterCandidates (the gate skips when either upstream is stale).
- Concurrency safety via pg_try_advisory_xact_lock inside the generator (skipped with reason='lock_held' if another invocation is running).

Option (b) extract the helper to a service module was rejected on duplication grounds — nmemo-2yv.88 already covers the longer-term move of triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute + triggerReconciliationDriftAfterCompute into a services/drift.ts (or similar). The doc gets updated again when .88 lands; that's a normal cost.

# Out of scope

Re-architecting the trigger to a true 'same-patrol' bothness check (i.e. require both topology AND clustering to have run since the last cross-cluster invocation). The freshness gate already enforces both-fresh by checking each *_compute_runs.completed_at >= entities.created_at, which gives equivalent guarantees in steady state. If a real bug surfaces (e.g. the generator runs twice in quick succession when both computes fire near-simultaneously) revisit then.

# Acceptance

1. Doc 25 §3.2 'Endpoint and pipeline wiring' subsection is updated to describe the actual implementation: helper in index.ts (or wherever .88 has moved it by the time this lands), called fire-and-forget from each compute's route success branch, both-fresh enforced by the inner freshness gate.
2. The misleading reference to 'pipeline.ts' and 'mirrors incrementPatrolCount pattern' is removed.
3. The doc adds a note that nmemo-2yv.88 will move the helper to a services/ module; the doc text is forward-compatible with that move (refer to 'the trigger helper' without pinning the file path).

title: Add CHECK constraint enumerating valid candidate_source values on merge_candidates
description:
# Summary

migration 017_candidate_source.sql adds candidate_source VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'three_signal_scoring' with no CHECK constraint. Doc 25 §2.3 enumerates exactly two values: 'three_signal_scoring' and 'cross_cluster_generator'. Sibling columns on the same table have CHECK constraints (valid_candidate_status, valid_resolution in 003_graph_meta.sql).

A typo in either writer (cross-cluster-generator.ts upsertCandidate or graph-meta.ts three-signal upsert) silently inserts a row that the reconciliation_agent's prompt-builder treats as 'unknown' and falls back to the three-signal block (per ml-services/tests/test_reconciliation_prompt.py:152 backward-compat path). Wrong prompt context delivered to the LLM with no signal at the schema layer.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-21)

Option (a) strict CHECK enumerating the two current values. Future sources (doc 26 structural-embeddings is the next candidate) extend via a follow-up migration that adds the new value to the CHECK. Reasoning:
- reconciliation_agent branches on exact string equality. Any new source MUST ship a coordinated prompt-builder update. A schema migration is the right forcing function to make those land together.
- (b) regex pattern CHECK does not catch typos within the alphabet (the bug class that matters).
- (c) lookup table with FK is over-engineered for a 2-value enum.

# Fix shape

New migration file:

    ALTER TABLE public.merge_candidates
      ADD CONSTRAINT valid_candidate_source CHECK (
        candidate_source IN ('three_signal_scoring', 'cross_cluster_generator')
      );

Idempotent: if a row exists with a value outside the set (shouldn't, but be safe in dev DBs), the ALTER will fail. Test on cognitive_test first.

# Acceptance

1. New migration adds CHECK constraint valid_candidate_source on public.merge_candidates restricting candidate_source to ('three_signal_scoring', 'cross_cluster_generator').
2. Migration is idempotent-safe (handles re-runs in dev — name the constraint, use IF NOT EXISTS pattern or guard with information_schema check).
3. Doc 25 §2.3 / §3.3 reference the constraint as the schema-layer enforcement of the source enum.
4. When doc 26 (structural-embeddings) lands, the spec must include a follow-up migration extending the CHECK to include the new source value. Add a note to doc 26's spec page (or open a tracking bead) that this migration is part of the new-source onboarding checklist.

title: (CHORE) Decide fate of entity-reclassification.ts — zero production callers, intended ontology evolution agent never built; docstring cites non-existent migration 024
description:
# Summary

`platform/src/services/entity-reclassification.ts` exports three functions intended for an "ontology evolution" agent that promotes new entity types and reclassifies existing entities matching the new type. No such agent exists in canonical code.

Exported functions:
- `findReclassificationCandidates(newType, exemplarEntityIds, sourceType, options)`
- `reclassifyEntity(entityId, newType, reason, changedBy='ontology-evolution')`
- `batchReclassify(entityIds, newType, reason)`

# Repo-wide callers (full grep)

Only two consumers, both integration tests:
- `src/test/integration/ontology-edge-cases.test.ts` (imports `reclassifyEntity`)
- `src/test/integration/ontology-reclassification.test.ts` (imports `reclassifyEntity` + `batchReclassify`)

**Zero production callers** in `services/`, `index.ts`, MCP servers, viz, or `scripts/`. The intended ontology-evolution agent was never built.

# Stale docstring

`entity-reclassification.ts:11`:
> "Every change is audited in entity_type_history (migration 024)"

Reality: `entity_type_history` table is defined in `001_consolidated.sql:256`. No file named `024_*.sql` exists in the repo (migrations directory only goes up to 016, modulo gaps).

# Falsifications attempted

- ml-services Python calls these via HTTP → falsified; no /api/reclassify or /api/ontology endpoints
- MCP tool exposes them → falsified; neither causal-mcp.ts nor graph-mcp.ts exposes reclassify
- Scripts in /scripts/ invoke them → falsified
- Dev tool / one-off script imports them → falsified

# Posture

This is *deferred capability* rather than dead code: working code + tests, no consumer. Same shape as `.26` (P3 CHORE — obsolete CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS) except .26 was clearly obsolete (replaced consumer); C9 is unfinished (consumer never built).

# Fate options for the implementer

(a) **Delete** — remove the service module + its tests. Reclaim the surface; if the ontology evolution agent ever lands, recreate from a future commit. Risk: lose a working implementation that future work has to redo.

(b) **Mark as future-use** — add a "currently unused — intended for the ontology evolution agent" header comment. Keep tests gated by skip-unless. Preserves the work; flags non-load-bearing.

(c) **Wire a consumer** — actually build the ontology evolution agent (much bigger scope; out-of-scope for this CHORE bead).

# Related beads

- `.26` (P3 CHORE) — Remove obsolete CAUSAL_AGENT_TOOLS export (analogous orphan-service pattern)
- `.46` (P2) — Delete /api/viz/run-meta (orphan endpoint pattern; service-side equivalent is this bead)
- `.59` (P2) — Doc gap for entity living-summary feature (analogous "code without canonical design doc" pattern)

# Note on scope statement

This bead was filed because Review #9's `nmemo-2yv.9` scope statement lists `entity-reclassification.ts` alongside migrations 014/015/016. They are unrelated features: 014/015/016 are topology/clustering/drift (covered in the rest of Review #9); `entity-reclassification.ts` is its own feature surface tied to `entity_type_history` (mig 001). Filed here as a side-track per scope-statement reconciliation in Review #9 candidate sweep.

title: (BUG) Race window in compute concurrency check — _check_in_progress + _acquire_run non-atomic across topology.py / semantic_clustering.py / drift.py
description:
# Summary

In `topology.py`, `semantic_clustering.py`, and `drift.py`, the in-progress check is non-atomic:

```python
in_progress = await _check_in_progress(conn, ...)
if in_progress:
    return 409
run_id = await _acquire_run(conn, ...)
```

Two concurrent callers can both observe `in_progress=False`, both `_acquire_run`, and both proceed to write derived state. Today this is rare because all three computes are manual-only (viz click). Once `.84` lands (scheduler + post-merge + post-ingest counter), concurrent fires become routine, not theoretical.

# Decision (locked 2026-05-20)

**Use `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` with a per-compute-kind key constant.** Locked decision over the partial-UNIQUE-index alternative for these reasons:

- Zero schema migration. Advisory locks live in shared memory, not the schema.
- Cross-compute uniform pattern. Same three-line shape in `topology.py`, `semantic_clustering.py`, `drift.py` with only the lock key constant differing.
- Lock auto-released on any transaction exit (commit, rollback, connection drop). No "stuck in_progress row" recovery dance, no orphan-status cleanup.
- Consistent with the existing codebase pattern. The cross-cluster generator already uses advisory locks (per `.86`'s test scope for "advisory-lock concurrent-call skip"). We extend the same idiom.

## Implementation shape

A shared constant module (e.g., `ml-services/app/locks.py` or extension to an existing constants module) defines:

```python
COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS = {
    "topology": 1001,
    "semantic_clustering": 1002,
    "drift": 1003,
}
```

(Keys are arbitrary distinct bigints; collisions with other advisory locks in the system must be checked. Cross-cluster generator's existing key should be documented in the same module.)

Each compute endpoint wraps its work:

```python
async with conn.transaction():
    acquired = await conn.fetchval(
        "SELECT pg_try_advisory_xact_lock($1)",
        COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS["topology"],
    )
    if not acquired:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="topology compute in progress")
    # existing _acquire_run + compute + write logic
```

The original `_check_in_progress` SELECT-then-something pattern is removed or repurposed for read-only status reporting (i.e., the `_check_in_progress` helper can stay as a read-only "is this lock currently held" query for diagnostic endpoints, but the race-prone pre-flight check before `_acquire_run` is gone).

## Test coverage

The "two concurrent calls, one wins with 409" integration test is already in `.86`'s scope (criterion 5). `.87` does not duplicate it; `.87` lands the lock primitive, `.86` lands the test that exercises it. Ordering: `.87` first OR they land together.

# Severity calibration

- `.38` (P1) — `resolveContradiction` race window (concurrent mutate on facts / edges). Same shape but on production transactional path with higher blast radius.
- `.48` (P3) — `computed_duration_ms` written outside transaction. Same tier.

P3 today; **automatically escalates to P2 once `.84` lands** because the scheduler / post-merge / post-ingest counter will routinely fire concurrent computes. Land `.87` together with or before `.84`.

# Falsifications attempted

- "Maybe `_acquire_run` is itself atomic" — no. It's a plain `INSERT ... RETURNING id` after the prior `SELECT`. Not race-free against another connection's `SELECT`.
- "Maybe there's an existing UNIQUE constraint that catches the race" — checked the migration files for topology / clustering / drift runs tables. No `WHERE status='in_progress'` partial unique index. The constraint that would make a partial UNIQUE solution work doesn't exist yet.
- "Maybe FastAPI worker isolation prevents concurrent calls" — no. uvicorn workers are independent processes / async tasks; same DB, same race.

# Related beads

- `.84` — auto-triggers; this is the trigger that turns the P3 race into a routine event. Land `.87` first or in the same change.
- `.38` (P1) — `resolveContradiction` race window. Analogous pattern, higher tier (transactional production path).
- `.48` (P3) — `computed_duration_ms` outside transaction. Same tier.
- `.86` — test scaffolding. Houses the "two concurrent calls" verification test for the lock primitive landed here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New shared constants module (ml-services/app/locks.py or equivalent) defines COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS dict with distinct bigint keys for topology, semantic_clustering, drift. Cross-cluster generator advisory-lock key is documented in the same module.

2. topology.py /topology/compute is race-free: wraps work in pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS[topology]); on lock-not-acquired, returns HTTP 409 with detail topology compute in progress; only one writer writes to entity_topology / topology_bridges per cycle.

3. semantic_clustering.py /clustering/compute is race-free in the same shape, using COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS[semantic_clustering].

4. drift.py /drift/compute is race-free in the same shape, using COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS[drift].

5. The race-prone SELECT-then-INSERT pattern (in-progress check followed by separate _acquire_run) is removed or repurposed for read-only diagnostic status. The atomicity guarantee comes from the advisory lock, not from the pre-check.

6. Concurrent-call verification test is owned by .86 (criterion 5) and exercises this primitive. .87 does not duplicate it. Land .87 before or together with .84 so the scheduler / post-merge / post-ingest fires from .84 do not hit the race.

7. Lock auto-release on transaction end (commit, rollback, connection drop) is verified by inspection — advisory locks held via pg_try_advisory_xact_lock are released automatically; no manual cleanup needed.

8. No schema migration is introduced by this work.
notes:
[2026-05-26] APPLIED: 4 edits — new ml-services/app/core/locks.py with COMPUTE_LOCK_KEYS dict; topology.py / semantic_clustering.py / drift.py @router.post handlers all rewrapped in 'with conn.transaction(): pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(...)' shape per locked spec. Race-prone _check_in_progress pre-flight call sites removed (functions remain defined but unused, per bead's 'removed OR repurposed' allowance — minimum-diff path). Single big transaction wraps lock + _acquire_run + compute + _complete_run; commits on success, rolls back on exception with no separate 'failed' row written (status visibility migrates from in_progress row to pg_locks). Python imports verified at runtime.
[2026-05-26] REVIEWED: focused medium-effort code-review returned [] (no high-confidence bugs). 1 stray dead-code line at topology.py:182 (unreachable raise referencing undefined exc — leftover from original except-as-exc body) caught and removed. locks.py docstring rewritten to accurately describe the shared keyspace + non-collision invariant (int4 hashtext range vs small bigints 1001-1003). Pre-existing stale 'in_progress' rows from before this change will sit forever (no caller cleans them up post-bead; harmless cruft — flagged for operator-side cleanup if needed). Three non-blocking notes worth noting in the lessons file.

title: Add triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('drift') hook after /api/drift/compute — drift events feed cross-cluster generator but only get consumed at next topology/clustering click
description:
# Summary

`platform/src/index.ts` fire-and-forgets `triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute(after)` from two call sites:

- `POST /api/topology/compute` (line 1036) → `triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('topology')`
- `POST /api/clustering/compute` (line 1197) → `triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('clustering')`

`POST /api/drift/compute` (line 1322+) does **not** fire the trigger. But `entity_drift_events` are a generator input (doc 25 §2.2, W2/W3 = 25% of combined score). Until the next manual topology/clustering click, new drift events sit unconsumed.

# Why this matters (and what limits it)

- The cross-cluster generator's freshness gate (doc 25 §3.2) is keyed on topology+clustering recency, not drift. So a "post-drift" trigger correctly runs when topology/clustering are still fresh, and skips with `stale_upstream` when they aren't. Safe to add.
- With `nmemo-2yv.84` landed (topology/clustering/drift auto-triggers), drift events get picked up at the next auto-fired topology/clustering anyway. This bead shaves hours/minutes off the latency by triggering immediately after a drift compute.
- Without .84 landed, drift events have *no* automatic consumer until a manual button click — this bead has somewhat higher value (P2-ish) standalone, but the project intent is to land .84 first.

# Falsifications attempted

- Freshness gate would reject post-drift triggers → falsified; the gate checks topology+clustering recency, not drift.
- Doc 25 forbids drift triggers → falsified; doc explicitly lists `entity_drift_events` as a generator input.

# Surgical change

```typescript
// index.ts ~line 998
async function triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute(after: 'topology' | 'clustering' | 'drift'): Promise<void> {
  // unchanged body — the log line just needs 'drift' to be a valid value
}

// index.ts ~line 1322 (inside /api/drift/compute success path)
void triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('drift');
```

# Related beads

- `nmemo-2yv.84` — three computes have no auto-trigger (parent context for this bead)
- `nmemo-2yv.83` — /reconciliation-agent/drift never invoked (separately wires the agent for drift events; this bead wires cross-cluster generator for the same events)
- doc 25 §2.2 / §3.2 — cross-cluster generator inputs + freshness gate
acceptance_criteria:
1. triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute's parameter type accepts 'drift' (in addition to 'topology' and 'clustering').
2. The success path of /api/drift/compute in platform/src/index.ts fire-and-forgets triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('drift').
3. The log message inside triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute correctly attributes 'drift' as the trigger source ('[cross-cluster] auto-trigger after drift/compute: ...').
4. Integration test verifies that a successful /api/drift/compute fires the cross-cluster generator (or shows the freshness-gate skip with skippedReason if topology/clustering are stale).
notes:
Closed by commit ceffe95.

Fix landed in two minimal edits to platform/src/index.ts:
1. Widened triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute's 'after' param type from 'topology' | 'clustering' to add 'drift'. The literal is only consumed by the log line.
2. Fire-and-forget triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('drift') in the /api/drift/compute success path, sitting next to the existing triggerReconciliationDriftAfterCompute() call (bead .83). Matches the topology/clustering hook pattern.

Tests in platform/src/test/harness/topology-clustering-drift-http.test.ts:
- New in-process T13 test: triggerCrossClusterAfterCompute('drift') with stale upstream resolves cleanly with no unhandled rejection.
- New env-gated smoke test (RUN_HTTP_SMOKE=1): POST /api/drift/compute on the live platform causes a cross_cluster_runs row to land.

Vitest shows the EXISTING happy-path test for /api/drift/compute now logs '[cross-cluster] auto-trigger after drift/compute skipped: stale_upstream' as a side-effect of hitting the route, which satisfies acceptance #2 (route fires the trigger) and #3 (log attributes 'drift') without needing a dedicated assertion.

All 4 acceptance criteria satisfied:
1. Param accepts 'drift' — types updated.
2. /api/drift/compute success path fires the trigger.
3. Log message reads '[cross-cluster] auto-trigger after drift/compute: ...' (confirmed in vitest stdout).
4. Integration test covers both the freshness-gate skip case (in-process) and the cross_cluster_runs lands case (env-gated smoke).

27/27 in-process tests pass in topology-clustering-drift-http.test.ts (4 smoke tests env-skipped as designed).

title: Other agents (reconciliation, gardener) should read scoped reasoning_history before acting — currently only the reasoning agent itself reads its own history
description:
`get_reasoning_history(entity_id, limit?)` is exposed in the unified `graph-mcp` tool surface — every agent that connects to the MCP server has access. In practice only the reasoning agent's system prompt (`ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py`) mentions it. Reconciliation and gardener prompts don't.

This means the reasoning agent's accumulated conclusions are invisible to the other agents at the moment they make decisions:

- **Reconciliation agent** decides whether to merge two entities. If the reasoning agent already concluded in a prior patrol "A and B are distinct because <reasoning>", the reconciliation agent has no signal — it re-evaluates from scratch. Same for the reverse (reasoning agent said they're the same identity in a query-mode pass; reconciliation agent doesn't know).
- **Gardener** decides structural changes (merges, same-as, islands). Same opacity to prior reasoning conclusions.

The scoped read pattern is already correct: `get_reasoning_history(entity_id, limit)` is bounded by entity and capped by recency. The user's note: "obviously not all of it but seems like a good feature to have" — i.e. scoped, not blanket. The infrastructure is right; the prompts don't use it.

## Decision needed (do not pre-decide implementation)

Per-agent audit and prompt addition:

1. **Reconciliation agent** — before calling `execute_merge` or `create_same_as_link`, fetch the reasoning_history for both candidate entities (capped at e.g. 3 most recent reports each). If any prior reasoning report explicitly addressed the identity question, surface that in the prompt to inform the decision.
2. **Gardener** — when investigating a neighbourhood, fetch reasoning_history for the central entity. Don't re-do work the reasoning agent already did.
3. **Token budget** — full reports can be long. Either limit by count + cap by character length, or fetch report summaries only (this might require schema work — add `summary TEXT` to reasoning_reports that the reasoning agent populates as it saves; or compute summaries on read).

## Risks / open questions

- **T8 prompt-injection compounds**: every additional agent that reads `reasoning_reports.report` and `reasoning_reports.question` becomes a new prompt-injection surface. Wait for nmemo-2yv.62 (centralised prompt-safety helper) to land before adding these read paths.
- **Token cost** — small reports are cheap, but agent prompts inflate fast when each one fetches history for every entity it considers.
- **Staleness** — old reasoning reports might be wrong (the world changed, new evidence arrived). The agent reading them must understand this is *prior reasoning at a point in time*, not current truth. Prompt framing matters.

## Cross-references

- nmemo-2yv.62 (T8 helper) — gates this work; do not add new prompt-injection surfaces until the helper lands.
- nmemo-2yv.73 (principle doc) — supports this finding: agents are first-class units that should be aware of each other's outputs.
- nmemo-2yv.42, .43, .44 (reconciliation scoring + agent prompt simplification work) — reconciliation agent prompt is being reworked; this read-path addition can ride that PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-agent decision recorded: which agents (beyond reasoning) should be prompted to read reasoning_history, and at which decision points in their loop.
- Prompt additions land in the relevant python agent files (reconciliation_agent.py, gardener_agent.py as appropriate), each routed through the nmemo-2yv.62 prompt-safety helper for the report and question fields.
- Token budget rule documented in each agent's prompt (limit + cap).
- Optional: schema extension to add reasoning_reports.summary TEXT for cheap-read summaries, populated by save_reasoning_report (would be a sibling task if pursued).
- Regression test for at least one consumer (e.g., reconciliation reads prior reasoning, doesn't merge entities that a prior reasoning pass marked distinct).
notes:
Closed by commits 7591069 + (pending) on bead/92-cross-cluster-runs-telemetry.

Per-agent decision (recorded as required by acceptance):
- reconciliation_agent — reads get_reasoning_history(entity_a_id, limit=3) AND get_reasoning_history(entity_b_id, limit=3) at the START of per-candidate investigation (INVESTIGATION PROCESS step 1; WORKFLOW step 2a). Decision point: BEFORE same_as / merge / distinct.
- gardener_agent — reads get_reasoning_history(entity_id, limit=3) for the central entity of each neighbourhood (PHASE 2 lead-in) and for BOTH entities of suspected name-variant pairs (name-variants subroutine step 1). Decision point: BEFORE consolidation actions.

Prompt-safety routing (acceptance: route through nmemo-2yv.62 helper):
- reasoning_reports.report + .question already routed via delimitForPrompt at the MCP boundary in causal-agent.ts:2218-2231 (landed under .62 Review #8). Both fields arrive at the agent already wrapped in <reasoning_report> / <prior_question> blocks.
- PROMPT_SAFETY_SYSTEM_CLAUSE now appears in all three system prompts that read these fields back (reasoning, reconciliation, gardener) so the agent knows the delimited blocks are DATA, not instructions.

Token budget rule (acceptance):
- limit=3 per entity per call, documented inline in both prompts. Each report already capped at ~2000-char soft / ~3000-char hard by the prompt-safety helper.

Schema extension (acceptance: optional):
- Deferred. No reasoning_reports.summary column added; the per-report 2000-char cap from the helper is sufficient at current scale. Sibling task if read cost grows.

Regression test (acceptance):
- ml-services/tests/test_agent_history_awareness.py — 12 prompt-shape tests covering: tool mention, scoped read cap, staleness framing (hypothesis seed, not verdict; re-verify against current), PROMPT_SAFETY_SYSTEM_CLAUSE presence, workflow ordering (history before facts), islands + name-variants subroutine ordering, reasoning-agent regression guard. All green. Existing test_reconciliation_prompt (8) and test_prompt_safety (27) still pass.

Scope decisions made as reviewer+implementer (bead body asked for the decision):
- Prompt-only change. No new tool, no schema change, no read-boundary code change — the read-boundary work for these fields already landed under .62.
- "Scoped" interpreted as limit=3 per entity + lifetime-of-prompt-safety-helper soft cap on report text. Matches the bead body's "obviously not all of it" framing.

title: Add viz debug panel for reasoning_reports — surface recent reports, patrol cadence, entity coverage
description:
The viz has dedicated panels for adjacent features (`viz/js/panels/history.js`, `contradictions.js`, `cross-cluster.js`, `detail.js`, `impact.js`, `patterns.js`, `stats.js`) but nothing surfaces `reasoning_reports`. The Reason button kicks the agent off; the agent's output appears in the answer textarea (`showAnswer(...)` in `viz/js/agents/reason.js`); past reports are invisible from the viz.

This is fine when the viz is purely an action-launcher, but the architectural principle in nmemo-2yv.73 frames viz explicitly as "a debugging surface" — and the most useful thing a developer can see when debugging the reasoning agent is the prior runs.

## Proposed panel content

- Recent reports list — last 20 by created_at DESC: mode, question (if query), timestamp, count of entity_ids/fact_ids/causal_edge_ids
- Click-through: open the full report markdown in a side panel
- Per-entity drill-in: when an entity is selected in the canvas, the panel filters to reports touching that entity (via the existing GIN index on `entity_ids`)
- Patrol-cadence stats: time-since-last-patrol, count by mode, average duration (from the durationMs returned by /api/reason)

## Endpoints needed

- `GET /api/reasoning-reports?limit=N&mode=patrol|query` — list endpoint, paginated
- `GET /api/reasoning-reports/by-entity/:entity_id?limit=N` — entity-filtered (could reuse `get_reasoning_history` tool's read logic; do not expose the MCP tool to viz directly)
- `GET /api/reasoning-reports/:id` — single report detail

## Cross-references

- nmemo-2yv.34 (surface decay manual trigger in viz alongside garden/reconcile/reason — same shape, P3)
- nmemo-2yv.73 (architectural principle: viz is a debugging surface; this panel is on-principle)

title: src/services/causal-agent.ts bundles four agents into one ~2300-line file misnamed for one of them — extract reasoning-agent.ts when next touching
description:
`src/services/causal-agent.ts` is ~2300 lines and owns:

- Causal-agent tool definitions and handlers
- Reasoning-agent tool definitions (`get_reasoning_history`, `save_reasoning_report`) + `invokeReasoningAgent()` (line 2238)
- Gardener-agent invocation `invokeGardenerAgent()` (line 2174)
- Graph-agent invocation `invokeGraphAgent()` (line ~2207)
- MCP health check `checkCausalMcpHealth()` (line 2290)
- ~25 unified tool definitions consumed by `graph-mcp.ts`

The file name advertises a single agent; the contents are the multi-agent surface. T1 fragmentation — name and scope diverge.

## Why this clashes with the principle in nmemo-2yv.73

"Users invoke agents only" treats agents as first-class architectural units. Bundling four agents into a file named for one fights the framing — a future contributor opening `causal-agent.ts` expecting causal-agent code finds the whole fleet.

## Proposed direction: extract when next touching

Split into:

- `src/services/causal-agent.ts` — causal-agent tools + handlers only
- `src/services/reasoning-agent.ts` — reasoning-agent tools, handler, `invokeReasoningAgent`
- `src/services/gardener-agent.ts` — `invokeGardenerAgent`
- `src/services/graph-agent.ts` — `invokeGraphAgent`
- `src/services/mcp-tools.ts` (or similar barrel) — re-aggregates the unified tool list so `graph-mcp.ts` import surface doesn't change

Shared helpers (`getMcpConfigPath`, `config`, fetch wrappers) move into a small `src/services/agent-common.ts` to avoid cross-imports between the agent files.

## Recommend: ride alongside the next PR that touches the file

Several Review #8 findings will require edits to `causal-agent.ts`:

- nmemo-2yv.71 (auto-trigger work — touches invokeReasoningAgent)
- nmemo-2yv.72 (decouple cadences — removes `incrementPatrolCount` call from invokeReasoningAgent)
- nmemo-2yv.76 (fetch timeout — touches invokeReasoningAgent fetch)
- nmemo-2yv.77 (idempotency key — touches save_reasoning_report handler + tool schema)

Whichever lands first can carry the rename + extraction. Picker-up gets a 2300-line review for free once and the file shrinks for everyone afterwards.

## Severity

P3 — refactor-when-touched. The bundled file works correctly; the issue is cognitive load and principle alignment, not a bug. Skipping is acceptable if no one touches the file, but the four findings above mean someone will.
acceptance_criteria:
- src/services/reasoning-agent.ts exists and owns the reasoning-agent tools, handler dispatch (cases for get_reasoning_history / save_reasoning_report), and invokeReasoningAgent.
- src/services/gardener-agent.ts and src/services/graph-agent.ts similarly extract their respective invokers.
- src/services/causal-agent.ts retains only the causal-agent tool definitions and handlers; file shrinks substantially.
- Unified MCP tool list re-aggregated (barrel file or equivalent) so graph-mcp.ts and other consumers see no API change.
- Shared helpers (getMcpConfigPath etc.) extracted to a common module to avoid agent-to-agent imports.
- All existing tests pass without modification (import paths may update in test files; behaviour unchanged).
notes: Extracted invokeReasoningAgent + ReasoningAgentParams + ReasoningAgentResult to src/services/reasoning-agent.ts. AgentInvocationTimeoutError and agentFetch stay in causal-agent.ts (shared by graph + gardener invokers); agentFetch promoted to exported so the new module can use it; AgentInvocationTimeoutError re-exported from reasoning-agent.ts for convenience. causal-agent.ts re-exports the three new symbols so existing consumers (src/index.ts, src/test/services/causal-agent-timeout.test.ts) need no import sweep — new code should import from './reasoning-agent.js' directly. The remaining reasoning-related surface — GRAPH_TOOLS entries (get_reasoning_history, save_reasoning_report, get_reasoning_targets) and dispatcher cases inside handleToolCall — stays in causal-agent.ts; splitting cleanly needs a barrel/dispatcher refactor explicitly out of scope per the bead's 'ride alongside' framing (extracting all four agents at once would be too sprawling). Diff: 1 file modified (causal-agent.ts: -50 +13), 1 file added (reasoning-agent.ts: 81 lines). Test: src/test/services/causal-agent-timeout.test.ts — all 6 cases pass against the re-exported symbols. Pre-existing pi-agent-bridge.test.ts failure (create_contradiction missing from EXPECTED_WRITE_TOOLS) reproduces on baseline — unrelated.

title: (BUG) reasoning_report_id FK columns lack explicit ON DELETE — default RESTRICT silently blocks future pruning; tests already work around it
description:
Three FK columns reference `public.reasoning_reports(id)` without an explicit ON DELETE clause. PostgreSQL defaults to NO ACTION (effectively RESTRICT at commit time). Nobody declared the policy — it's a non-decision that bites only at deletion time.

## Affected columns

- `src/db/migrations/009_audit_trail.sql:36` — `fact_history.reasoning_report_id   UUID REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id)`
- `src/db/migrations/009_audit_trail.sql:82` — `causal_edge_history.reasoning_report_id   UUID REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id)`
- `src/db/migrations/011_contradictions.sql:57` — `contradictions.resolution_report_id   UUID REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id)`

All three columns are nullable. Non-agent actors (user, system_trigger, cascade) already write history rows with NULL `reasoning_report_id`, so the column legitimately holds NULL.

## Evidence of current fragility

`src/test/harness/contradictions.test.ts:67-69` carries a workaround that names this exact constraint:

```
// reasoning_reports is not in deleteFromTables's canonical order; clear it
// here because Phase 5 resolutions can link to it via resolution_report_id.
await testDb.unsafe('DELETE FROM public.reasoning_reports');
```

Tests have to hand-maintain a cleanup order because the constraint blocks teardown unless reasoning_reports is wiped before the referencing tables. This is a smell — not a load-bearing bug, but it points at the unstated policy.

## Right policy is ON DELETE SET NULL

The history tables are the audit trail. They must survive even if a report is pruned for storage. CASCADE is the wrong direction (it would silently destroy audit rows). NO ACTION (current default) prevents the prune. SET NULL preserves the audit row while acknowledging the provenance link is gone.

The "Explicit Over Implicit" principle in `docs/architecture/truth-graph/10-reasoning-layer-overview.md` already documents the design stance: "every history row carries the `actor`, the `reasoning`, and the `reasoning_report_id` that caused it." That principle is consistent with SET NULL — the column is the link, not the parent.

## Production impact today

Zero. No production code path deletes `reasoning_reports` rows. This is a latent-defect finding — the constraint never fires in prod because the action never happens. But:

1. Tests already feel the friction (workaround at contradictions.test.ts:67-69).
2. Any future "prune old reasoning reports" cleanup hits the wall — storage pressure isn't a concern now, but it's the type of feature that lands later.
3. Migration cost is tiny: three `ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY (...) REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` statements in one new migration.

## Proposed fix

New migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.fact_history
  DROP CONSTRAINT fact_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey,
  ADD CONSTRAINT fact_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey
    FOREIGN KEY (reasoning_report_id) REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

ALTER TABLE public.causal_edge_history
  DROP CONSTRAINT causal_edge_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey,
  ADD CONSTRAINT causal_edge_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey
    FOREIGN KEY (reasoning_report_id) REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

ALTER TABLE public.contradictions
  DROP CONSTRAINT contradictions_resolution_report_id_fkey,
  ADD CONSTRAINT contradictions_resolution_report_id_fkey
    FOREIGN KEY (resolution_report_id) REFERENCES public.reasoning_reports(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
```

Adjust constraint names to whatever the migrations actually generated. Verify the exact names via `\d public.fact_history` (or pg_constraint) before writing the migration.

After the migration, the workaround at `contradictions.test.ts:67-69` becomes unnecessary — `deleteFromTables` can include reasoning_reports in its canonical order without the dependency dance.

## Cross-references

- Carry-forward theme T10 (deferred-default schema policies that bite later — different shape from merge_entities paper-cuts but same family).
- nmemo-2yv.69 (missing CHECK constraints on gardening_reports.trigger_type and merge_candidates.candidate_source — different defect class, also schema hardening; consider bundling into one migration PR for efficiency).
- docs/architecture/truth-graph/10-reasoning-layer-overview.md "Explicit Over Implicit" principle — articulates the design stance that supports SET NULL.
acceptance_criteria:
- New migration drops the three implicit-RESTRICT FK constraints and recreates them with ON DELETE SET NULL.
- Constraint names verified against pg_constraint (or \d output) before the migration is written — DROP CONSTRAINT must match the actual generated name.
- contradictions.test.ts workaround at line 67-69 removed; reasoning_reports added to deleteFromTables canonical order.
- Regression test: DELETE from reasoning_reports succeeds when fact_history rows reference it; fact_history rows survive with reasoning_report_id = NULL.
- No production behaviour change today (no caller deletes reports); change is purely policy-explicit + future-proofing.
notes:
Closed by bead/92 commit 7011d65. Migration 033_reasoning_report_fk_on_delete_set_null.sql replaces the implicit NO ACTION policy with ON DELETE SET NULL on all three FK columns referencing public.reasoning_reports(id):
- fact_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey
- causal_edge_history_reasoning_report_id_fkey
- contradictions_resolution_report_id_fkey

Verified pg_constraint confdeltype='n' on all three (was 'a' pre-fix). DELETE FROM reasoning_reports now nulls the referrer columns instead of raising. reasoning_reports added to deleteFromTables's canonical order (src/test/setup.ts); the hand-maintained DELETE workaround at the old contradictions.test.ts cleanSlate removed. New regression test src/test/harness/reasoning-report-fk-on-delete.test.ts locks all three behaviours.

Production impact today: zero — no caller deletes reasoning_reports rows. The change is policy-explicit + future-proofing for any storage-pressure prune that might land later. Aligns with the 'Explicit Over Implicit' principle in docs/architecture/truth-graph/10-reasoning-layer-overview.md.

Pre-existing flake unrelated to this bead: 'Phase 5 — fixture-driven: opposing-object-exclusive' fails on both pre- and post-fix runs (row_count(contradictions): expected 0, got 1). Same 57/58 pass count under stash. Not introduced here.

Acceptance criteria:
- Migration drops + recreates the three FK constraints with ON DELETE SET NULL [done].
- Constraint names verified against pg_constraint before migration written (matched the predicted *_fkey shape) [done].
- contradictions.test.ts workaround removed; reasoning_reports added to deleteFromTables order [done].
- Regression test: DELETE reasoning_reports succeeds + history rows survive with NULL reasoning_report_id [done].
- No production behaviour change [done — only behavioural diff is on the unexercised DELETE path].
close_reason: Migration 033 + regression test landed; see notes.

title: save_reasoning_report has no server-side idempotency — multiple agent calls create duplicate rows (and the tool description's 'break patrol cooldown' line is misleading)
description:
The "save a report exactly once per pass" contract is enforced entirely by hope. The TS handler at `src/services/causal-agent.ts:1797-1810` inserts a new `reasoning_reports` row on every call — no idempotency key, no session check, no dedup window. The guidance is in three prompt locations:

- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:663` — tool description: "Save a reasoning report ONCE at the very end of a reasoning pass. Call this exactly one time per /api/reason invocation — multiple calls create duplicate rows and break patrol cooldown."
- `ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:296` — "Call save_reasoning_report ONCE — and only once — at the very end of the pass"
- `ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:327` — "9. ALWAYS REPORT — EXACTLY ONCE: Every reasoning pass MUST end with save_reasoning_report, called once. Multiple saves per pass create duplicate rows and break patrol cooldown."

LLM nondeterminism (rare but real over a 100-tool-call budget), retry logic added by future maintainers, or a sloppy refactor on the python side can each produce a double-save.

## Downstream impact when duplicates happen

- Duplicate rows in `reasoning_reports` — cosmetic clutter.
- `get_reasoning_history` returns more results than expected — slight prompt-context pollution on subsequent patrols.
- `entity_meta.last_reasoned_at` set twice in succession — harmless overwrite.
- `fact_history.reasoning_report_id` (set during the reasoning pass via tool calls like `update_fact_confidence`) references whichever save row was current at the time of the mutation. If a second save is inserted afterwards, the FK refs point at the first row while the second row sits orphaned. Provenance fragments.

## The "break patrol cooldown" line is misleading

`pipeline.ts` patrol-success counters (`incrementPatrolCount`, `incrementGraphStatsCount`) fire from the HTTP-wrapper edge (`src/services/causal-agent.ts:2266-2270`), not from `save_reasoning_report`. They advance once per /api/reason invocation regardless of how many times save_reasoning_report fires inside the pass. So "break patrol cooldown" doesn't actually describe a real consequence of duplicate saves — duplicate rows don't make pattern detection or graph-stats fire faster.

Fix the tool description and the python prompt either to drop the claim, or to point at the actual consequence (provenance fragmentation, get_reasoning_history pollution).

## Proposed fix (option A, agreed with user 2026-05-19): idempotency key

Pass an idempotency key from the platform's /api/reason endpoint through to the python agent, have the agent forward it on save_reasoning_report, and have the TS handler upsert on the key.

Layer-by-layer:

1. **`/api/reason` and `/api/reason/query`** (`src/index.ts:944-972`) — generate a UUID per invocation; include in the `invokeReasoningAgent` params.
2. **`invokeReasoningAgent`** (`src/services/causal-agent.ts:2238`) — forward the key in the POST body to ml-services as `invocation_id` or `idempotency_key`.
3. **`ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py`** — receive the key, render it into the agent's system prompt as a piece of context (e.g., "Your invocation id for this pass is `<uuid>`. Pass it on save_reasoning_report as `invocation_id`.").
4. **Tool input schema** (`src/services/causal-agent.ts:660-702`) — add optional `invocation_id` string field.
5. **TS handler** (`src/services/causal-agent.ts:1797-1810`) — when `invocation_id` is present, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (invocation_id) DO UPDATE SET report = EXCLUDED.report, entity_ids = EXCLUDED.entity_ids, fact_ids = EXCLUDED.fact_ids, causal_edge_ids = EXCLUDED.causal_edge_ids, actions_taken = EXCLUDED.actions_taken. Returns the same row ID across duplicate calls.
6. **Schema** — `reasoning_reports.invocation_id UUID UNIQUE` (nullable for backfill; new migration). Index on the column.

Backwards compatibility: when `invocation_id` is absent (legacy callers or test fixtures), keep the current INSERT behaviour. The constraint is UNIQUE-where-NOT-NULL via a partial index.

## Cross-references

- nmemo-2yv.76 (timeout/cancellation on invokeReasoningAgent) — fix in the same area; touch the same file.
- nmemo-2yv.71 (auto-trigger work) — if patrol acquires multiple anchors (post-ingest counter, time-based, etc), the idempotency key gains importance because retry/race conditions become more plausible.
acceptance_criteria:
- New migration adds reasoning_reports.invocation_id UUID column + UNIQUE partial index (WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL).
- /api/reason and /api/reason/query generate a UUID per invocation and forward to invokeReasoningAgent.
- invokeReasoningAgent forwards the key to ml-services in the POST body.
- ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py renders the key into the agent's prompt as the invocation_id to use when calling save_reasoning_report.
- save_reasoning_report tool input schema accepts invocation_id (optional, string UUID).
- TS handler does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (invocation_id) DO UPDATE when the key is present; legacy INSERT path retained when absent.
- Tool description and python prompt "break patrol cooldown" lines corrected to reflect actual consequence (provenance fragmentation, get_reasoning_history pollution) or dropped.
- Regression test: call save_reasoning_report twice with the same invocation_id; verify a single row exists and the second call updated the fields without inserting.
notes:
Implemented option A (idempotency key) per the bead's proposed fix.

Migration 034 adds reasoning_reports.invocation_id UUID with a partial unique index (WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL). Nullable so legacy callers (older python clients, direct handleToolCall consumers, ad-hoc fixtures) keep working with the existing INSERT path; uniqueness enforced only when the platform threads a key through.

Wiring layer-by-layer:
- /api/reason + /api/reason/query mint a UUID per HTTP call via randomUUID() (new import in src/index.ts).
- invokeReasoningAgent forwards invocation_id to ml-services in the POST body. ReasoningAgentParams gained an optional invocationId field.
- reasoning_agent.py's ReasoningRequest accepts invocation_id; _build_reasoning_prompt renders it into the system prompt header with explicit instruction to pass it through verbatim on save_reasoning_report.
- save_reasoning_report tool schema gained an optional invocation_id string. Tool description rewritten to drop the misleading "break patrol cooldown" claim (the patrol counters fire from invokeReasoningAgent on /api/reason success, not from save_reasoning_report — duplicate saves don't influence them) and replaced with the actual consequence: provenance fragmentation + get_reasoning_history pollution.
- TS handler branches on invocation_id presence: when present, raw-SQL UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (invocation_id) WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET ...) returning the existing id; when absent, the legacy drizzle INSERT path. Drizzle 0.29's onConflictDoUpdate doesn't support partial-index inference (no `targetWhere`), so the UPSERT branch is raw SQL using the `{uuid,...}` array-literal pattern already canonical in this codebase (causal-patterns.ts:639). JSONB columns pass through as objects (postgres lib auto-serialises).

Python prompt principle 9 also updated — the "Multiple saves per pass create duplicate rows and break patrol cooldown" line now describes the UPSERT safety net plus the real downstream cost (history rows reference whichever save was current; second save sits orphaned).

Regression tests added to causal-agent-tools.test.ts:
- save_reasoning_report dedupes on invocation_id across duplicate calls: proves two calls with the same key return the same id, exactly one row exists, second call's payload overwrites the first's.
- save_reasoning_report without invocation_id still inserts a fresh row each call: proves legacy back-compat — different ids returned, two rows created.

All 15 tests in causal-agent-tools.test.ts pass. The existing F3 regression (save_reasoning_report sets last_reasoned_at on every referenced entity) still passes — both code paths share the entity_meta update.

Pre-existing failure on src/test/services/pi-agent-bridge.test.ts ("expected write tools are flagged mutates: true") is unrelated to this bead — `create_contradiction` was added by earlier work and the EXPECTED_WRITE_TOOLS set wasn't refreshed. Verified by git stash + test rerun: same failure on the pre-change baseline.

Acceptance criteria coverage:
- ✓ New migration adds reasoning_reports.invocation_id UUID column + UNIQUE partial index (WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL).
- ✓ /api/reason and /api/reason/query generate a UUID per invocation and forward to invokeReasoningAgent.
- ✓ invokeReasoningAgent forwards the key to ml-services in the POST body.
- ✓ ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py renders the key into the agent's prompt as the invocation_id to use when calling save_reasoning_report.
- ✓ save_reasoning_report tool input schema accepts invocation_id (optional, string UUID).
- ✓ TS handler does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (invocation_id) DO UPDATE when the key is present; legacy INSERT path retained when absent.
- ✓ Tool description and python prompt "break patrol cooldown" lines corrected to reflect actual consequence.
- ✓ Regression test: call save_reasoning_report twice with the same invocation_id; verify a single row exists and the second call updated the fields without inserting.

Cruft IGNORE noted. Closed out as part of nmemo-2yv epic.

title: actions_taken structured-shape is half-implemented — strip the python prompt instruction and schema comment to freeform JSONB
description:
The `reasoning_reports.actions_taken` JSONB column documents a four-key structured shape (`{expired, created_facts, created_edges, updated_summaries}`) at three places: the schema comment, the schema.ts type doc, and the python reasoning agent's system prompt. Nothing in the codebase enforces or consumes that shape.

## Falsifying evidence

Producer instruction (only one):
- `ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:264` — prompt tells the agent: `actions_taken: {expired: [...], created_facts: [...], created_edges: [...], updated_summaries: [...]}`
- `ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:296,327` — repeated "Call save_reasoning_report ONCE" guidance, treating the structured log as part of the final aggregate.

Enforcement (none):
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:695-698` — tool input schema: `actions_taken: { type: 'object', description: 'Structured log of actions' }`. No required keys, no per-key item types.
- `src/db/migrations/008_reasoning_reports.sql:21` — `actions_taken JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`. No CHECK, no constraint, no jsonb_typeof gating.
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:1809` — handler passes `toolInput.actions_taken ?? {}` straight through.

Consumers (none):
- Grep on `actions_taken|actionsTaken` across `./src/**`, `./viz/**`, `./ml-services/**`, `./scripts/**` (excluding tests and verify-f3-live) returns only writers — never a reader that touches any of the four documented keys.
- `viz/js/panels/**` — no actions_taken reference anywhere.
- The TS side surfaces `actionsTaken: r.actionsTaken` back through `get_reasoning_history` (causal-agent.ts:1793), but the only consumer of that is the agent itself — which only sees the shape it wrote.

## Why this is finding-worthy despite no live bug

The agent currently spends tokens producing structured data nobody reads. That alone is mild. The trap: when a future contributor adds a viz panel or analytics consumer that reads `actions_taken.expired`, they will get `undefined` (or KeyError on python side) for:

- Test rows: `{test: true}`, `{verify: true}`
- The `scripts/verify-f3-live.ts:43` row: `{verify: true}`
- Any legacy patrol whose agent followed the prompt imperfectly (LLM nondeterminism)
- The default `{}` for any row where the tool was invoked without supplying the field

Half-built features that quietly grow consumers without enforcement are the way schema-vs-code drift compounds. Best to either close the loop or close the door.

## Chosen direction (option A, agreed with user 2026-05-19): strip and simplify

Make `actions_taken` officially freeform JSONB. The prose `report TEXT` field is the canonical source of truth for what happened in a pass; the structured log was a "useful one day" placeholder.

Changes:
1. **Python prompt** — remove the line at `ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:264` that specifies the four-key shape. Leave the rest of the save_reasoning_report invocation guidance intact; the agent still calls the tool, it just doesn't waste tokens producing structured logs.
2. **Schema comment** — `src/db/migrations/008_reasoning_reports.sql:21` change the inline comment from `{expired: [], created_facts: [], created_edges: [], updated_summaries: []}` to something like `freeform structured log; consumer-defined`. Optionally add a header note that the column is provided for future structured-logging needs but currently has no canonical shape.
3. **schema.ts** — `src/db/schema.ts:469` if there's a comment claiming the shape, drop it.
4. **No DB migration** — still free-form JSONB. The column is untouched.
5. **Tool input schema** — leave as `{ type: 'object' }`. No tighter enforcement needed since there's no shape.

## Option B (deferred, not chosen): close the loop

For future reference if a consumer is wanted: add a viz panel surfacing "Actions in this patrol" against `actions_taken`, add JSON Schema validation at the tool input boundary, add a one-line DB CHECK on `jsonb_typeof(actions_taken->'expired') = 'array'` etc. Larger; deferred until there's a real consumer use case.

## Cross-references

- Carry-forward theme T9 (schema-vs-code vocabulary drift; this is the soft-doc variant — schema header documents intent, code does not enforce).
- Falsification rate update: I initially framed this as "schema comment is misleading"; after reading the python prompt I corrected to "instruction exists but no enforcement and no consumer".
acceptance_criteria:
- ml-services/app/reasoning_agent.py:264 structured-shape line removed; agent no longer instructed to produce the four-key shape.
- 008_reasoning_reports.sql column comment updated from the four-key shape to "freeform structured log; consumer-defined" or equivalent.
- src/db/schema.ts comment on actionsTaken (if any) updated to match.
- No new DB migration required.
- Tool input schema unchanged ({ type: 'object' }).
- The change is verifiable by grep: zero references to {expired, created_facts, created_edges, updated_summaries} remain anywhere in repo (outside this bead and possibly historical commit messages).
notes:
Landed in two commits on bead/92-cross-cluster-runs-telemetry:

- 4536ab0 — strip structured-shape line from reasoning_agent.py patrol
  mode prompt and from the save_reasoning_report tool reference
- 303c23c — update 008_reasoning_reports.sql column comment + add doc
  comment above actionsTaken in src/db/schema.ts

Verification:
- Grep across the repo for the four-key shape pattern
  ({expired, created_facts, created_edges, updated_summaries}) returns
  only .beads/issues.jsonl (this bead itself).
- Tool input schema unchanged ({type: 'object'}).
- No new DB migration required (column unchanged, comment-only edit
  in the historical migration file).

Schema.ts didn't have an inline shape comment to remove; added a
one-line "Freeform JSONB — consumer-defined, no canonical shape
enforced anywhere." comment above the column so future readers of the
Drizzle definition match the SQL header intent.

title: (BUG) reasoning_reports allows mode='query' rows with NULL question — missing CHECK constraint
description:
The schema header of `src/db/migrations/008_reasoning_reports.sql` documents the contract: "Each reasoning pass (patrol or query) produces a report linked to the entities, facts, and causal edges it touched." But the contract is enforced only at the HTTP boundary, not at the DB.

## Falsifying evidence

- `008_reasoning_reports.sql:17-18` — `mode VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('patrol', 'query'))`; `question TEXT` (nullable, no CHECK relating it to mode)
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:700` — `save_reasoning_report` tool input schema marks `question` as optional: `required: ['mode', 'report', 'entity_ids']`
- `src/services/causal-agent.ts:1797-1810` — handler accepts whatever the agent sends; passes `toolInput.question` straight through.
- `src/index.ts:957-958` — POST /api/reason/query validates `body.question` is present. HTTP layer catches the obvious case.
- `src/services/pi-agent-bridge.ts:90` — pi bridge whitelists `save_reasoning_report`. Any consumer reaching the tool through the bridge or graph-mcp bypasses the HTTP validation entirely.

If the python reasoning agent forgets to forward the user's question into the final `save_reasoning_report` call (a routine prompt-engineering footgun), the row persists with mode='query' and NULL question. Silent.

## Impact

- Silently-lost audit trail. Future patrols reading the same entity via `get_reasoning_history` see a query-mode report with no recoverable record of what the query was.
- Breaks the schema-header provenance contract.
- The agent loop can drift between "I'm in query mode" and "I have a question to record" without anyone noticing.

## Fix shape (small)

Load-bearing fix is the DB CHECK:

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.reasoning_reports
  ADD CONSTRAINT reasoning_reports_query_has_question
  CHECK (mode = 'patrol' OR (mode = 'query' AND question IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(question)) > 0));
```

Optional defence-in-depth (tool input schema): use JSON Schema `oneOf` to require `question` when `mode='query'`. Not all MCP consumers honour conditional schemas, so this is layered on top, not a substitute for the DB CHECK.

## Cross-references

- Carry-forward theme T9 (schema-vs-code vocabulary drift; schema-header comment documents contract, code does not enforce it).
- Same shape as nmemo-2yv.69 (missing CHECK constraints on gardening_reports.trigger_type and merge_candidates.candidate_source).
acceptance_criteria:
- New migration adds CHECK constraint enforcing (mode='query' implies question IS NOT NULL AND non-blank).
- Any existing rows that violate the constraint are migrated (set question to a sentinel, or the migration fails loudly until cleaned — choice recorded in the migration header).
- Regression test: attempting to INSERT (mode='query', question=NULL) raises a check_violation; (mode='query', question='') raises the same.
- /api/reason/query continues to reject empty body.question at the HTTP boundary (no behavioural change there).
notes:
RESOLVED via migration 032_reasoning_reports_query_question_check.sql + regression test src/test/harness/reasoning-reports-query-question-check.test.ts.

## Fix shape
Added CONSTRAINT reasoning_reports_query_question_required to public.reasoning_reports:
  CHECK (mode <> 'query' OR (question IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(question)) > 0))

length(trim(...)) > 0 also rejects whitespace-only questions, matching the HTTP boundary's `if (!body.question)` falsy semantics (index.ts:929).

## Acceptance criteria — all met
- ✅ New migration adds CHECK constraint enforcing mode='query' implies question IS NOT NULL AND non-blank — mig 032.
- ✅ Pre-existing-data policy recorded in migration header: fail loudly. No prod rows match broken shape today (only mode='patrol' inserts in src/: index.ts:1108, graph-stats.ts:407, contradictions test).
- ✅ Regression test asserts INSERT (mode='query', question=NULL) raises check_violation; (mode='query', question='') and (mode='query', question='   ') both raise the same. Plus positive cases: (query, non-blank) accepted; (patrol, NULL) and (patrol, non-blank) unchanged.
- ✅ /api/reason/query HTTP guard unchanged — DB CHECK is defence-in-depth catching consumers that bypass the HTTP layer (causal-agent.ts tool dispatcher, pi-agent-bridge.ts whitelist).

## Tests
All 6 tests in src/test/harness/reasoning-reports-query-question-check.test.ts pass. Migration 032 applied cleanly in test setup (verified `✅ 032_reasoning_reports_query_question_check.sql` in global-setup output).

## Sibling pattern
Mirrors bead nmemo-2yv.69 (valid_trigger_type, mig 031) and nmemo-2yv.93 (valid_candidate_source, mig 030) — same T9 schema-vs-code drift theme.

title: Add missing CHECK constraints on gardening_reports.trigger_type and merge_candidates.candidate_source
description:
Premise: Two reconciliation/gardening surface columns document enums in COMMENT but lack CHECK constraints; sibling columns on the same tables enforce theirs.

Falsifying test run:
- mig 006_gardening.sql:13: 'trigger_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT "manual"  -- "manual" | "auto"'. No CHECK.
- mig 017_candidate_source.sql:21: 'candidate_source VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT "three_signal_scoring"' (comment in header lists 'three_signal_scoring' and 'cross_cluster_generator'). No CHECK.
- mig 003_graph_meta.sql:67,70: merge_candidates.status and merge_candidates.resolution BOTH have CHECK constraints (valid_candidate_status and valid_resolution). The pattern is inconsistent within the same table on the same review surface.

Result: Mismatch between documented enum and enforced enum. A typo or new value lands silently.

Impact:
- ml-services/app/reconciliation_agent.py _build_reconciliation_prompt at line 187-188 does exact-string equality on candidate_source ('three_signal_scoring' vs 'cross_cluster_generator'). A typo on the write side leaks an unsplit candidate into a default block — silent miscategorisation, no error.
- Any future analytics over gardening_reports.trigger_type would silently miscount on a typo.
- Combined with nmemo-2yv.60's enum/CHECK alignment, this is the same review (#7) finding pattern at a smaller scale: schema-level vocabulary should be enforced.

Scoped fix:
1. New migration adds:
   - CONSTRAINT valid_trigger_type CHECK (trigger_type IN ('manual', 'auto')) on gardening_reports.
   - CONSTRAINT valid_candidate_source CHECK (candidate_source IN ('three_signal_scoring', 'cross_cluster_generator')) on merge_candidates.
2. Pre-flight: SELECT DISTINCT trigger_type FROM gardening_reports and SELECT DISTINCT candidate_source FROM merge_candidates to confirm existing rows are in-bounds before adding the constraint.
3. If any out-of-bounds rows exist (e.g. silent typos), the migration script must fix them before adding the constraint — fail-loud, don't drop.

Acceptance:
- Both constraints are present and enforced. Attempts to INSERT/UPDATE with out-of-enum values raise constraint violations.
- Existing data passes the constraint.

Future direction (synthesis): Sweep all VARCHAR columns across migrations for missing CHECK constraints on documented enums. Many candidates likely exist beyond this review's surface.

title: entity-profile.ts hardening: log Qdrant failures + DISTINCT in getEntityMemories
description:
Two small hardening gaps in entity-profile.ts.

=== H6 — Qdrant errors are swallowed silently ===

Premise: getEntityMemories at entity-profile.ts:67-86 wraps qdrant.retrieve in try/catch and returns [] on any error. No logging, no metric, no signal at all:

  try {
    const points = await qdrant.retrieve(COLLECTIONS.MEMORIES, { ... });
    return points.map(...);
  } catch {
    // Qdrant may be unavailable
    return [];
  }

Falsifying test run:
  Read entity-profile.ts:67-86

Result: bare catch block, comment-only acknowledgement, no logger call, no telemetry hook.

Impact: A persistent Qdrant outage looks like "this entity has no recent memories" to every consumer. The .51 endpoint will report empty memories. The .52 viz panel will render "no recent mentions" when the actual cause is infrastructure failure. Debugging requires finding the Qdrant logs separately — no breadcrumb in the application logs ties the empty result to the upstream failure.

Scoped fix:
  - Log the caught error at warn level with a stable message ("entity-profile.getEntityMemories: qdrant.retrieve failed", { entityId, error }).
  - Use whichever logger the project already standardises on (grep platform/src/ for the convention before adding a new one).
  - Behaviour stays the same (still return [] for graceful degradation) — only telemetry is added.

Acceptance:
  - With qdrant.retrieve throwing in a test, getEntityMemories logs a warn-level message containing the entity_id and the underlying error, then returns [].

=== H8 — getEntityMemories underdelivers on multi-mention entities ===

Premise: The query at entity-profile.ts:57-62 selects memoryId from memoryEntities without DISTINCT:

  db.select({ memoryId: memoryEntities.memoryId })
    .from(memoryEntities)
    .where(eq(memoryEntities.entityId, entityId))
    .orderBy(desc(memoryEntities.createdAt))
    .limit(limit);

Schema: 001_consolidated.sql:121-122 shows the unique index is on (memory_id, entity_id, COALESCE(mention_start, -1)). So the same (memory_id, entity_id) pair CAN appear multiple times if the entity is mentioned at multiple offsets in one memory.

Falsifying test run:
  Read 001_consolidated.sql:121-122
  Read entity-profile.ts:57-72

Result: Multiple mention_start rows are not deduplicated before LIMIT consumes them. If "Bruce" is mentioned 3 times in memory M1 (at offsets 10, 200, 500), the SELECT with limit=10 grabs those 3 rows plus 7 others; qdrant.retrieve dedupes IDs server-side and returns 8 points; the user asked for 10 and gets 8 distinct memories.

Impact: Heavily-mentioned hub entities (the most narratively interesting cases) silently return fewer recent memories than the caller requested. The bug is invisible because it manifests as "slightly fewer results than expected" rather than an error.

Scoped fix:
  - Change the SELECT to deduplicate by memory_id. Options:
      (a) SELECT DISTINCT memoryId — but DISTINCT + ORDER BY desc(createdAt) interacts oddly with the link's createdAt column (which row's createdAt wins?). Drizzle equivalent: db.selectDistinct({...}). Behaviour: keeps the memory but loses the "ordered by most recent link creation" guarantee unless ORDER BY is also on memoryId.
      (b) Subquery: SELECT memoryId FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (memory_id) memory_id, created_at FROM memory_entities WHERE entity_id = $1 ORDER BY memory_id, created_at DESC) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $2 — preserves the "most recent" semantics correctly.
      (c) Application-level dedup: select with a larger limit (e.g. limit * 3), dedupe in JS, then slice to limit. Cheap; slightly wasteful; doesn't guarantee N results if mention density is extreme.
    Recommend (b) as the most correct; fall back to (c) if Drizzle's DISTINCT ON support is too awkward.

Acceptance:
  - With a fixture where entity E is mentioned 5 times in memory M1 and once each in M2-M11, getEntityMemories(E, { limit: 10 }) returns 10 distinct memories (M1, M2, ..., M10), not just 6 due to M1 dedup.

Future direction: Both H6 and H8 are observability/correctness fixes that benefit from being landed alongside the .56 fixture work — the fixtures provide the conditions to test these paths.

title: computed_duration_ms written outside transaction in computeGraphStats
description:
Premise: graph-stats.ts:228-231 issues a separate UPDATE public.graph_stats SET computed_duration_ms = ... after the transaction at lines 129-222 commits. The duration write is not atomic with the upsert.

Falsifying test run:
  Read src/services/graph-stats.ts:126-234.
  Confirmed: transaction at 129-222 returns upserted row; separate UPDATE at line 229-231 runs against the pool.
  Read src/test/harness/graph-stats.test.ts:217-233 (idempotency test) → explicitly excludes computed_duration_ms ("self-reported durations are *expected* to change").

Result: confirmed non-atomic. Asymmetry acknowledged but not minimised.

Impact:
- Process death between commit and the post-transaction UPDATE leaves new aggregate columns with stale duration_ms from the prior run. Observational data only — no correctness consequence.
- Two roundtrips when one would suffice.
- Slightly weakens the per-row consistency guarantee of the singleton.

Scoped fix — two options for the implementer:
  (a) Move the UPDATE inside the existing db.transaction block. After the upsert returns, compute durationMs from the JS-side Date.now(), then issue UPDATE within the same tx. One extra roundtrip but atomic.
  (b) Compute duration in SQL via clock_timestamp() - statement_timestamp() within the CTE. Zero extra roundtrip; the duration is measured server-side and atomic with the upsert. Most idiomatic. Slightly more SQL complexity.

Acceptance:
- Process death between any two phases of computeGraphStats cannot produce drift between aggregate columns and computed_duration_ms.
- Test added: kill the connection mid-compute (or simulate via injected pre-commit failure); verify that on next read, no row has new aggregates with stale duration.
- Idempotency test (graph-stats.test.ts:217) may now compare computed_duration_ms (option b) or continues to exclude it (option a).
notes:
[2026-05-27] APPLIED: option (a) — moved duration UPDATE inside db.transaction block. src/services/graph-stats.ts:126-241 restructured: tx callback now does upsert, computes durationMs = Date.now() - start, issues duration UPDATE within same tx, returns spliced row. Rationale: option (a) preserves the full-call wall-clock semantic; option (b) (clock_timestamp() in SQL) would have silently narrowed the metric to just the INSERT statement duration.
[2026-05-27] VERIFIED: new test src/test/harness/graph-stats.test.ts:240-296 (test 11 atomicity) passes. Uses BEFORE UPDATE trigger with NEW.computed_duration_ms IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.computed_duration_ms predicate to RAISE on the duration-write statement only; verifies aggregate columns AND computed_duration_ms both stay at pre-compute values after the failed call. 4 pre-existing test failures (tests 2/3/4/8) confirmed unrelated via git-stash verify pass on base — they are merge_candidates/entity_meta cleanSlate gaps not in scope for this bead.
