title: detectContradictions Promise.all aborts whole sweep on one heuristic failure — switch to per-heuristic isolation + errors in DetectionResult
description:
Premise: detectContradictions runs the four SQL heuristics under Promise.all (contradictions.ts:278-283). If any single heuristic rejects (transient DB error, statement timeout, lock contention, future query bug), Promise.all aborts the whole batch — the other three heuristics' work is discarded. Pipeline auto-trigger and HTTP /api/contradictions/detect both lose the entire sweep on a single-heuristic failure, with no observability into which heuristic actually failed.

Falsifying test run:
  - Read platform/src/services/contradictions.ts lines 277-295: Promise.all wraps all four detectors; aggregate count = simple sum
  - Read platform/src/pipeline.ts lines 313-324: try/catch logs `[contradictions] auto-detect failed: <err.message>` — no per-heuristic context
  - Read platform/src/index.ts lines 622-651: POST /api/contradictions/detect catch block returns HTTP 500 with the error string when the Promise rejects
  - No test exercises a partial-failure path (one heuristic throws, others succeed)

Result:
  - One blip → all four heuristics' results discarded
  - Caller logs a generic `[contradictions] auto-detect failed: <message>` with no signal about which heuristic broke
  - HTTP caller receives 500 with raw error string and no partial detection counts
  - Re-run on next pipeline tick recovers, so this manifests as observability gaps + transient detection lag

Impact:
  - Lost detection sweep per blip (detection lag of one DECAY_RUN_INTERVAL tick)
  - HTTP triggers (viz button, agent manual trigger) get 500 without knowing whether any contradictions were detected before the blip
  - Pipeline log doesn't say which heuristic failed — operator debugging is harder than it needs to be
  - Future regression in one heuristic's query (e.g., a Postgres version upgrade changes plan behaviour for the cyclic join) takes down all detection until the regression is found

Scoped fix (Option C — per-heuristic try/catch + errors in DetectionResult):
  1. platform/src/services/contradictions.ts:
     - Extend DetectionResult: add optional `errors?: Partial<Record<ContradictionType, string>>` field
     - Replace Promise.all with per-heuristic safeRun wrapper that try/catches and returns either { ok: true, count } or { ok: false, error: string }
     - Aggregate `detected` sums only successful counts
     - Populate `byType[type]` only on success (omit on failure — symmetric with current "if (count > 0)" behaviour)
     - Populate `errors[type]` on failure with the error message
     - Per-heuristic console.warn with named context: `[contradictions] <type> heuristic failed: <message>`
  2. platform/src/pipeline.ts:
     - The pipeline-level try/catch around detectContradictions() can stay (defensive), but the inner orchestrator now never throws — the pipeline log line gets richer:
       `[contradictions] auto-detect complete detected=N byType=... errors=...`
     - When errors is non-empty: log warn lines per heuristic listing the failures
  3. platform/src/index.ts (POST /api/contradictions/detect):
     - Drop the try/catch around detectContradictions() — orchestrator no longer throws
     - Return shape: { triggered: true, detected, byType, errors?, durationMs }
     - HTTP 200 even when errors is non-empty — partial success is communicated via the errors field, not the status code
     - Keep a top-level try/catch for unexpected non-heuristic errors (DB connection lost mid-orchestrator etc.) — those still return 500
  4. Test (contradictions.test.ts new section "partial heuristic failure"):
     - Use vitest's vi.spyOn to make detectCyclicCausal throw once
     - Call detectContradictions(); assert detected sums only successful heuristics
     - Assert result.errors.cyclic_causal contains the simulated message
     - Assert result.byType doesn't include cyclic_causal
     - Restore the mock; assert next call succeeds normally
  5. Test: HTTP endpoint returns 200 with errors field when one heuristic fails (use same vi.spyOn shape)
  6. Doc 16: no spec change required (the new errors field is an additive observability surface; the heuristics' contract is unchanged)

Acceptance:
  - One simulated heuristic failure does not abort the other three
  - DetectionResult.errors populated per failed heuristic with the error message
  - POST /api/contradictions/detect returns 200 with errors field on partial failure (not 500)
  - Pipeline log emits per-heuristic warn lines naming the failing heuristic
  - Existing tests pass without modification (errors field is optional, omitted on full success)
  - New tests cover partial-failure path at service + HTTP layers

Future direction (note for end-of-review synthesis, not part of this bead's scope):
  Per-heuristic error rates become a telemetry surface — if cyclic_causal starts failing 5% of the time, that's a hint of either a real query regression or an ambient DB issue worth investigating. Worth surfacing in the viz stats panel alongside the badge counts: "errors last hour: cyclic_causal: 3". Phase 6+ observability layer.

description:

title: (DOC) doc 03 §5.3 uses wrong extraction_method sentinels ('inferred'/'explicit') — code uses ('llm'/'user')
description:
Premise: docs/architecture/truth-graph/03-graph-c-technical-design.md §5.3 references extraction_method values 'inferred' and 'explicit'. The code uses 'llm' (default) and 'user'. The schema has no CHECK constraint, so the typo class isn't caught at write time.

Falsifying test run:
  Grep pattern="extraction_method|extractionMethod" path=platform/src (excluding test/)
  Read docs/architecture/truth-graph/03-graph-c-technical-design.md lines 116, 605-626

Result:
  Schema (002_causal_graph.sql:121): VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, no CHECK
  causal.ts:270 default: 'llm'
  facts.ts:64 default: 'llm'
  causal.ts:646 decay filter: extraction_method = 'llm'
  Tests use 'llm' and 'user'

  Doc 03 §1.1 line 116: "llm (Haiku agentic reasoning)" — suggests single value 'llm', no other sentinel mentioned
  Doc 03 §5.3 line 614: "WHERE extraction_method = 'inferred'" decay SQL
  Doc 03 §5.3 line 626: "extraction_method = 'explicit' do not decay"

Impact:
  - Anyone implementing decay-related work from doc 03 §5.3 will write the wrong sentinel ('inferred') and quietly break the filter — the decay would skip ALL edges because no row has that value.
  - Schema permits typos to silently land (no CHECK).
  - Internal doc inconsistency: §1.1 implies one sentinel, §5.3 implies two different sentinels. Three different value sets across one doc.

Scoped fix:
  1. Decide canonical sentinels. Recommendation: keep what code uses — ('llm', 'user'). 'llm' = agent-asserted (decay-eligible); 'user' = user-asserted (no decay).
  2. Add CHECK constraint via a new migration:
       ALTER TABLE public.causal_edges
       ADD CONSTRAINT valid_extraction_method
       CHECK (extraction_method IN ('llm', 'user'));
  3. Rewrite doc 03 §5.3 SQL and prose to use the canonical pair.
  4. Tighten doc 03 §1.1 to enumerate both values explicitly.

Acceptance:
  - Schema CHECK exists on causal_edges.extraction_method
  - Doc 03 §1.1 and §5.3 both reference the same two sentinels ('llm', 'user')
  - tsc + tests pass after adding the CHECK migration

title: (DOC) doc 03 §5.2 "Cascading Invalidation" is stale — superseded by doc 13 Part C
description:
Premise: docs/architecture/truth-graph/03-graph-c-technical-design.md §5.2 describes a 4-step cascade (mark event expired → mark edges expired on cause-or-effect linkage → re-evaluate downstream → update pattern counts). This was the Phase B design. Doc 13 Part C "Cascade Invalidation" later hardened the cascade into a 2-behaviour citation-based shape (weaken if corroboration_count > 1, expire if = 1; source_references citation lookup). The code in services/causal.ts:484 (cascadeFactExpiry) matches doc 13. Doc 03 §5.2 was never updated to reflect the supersession.

Scoped fix:
  1. Diff doc 03 §5.2 against doc 13 Part C. Identify any content in doc 03 §5.2 that is NOT covered in doc 13 (e.g. high-level rationale for why cascade exists, or commentary on second-order effects).
  2. For each unique piece of content: merge it into the appropriate section of doc 13 (likely Part C "Rationale" or as an addendum).
  3. Only AFTER merging useful content: either rewrite doc 03 §5.2 to be a short pointer at doc 13, or delete the section entirely. Choice depends on whether the doc 03 chapter still reads coherently without it.
  4. Update README.md table of contents if needed.

Rule: do not delete content that's useful — merge into doc 13 first.

Acceptance:
  - No content unique to doc 03 §5.2 is lost

  - Both docs agree on the cascade shape

title: AGE edge SET drops fact metadata; trigger_sync_fact does dead work
description:
Per CLAUDE.md, AGE silently drops `MERGE (a)-[r:REL]->(b) SET r.prop = value`. `trigger_sync_fact` -> `create_entity_edge` passes `jsonb_build_object('fact_id', NEW.id, 'confidence', NEW.confidence, 'valid_at', NEW.valid_at)` as edge props, all of which are silently dropped.

Two options:
1. Remove the props payload from create_entity_edge — clearer that AGE is just a traversal index
2. Document the limitation inline in create_entity_edge and keep the params for future AGE versions

Either way the trigger is misleading as written.

Acceptance: trigger_sync_fact either documented as edge-only-sync, or the props parameter removed.
notes:
Landed on bead/92-cross-cluster-runs-telemetry as commit 2d07ff2.

Scoped fix applied per locked spec:
- Removed `p_props JSONB DEFAULT '{}'` param from create_entity_edge (signature now 3-arg: UUID, UUID, VARCHAR).
- Removed jsonb_build_object('fact_id', ..., 'confidence', ..., 'valid_at', ...) call from trigger_sync_fact.
- Added 5-line comment block above create_entity_edge documenting AGE-as-traversal-index intent + MERGE-time-properties workaround for any future AGE-native filtered traversal need.

Acceptance: trigger_sync_fact either documented as edge-only-sync, or the props parameter removed.
→ Both: param removed AND comment added documenting the AGE limitation.

/code-review on diff: clean (no correctness findings).
/simplify on diff: clean (nothing to scrub — diff is a pure dead-code removal + comment).

Forward-only migration note: Postgres CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION does NOT replace across arity changes — it creates an orphan overload. The old 4-arg `create_entity_edge(UUID, UUID, VARCHAR, JSONB)` may persist alongside the new 3-arg form on long-lived DBs that ran the earlier migration; no current caller invokes the 4-arg signature. Test DBs recreate on schema changes, so test environment unaffected. No explicit DROP FUNCTION was added because the bead notes anticipated this as a forward-only migration.

Lessons logged in docs/architecture/truth-graph/33-implementation-lessons.md entry for nmemo-2yv.21 — covering (a) dead-seam-vs-document tradeoff, (b) CREATE OR REPLACE arity-change pitfall, (c) pairing dead-code-removal beads with file-adjacent bug beads (.17 + .21 both touched 001_consolidated.sql AGE functions in the same week).

title: AGE sync functions silently swallow all exceptions
description:
`sync_entity_to_graph`, `create_entity_edge`, `find_entity_paths`, `get_entity_neighbors` (in 001_consolidated.sql) all use `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL` / `RETURN`. Missing AGE nodes/edges and traversal failures are unobservable.

Impact: Graph traversal silently returns empty results when AGE is broken. Sync errors during entity insert are dropped.

Fix: Replace bare exception handler with targeted exception handling (catch only AGE-specific error codes like `feature_not_supported`, `undefined_function`) and emit a NOTICE / RAISE WARNING for everything else. Optionally surface failures via a counters table.

Acceptance: AGE sync errors are logged. Traversal failures distinguishable from empty-result.
notes:
Verified 2026-05-13. All four functions confirmed bare-catch in migration 001_consolidated.sql:
- sync_entity_to_graph (line 419-433): EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL
- create_entity_edge (line 436-452): EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL
- find_entity_paths (line 455-469): EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN
- get_entity_neighbors (line 472-485): EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN

Downgraded to P3. AGE is described in CLAUDE.md as "a traversal index — canonical data lives in PostgreSQL tables." So AGE outage degrades traversal but never loses data. The bare catches are intentional defense against AGE's known quirks (edge SET drop, search_path traps).

Scoped fix (instead of strict re-raise):
- Replace bare NULL with RAISE WARNING 'AGE sync failed: %', SQLERRM
- OR add last_age_sync_error TEXT on public.entity_meta and populate it from the sync triggers so failures are queryable from SQL

title: Learn schema + test housekeeping: bound overlay/notes growth, prune dead JSON columns, learn-side test harness
description:
# Learn Schema + Test Housekeeping

Five concrete debt items identified in the learn platform, with confirmed-dead status on `quizAttempts.nmemoUpdates` via codebase grep:

## 1. Unbounded Overlay Growth (~100–500 rows/learner/year)
`lesson_overlays` table grows without compaction policy. Every `applyEditOp` call creates a new row. A learner actively editing lessons will accumulate hundreds of rows per section over months. Schema has UNIQUE(learner_id, section_id, version) and indexes, but no retention logic. Current footprint: negligible for POC (< 10K rows), but will scale into a scaling bottleneck post-launch.

**Status: Active debt. Requires policy + compaction job.**

## 2. Notes Archive Gap (~100–1000 rows/learner/year)  
`notes` table has no soft-delete or archive flag. Once `promoted_to_graph=1`, rows are essentially zombie data—shown in API calls, taking storage, but no user action can remove them. Dashboard has no filter to hide promoted notes from the note-creation surface. 

**Status: Active design debt. Functional but poor UX.**

## 3. chat_sessions FK Asymmetry (Documentation)
`chat_sessions.sectionId` is NOT foreign-keyed to `sections.id` (intentional per v0.3 design: sessions outlive sections). But this asymmetry—courseId *has* an FK, sectionId does *not*—is undocumented in the schema. Future maintainers will puzzle over it or accidentally add an FK, breaking the invariant.

**Status: Design hygiene issue. No code change needed, schema comment only.**

## 4. Dead JSON Column: `quizAttempts.nmemoUpdates` — CONFIRMED DEAD
Grep result: found 4 file matches, all writes-only:
- `schema.ts` line 58: column definition with `DEFAULT '[]'`
- `agents/chat-tutor.ts` lines 155, 316, 327, 336: populated inside structures built for chat messages (not quiz attempts)
- `routes/quiz.ts` line 90: written as `'[]'` but **never read**
- `routes/chat.ts` line 145: written if `result.nmemoUpdates.length > 0` (for *chat* message rows, not quiz attempts)

**Zero reads across the entire learn/ codebase.** Column serves no purpose. Migration will mark it for deprecation (set DEFAULT '[]', stop all writes) in this release; physical drop after a cooldown release.

**Status: Confirmed dead. Safe to deprecate now.**

## 5. No Learn-Side Test Harness (0 tests)
`learn/` package has zero test files. `package.json` has no vitest / test scripts. Platform has comprehensive tests (factories, setup.ts helpers, snapshot support), but every learn route and agent is untested. As graph-aware features (lesson generation, gap analysis, patrol) land, regressions are invisible.

**Status: Critical debt. Blocks safe refactoring and feature expansion.**

## Summary
- 4/5 items confirmed actionable (overlay compaction policy, notes archive route, FK comment, quizAttempts deprecation).
- 1/5 item is foundational (test harness).
- All fit within a single bead for schema hygiene + test bootstrap.
design:
# Design Specification: Learn Schema Hygiene + Test Bootstrap

## 1. Overlay Retention & Compaction

**Policy:** Keep latest 5 versions per (learner, section) + one weekly snapshot.

**Mechanism:**
- Add `isWeeklySnapshot` boolean column to `lesson_overlays` (migration adds column with DEFAULT 0).
- A job runs on-demand via `POST /api/admin/compact-overlays` (or called at boot during orphan-sweep).
- For each (learner, section) pair:
  - Count versions where `isWeeklySnapshot=0`. If > 5, delete oldest such rows until exactly 5 remain (preserving insertion order).
  - For snapshots (isWeeklySnapshot=1), keep newest 4 (roughly one per week over a month).
- SQL (drizzle pseudocode):
  ```typescript
  const toDelete = await db.select({ id: lessonOverlays.id })
    .from(lessonOverlays)
    .where(and(
      eq(lessonOverlays.learnerId, learner),
      eq(lessonOverlays.sectionId, section),
      eq(lessonOverlays.isWeeklySnapshot, 0)
    ))
    .orderBy(asc(lessonOverlays.createdAt))
    .limit(sql`(SELECT COUNT(*) - 5 FROM ${lessonOverlays} WHERE learner_id = ${learner} AND section_id = ${section} AND is_weekly_snapshot = 0)`)
  await db.delete(lessonOverlays).where(inArray(lessonOverlays.id, toDelete.map(r => r.id)))
  ```

**Non-destructive:** Compaction only removes the oldest rows, preserving recent history and snapshots.

---

## 2. Notes Archive

**Schema change:** Add `archivedAt` column to `notes` table (TEXT, nullable).

**Endpoints:**
- `POST /api/notes/:id/archive` — sets `archivedAt` to now, no hard-delete.
- `GET /api/notes?sectionId=…&include_archived=true|false` — default `false`. Filter excludes archived rows unless opt-in.
- Dashboard note-creation surface calls the GET endpoint without `include_archived`, so archived notes are invisible to learners creating new notes.

**Non-destructive:** Archived data stays in the database; if a learner changes their mind, a `POST /api/notes/:id/unarchive` can restore (sets `archivedAt` to NULL).

---

## 3. FK Asymmetry Documentation

**Code:** Add a comment to `lessonOverlays.sectionId` in `schema.ts`:
```typescript
sectionId: text('section_id'),  // NO FK intentional: overlays may outlive sections (v0.3 design invariant)
```

Also document `chat_sessions.sectionId`:
```typescript
sectionId: text('section_id'),  // NO FK intentional: sessions outlive deleted sections per v0.3 lifecycle model
```

**Rationale:** Sections are ephemeral during course redesign; lessons and chat threads are learner assets that survive section edits. This invariant is by design and must not be accidentally "fixed" by adding FKs.

---

## 4. Dead JSON Column: `quizAttempts.nmemoUpdates`

**Grep confirms:** Column is written but never read. (See description.md for evidence.)

**Migration approach (two-phase for safety):**
1. **Phase 1 (this bead):** Add migration that:
   - Creates a new migration file in `learn/src/db/migrations/`.
   - Drizzle approach: Use an ALTER statement to mark the column as deprecated. In practice, since SQLite has limited ALTER support, the migration:
     - Stops all writes to `nmemoUpdates` in code (quiz.ts line 90 → set `nmemoUpdates: null` or omit it).
     - Adds a comment in the route explaining the column is deprecated.
   - **No data loss yet** — column remains in the table for backward compat with any old client code.

2. **Phase 2 (future bead, 2+ releases later):** Drop the column via ALTER TABLE.

**Code changes:**
- `routes/quiz.ts` line 90: change `nmemoUpdates: '[]'` to `nmemoUpdates: null` or remove it entirely (drizzle will use DEFAULT).
- Confirm zero reads via grep (already done).

---

## 5. Test Harness Setup

**Structure:**
```
learn/
├── vitest.config.ts (new)
├── src/
│   ├── test/
│   │   ├── setup.ts (new, mirrors platform/src/test/setup.ts)
│   │   └── fixtures/
│   │       ├── lesson-overlay.test.ts
│   │       ├── chat-tutor.test.ts
│   │       ├── patrol-agent.test.ts
│   │       ├── learning-mcp.test.ts
│   │       └── lesson-generator.test.ts
```

**vitest.config.ts:**
```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'node',
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: ['./src/test/setup.ts'],
    include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'],
  },
});
```

**setup.ts:** (simplified version of platform pattern)
- `testDb`: LibSQL client connection to an ephemeral test database.
- `beforeEach`/`afterEach` hooks to truncate tables.
- Factory helpers: `createTestSection()`, `createTestQuestion()`, `createTestChatSession()`.
- Mock helpers for Nmemo client calls.

**Five representative tests:**

1. **chat-tutor: parseStructuredBlocks happy path + fallback wrapper**
   - Test that tutor correctly parses LessonBlock[] responses.
   - Fallback: if Nmemo returns plain markdown, wrap it as `{ type: 'markdown', content: ... }`.

2. **lesson-overlay: applyEditOp insert_block + version bump**
   - Insert a markdown block into an empty overlay.
   - Assert version increments from 0 → 1 → 2.
   - Verify UNIQUE(learner, section, version) race detection (concurrent write → 409).

3. **patrol-agent: parseReport handles missing trailer**
   - Patrol agent generates a report ending with a trailer line (e.g., "---").
   - Test that parser handles missing trailer gracefully (doesn't crash, extracts metadata).

4. **learning-mcp: write_insight idempotency on duplicate (type, entities)**
   - Write the same insight twice with identical type and entities.
   - Assert second write returns the same `id` (idempotency via `idempotencyKey` hash).

5. **lesson-generator: cold-start (no learner facts) produces canonical output**
   - Generate a lesson for a learner with zero prior facts.
   - Assert output is deterministic and matches a canonical snapshot.
   - Guards against accidental personalisation drift once nmemo-7si lands.

**package.json additions:**
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "vitest",
    "test:watch": "vitest --watch",
    "test:coverage": "vitest --coverage"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@vitest/coverage-v8": "^1.0.0",
    "vitest": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

---

## 6. Migration Mechanics

**Drizzle approach:**
- New file: `learn/src/db/migrations/001_schema-hygiene-v0.2.ts`
- Exports an async `migrate()` function.
- Calls are sequenced in `migrate.ts`:
  ```typescript
  const migrations = [
    { name: '001_schema-hygiene-v0.2', fn: import('./migrations/001_schema-hygiene-v0.2.ts') }
  ];
  for (const m of migrations) {
    await m.fn.migrate();
    console.log(`Migration ${m.name} applied.`);
  }
  ```

**Migration contents:**
```typescript
export async function migrate() {
  const client = createClient({ url: `file:${config.DB_PATH}` });
  
  // Add isWeeklySnapshot to lesson_overlays
  await client.execute(`
    ALTER TABLE lesson_overlays ADD COLUMN is_weekly_snapshot INTEGER DEFAULT 0
  `).catch(err => {
    if (err.message.includes('duplicate column')) {
      console.log('Column already exists, skipping.');
    } else throw err;
  });

  // Add archivedAt to notes
  await client.execute(`
    ALTER TABLE notes ADD COLUMN archived_at TEXT
  `).catch(err => {
    if (err.message.includes('duplicate column')) {
      console.log('Column already exists, skipping.');
    } else throw err;
  });

  console.log('Schema hygiene migration complete.');
  await client.close();
}
```

---

## 7. CI Integration

**Out of scope for v1.** Flag as follow-up bead: "Learn platform CI: run tests on PR, enforce coverage floor."

# Acceptance Criteria

- **Overlay compaction:** After running the compaction job (via `POST /api/admin/compact-overlays`), verify no (learner, section) pair has more than 5 non-snapshot versions + 4 weekly snapshots. Query: `SELECT learner_id, section_id, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM lesson_overlays WHERE is_weekly_snapshot = 0 GROUP BY learner_id, section_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5` returns zero rows.

- **Overlay retention:** Compaction preserves newest 5 versions and all snapshots. Oldest versions are deleted first (oldest ID removed, newest ID preserved). Verify by comparing row IDs before/after compaction.

- **Notes archive endpoint:** `POST /api/notes/:id/archive` sets `archivedAt` to ISO timestamp and returns 200. Archiving a note not found returns 404. Archiving twice is idempotent (second call returns 200 with the same `archivedAt`).

- **Notes visibility after archive:** `GET /api/notes?sectionId=X` (default `include_archived=false`) returns zero archived notes. Same query with `include_archived=true` includes all archived rows.

- **Notes unarchive endpoint:** `POST /api/notes/:id/unarchive` sets `archivedAt` to NULL and returns 200. Unarchived note reappears in default GET query.

- **FK asymmetry documented:** `schema.ts` lines for `lessonOverlays.sectionId` and `chat_sessions.sectionId` include inline comments explaining why FK is intentionally absent (overlays/sessions outlive sections).

- **Dead column writes stopped:** `routes/quiz.ts` line 90 no longer writes `nmemoUpdates` field (or writes `null`). Grep for `nmemoUpdates` in `learn/src/routes/quiz.ts` returns zero matches on write operations (schema definition and comments only).

- **Dead column reads confirmed zero:** Grep across entire `learn/` codebase for pattern `quizAttempts\.nmemoUpdates|\.nmemoUpdates\s*\)` returns zero matches (no destructuring or direct reads). All four grep-found files are schema definitions or chat-message writes, not quiz-attempt reads.

- **Test harness installed:** `learn/` directory contains `vitest.config.ts` and `src/test/setup.ts`. `package.json` has test scripts: `pnpm test` runs vitest and exits 0. `pnpm test:watch` starts watch mode.

- **Five tests passing:** `pnpm test` in `learn/` exits 0 with at least 5 tests passing:
  - `chat-tutor: parseStructuredBlocks happy path`
  - `lesson-overlay: applyEditOp insert_block version bump`
  - `patrol-agent: parseReport handles missing trailer`
  - `learning-mcp: write_insight idempotency`
  - `lesson-generator: cold-start canonical output`

- **Migrations applied without error:** Running `pnpm db:migrate` in `learn/` executes `001_schema-hygiene-v0.2.ts` and logs success. Rerunning is idempotent (duplicate-column errors are caught and skipped).

- **Schema introspection:** `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='lesson_overlays'` shows `is_weekly_snapshot INTEGER DEFAULT 0` column. Same for `notes` showing `archived_at TEXT`.

- **No schema FKs added:** Verify `chat_sessions.section_id` still has no FOREIGN KEY constraint. Query: `PRAGMA foreign_key_list(chat_sessions);` shows no constraint on `section_id`.
notes:
# Implementation Notes & Risk Analysis

## Risks

1. **Overlay compaction causes learner-valued history loss.** A learner may have edited a lesson dozens of times and values the fine-grained revert capability. Compacting to 5 versions erases that history. *Mitigation:* The policy is conservative (5 versions is generous for normal editing); learners can manually snapshot before major changes; future UI can offer "save as snapshot" before compaction runs.

2. **Archived notes *feel* deleted.** Once a note is archived, it disappears from the default note list, which may confuse learners who expect soft-delete to be reversible via UI. *Mitigation:* Document archive semantics clearly in dashboards; offer an "archived notes" section accessible from a tab or filter; ensure unarchive endpoint is discoverable.

3. **Tests freeze incorrect behaviour as canon.** The five representative tests guard against regressions, but if the current implementation has subtle bugs (e.g., lesson-generator personalisation is not deterministic), the snapshot test will canonicalize the bug. *Mitigation:* Review each test's subject (e.g., lesson-generator cold-start) before shipping to ensure it's correct; use visual review + manual QA before snapshot acceptance.

---

## Open Questions

1. **Should overlay compaction be opt-in per learner?** The design assumes a global 5-version policy, but some learners might want fewer or more. Alternative: Add a learner preference (e.g., `maxOverlayVersions` in user prefs) and check it during compaction. *Decision: Start with global policy; add learner prefs as a follow-up if usage data shows demand.*

2. **What's the right weekly-snapshot retention (4 weeks? 12)?** The design suggests keeping 4 snapshots (roughly 1 per week over a month). Is a month enough, or should we keep 12 weeks? *Decision: Start with 4 weeks; monitor storage and adjust post-launch.*

3. **Should archived notes be hard-deletable on a separate user action?** After archiving, should there be a "permanently delete" option after 30 days? Or should archive be the end of the lifecycle? *Decision: Archive is final for v1; permanent deletion is a future bead if GDPR/compliance requires it.*

4. **When should the compaction job run?** On-demand endpoint is safe but requires manual trigger. Should it run automatically on boot, once per day, or on every overlay edit? *Decision: On-demand endpoint + optional daily cron (flagged as follow-up CI bead).*

---

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Leave overlays unbounded, add UI to manually clean.** Puts the burden on learners to manage their own storage. Not acceptable for a launched product.

2. **Archive all promoted notes immediately.** Skip the soft-delete and archive promoted notes automatically. Risk: learners lose the note from search/recall before they realize it's promoted. Current approach (explicit archive action) is safer.

3. **Skip the test harness now, add it in other beads.** Tests are split across separate PRs and not co-located with implementation. Risk: tests lag implementation; regressions slip through. Current approach (bootstrapping a shared harness) is better.

title: Session report passing — previous agent report as context for next session
description:
## Context

Each extraction agent session produces a structured PHASE 6 REPORT with:
- Entities found, pronouns resolved, facts created/skipped
- Difficulties and observations  
- Aliases created (including unconfirmed)

Currently this report is logged but not passed to the next agent session. The next session starts fresh with only graph state (facts, summaries, aliases) — it doesn't know what the previous session struggled with or concluded.

## Proposal

Pass the previous session's report (or a condensed version) as additional context to the next agent session. This gives the agent continuity:
- "Previous session noted: the stranger may transition to first-person narrator"
- "Previous session could not resolve: 'my father' — no proper noun available"
- "Previous session created unconfirmed alias: stranger → Victor Frankenstein"

## Considerations

- This is injected context, which we want to minimise. But it's temporary — once the graph carries the information properly (via summaries, aliases, facts), the report context becomes redundant.
- Could store reports in a table keyed by memory_id, or just pass the last N reports as a sliding window.
- Should be optional/configurable — the agent should work without it, this just accelerates convergence.
- May not be needed if aliases + summaries carry enough information.

## Status: Research — evaluate after aliases + summaries are tested
notes:
Implementation landed in commits 604c9ec + b6800b5.

WIRE PATH:
- pipeline.ts extract() fetches latest prior extraction_reports row (excluding current memory_id) via ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
- passes previousReport into invokeGraphAgent({sourceText, memoryId, previousReport})
- invokeGraphAgent serialises as previous_report on POST /graph-agent body (null when omitted)
- ml-services graph_agent.py renders prior report as delimited <extraction_report> block in user prompt using delimit_for_prompt(kind='report') for T8 prompt-safety
- agent reads it during ORIENT for continuity context

DECISIONS:
- Reused existing extraction_reports table (no new migration) — matches bead's preferred minimum-change path
- Single most-recent prior report (not sliding window of N) — minimal context overhead; can grow if proven valuable
- WHERE memory_id <> current_memory_id defends against re-extract feeding the agent its own prior report
- Fetch is best-effort: DB error logs but never blocks extraction (matches the fire-and-forget INSERT shape already in extract())
- First-chunk path: previousReport=null → handler skips the continuity block entirely (clean prompt for fresh starts)
- PROMPT_SAFETY_SYSTEM_CLAUSE already covers <extraction_report> as data-not-instructions, so no system-prompt change needed

TEST COVERAGE:
- TS: 6 tests in src/test/harness/graph-agent-prior-report.test.ts — wire shape (param→body), exclusion of current memory_id, ordering by created_at DESC, null-safe empty case
- Python: 5 tests in ml-services/tests/test_graph_agent_prompt.py — omitted when None/empty, rendered as delimited block, injection-marker sanitisation, block ordering between source-text and instructions

- python tests/test_graph_agent_prompt.py → 5/5 pass
- npx vitest src/test/services/causal-agent-timeout.test.ts src/test/harness/reconciliation-auto-trigger.test.ts → 11/11 pass (regression on touched code paths)
- Pydantic model accepts new field; smoke import OK

d3 force strength values from a bead spec are STARTING POINTS, not contracts — verify against the real graph and bump if visibly weak. Injecting synthetic/pseudo-links into a d3.forceLink at runtime (e.g. a toggleable affinity force) has two non-obvious traps. (1) d3 MUTATES link.source/link.target in place — rewriting string ids to node-object references — every time .links() runs. So a CACHED list of synthetic links must be deep-enough-cloned (spread is enough for flat link objects) before each merge, else the cache's string ids get replaced with objects and the next merge's id-based filter silently breaks. (2) d3.forceLink THROWS 'missing: <id>' if any link references an id not in simulation.nodes() — so filter synthetic links to the live node-id set before .links(). Idempotent merge pattern that works across toggle/render: linkForce.links(current.filter(l=>l._edgeType!=='X').concat(cloned-filtered synthetics)). Keep synthetics OUT of state.data.edges so the render/draw path (which filters by _edgeType per group) never draws them — no render.js change needed. Pattern from bead nmemo-pd5.6 (predicate affinity force).

When a d3 force accessor needs per-flag overrides (e.g. link distance varies with a feature toggle), extract the canonical accessor as a named export and compose overrides via ternary: `.distance(d => (flag && cond) ? value : defaultAccessor(d))`. Avoids the 'restate the whole table per override' anti-pattern d3's force-replaces-wholesale API tempts. Pattern from bead nmemo-hyh extracting forces.js's pd5.2 duplication.

Any d3-force that pins nodes by setting fx/fy needs a SYMMETRIC release path for EVERY way a node leaves the managed set — not just the obvious toggle-OFF. The non-obvious one: a node that was managed (pinned) but whose membership key disappears mid-life (e.g. a causal event whose anchor entity is filtered out / merged / deleted) gets silently dropped from the force's group map, but its last fx/fy stays set, so d3 freezes it at a stale position forever. Fix: in the force's initialize (which re-runs on every simulation.nodes() reset / fetchData), when a candidate node fails the membership test, clear its fx=fy=null in the else-branch — mirror the articulation force's 'clear fx/fy for non-managed entities' sweep. Caught by /code-review on bead nmemo-pd5.7 (causalRadial); the OFF-path clear existed but the anchor-disappeared-while-ON path was missing. Rule: wherever you write node.fx=..., grep for the matching node.fx=null and make sure it covers all exit transitions.

Hard-pin geometry choice matters: pin-at-current-position is stable but visually arbitrary; pin-on-a-deliberate-ring (id-sorted, viewport-proportional radius) makes the structural backbone visible and reproducible. Bumped applied alpha to 1.0 on toggle for snappier re-settle. Pattern from bead nmemo-ywe — soft pin (pd5.4) → hard pin at current pos (smr) → hard pin on ring (ywe) is a 3-step evolution worth keeping in mind for future force-layout work: don't ship at 'stable but ugly' if there's a 'stable AND structured' option a few lines away.

JS FP gotcha for strict-less-than threshold tests: 0.5 - 0.4 = 0.09999999...; 0.3 - 0.2 = 0.09999999... etc. To test exactly-at-boundary, never use values that produce a decimal via subtraction (0.1, 0.3, 0.6). Use exact-FP values (0.5, 0.25, 0.75) or offset to either side (0.099, 0.101).

When a hand-maintained allowlist (Set/list) drives a policy decision (route X vs Y) over entities in a static list AND the allowlist is in a different file from the entity declarations, the allowlist will drift the moment the list grows. Fix: push the property onto each entity declaration (required typed field), derive the set at module-load via filter+map, optionally add a startup assertion catching cast-bypass slips. nmemo-2yv.113.

When a scaffolding test surfaces a pre-existing bug out of scope for the current bead, pin BOTH expected behaviour via it.skip ('PRE-EXISTING BUG: ...; unskip after fix') AND current behaviour via rejects.toThrow regression guard. First flips green when fix lands; second flips red. Better than a TODO comment because machine-checked. Pattern from bead nmemo-2yv.68.

Checkboxes built via createElement need autocomplete='off' + matching setAttribute('checked', '') alongside the .checked property, else browsers' form-state restoration silently overrides the script-set property after navigation — DOM visibly drifts from app state even when localStorage and the model agree. Caught by /verify on bead nmemo-pd5.1; would have shipped as a confusing UX bug.

nomic-embed-text 500s above ~2048 tokens (~10-13K chars). To reproduce a 'whole-window baseline' embedding number, chunk at the platform's max_ingest_chars (6000), NOT the raw document - that both avoids the 500 and matches the chunk size the baseline was actually measured at. Confirmed in yxj.1: 6000-char baseline degree score 0.471 reproduced the prior ~0.47 Frankenstein probe exactly.
Postgres ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS inserted distinguishes fresh-insert (true) from existing-row-updated (false) in one round trip; canonical idiom for upsert detection.

Postgres COUNT() returns bigint, which postgres.js delivers as string ('2', not 2). Use ::integer cast in SELECT (or Number() in JS) when tests assert .toBe(number). Affects every COUNT-derived numeric field on a row.

Postgres NOW() inside a transaction returns the transaction-start timestamp, NOT the statement-start. Two audit rows emitted in the same tx have IDENTICAL occurred_at. Tests asserting order by occurred_at DESC must use set-membership (rows.some(r => r.X includes Y)) not positional access (rows[0]/rows[1]). Use clock_timestamp() if statement-level ordering matters. nmemo-2yv.30

UPDATE...RETURNING is the only audit-set-integrity-preserving shape for 'mutate a set of rows and emit one audit row per row'. SELECT-then-UPDATE under READ COMMITTED isolation has a race window where concurrent inserts get UPDATEd without an audit row. Default to UPDATE...RETURNING / DELETE...RETURNING whenever an acceptance bullet says 'every affected row gets exactly one history row'. nmemo-2yv.30

When adding a dirty-check that skips an expensive recompute on unchanged input, make the skip path return the SAME cached object reference (and the recompute path a fresh one). Reference equality across two unchanged-input calls is then a clean, production-code-free /verify signal for 'skip fired' — no need to add a debug counter or log just for testing. Correctness falls out for free: a skip returns the literally-last-computed value, so it can never diverge from a fresh recompute of the same data. Key the fingerprint on the EXACT inputs that determine the output (e.g. for predicate-affinity Jaccard: the fact-edge (source,predicate) pairs only), computed in a linear pass cheaper than the guarded work. Bias the hash toward false-dirty (harmless recompute) over false-clean (stale result): natural-order string hash + count is fine when the data source returns stable order. Pattern from bead nmemo-pd5.9.

Rebuilding a search_path-polluted Apache AGE Postgres DB (app tables leaked into ag_catalog because old migrations lacked public. qualifiers): drop+recreate the whole database, re-run docker/postgres/init-age.sql FIRST (it owns 'ALTER DATABASE ... SET search_path = ag_catalog,public,$user' — the DB-level default for every connection; migration 001 only sets it session-level), THEN npm run db:migrate. create_graph is guarded by an ag_graph existence check so init->migrate is idempotent. Selective ag_catalog table cleanup is insufficient — leaked functions/sequences also shadow public. Diagnose with SELECT schemaname,tablename FROM pg_tables across ALL schemas. From nmemo-3f9.1.

When composing a per-node d3-force accessor that gates on a state map keyed by entity id (e.g. state.topology.entities[d.id]), include an explicit _nodeType guard. Multiple node namespaces (entity / sourceMemory / causalEvent) coexist in the same simulation and can share ids if any upstream join is sloppy — without the type guard, the accessor will silently mis-target the wrong node class. Probe-confirmed on bead nmemo-pd5.4: articulation entity id with _nodeType:'sourceMemory' correctly returned -30, not -2000.
